Humanae Vitae (1968) reaffirmed Catholic opposition to artificial contraception and predicted societal harms including infidelity and government coercion.
The principle of double effect is introduced as a tool for evaluating actions with both good and bad consequences.
Discernment and planning one's family is good, but methods must align with Christian principles and not be driven by selfishness or convenience.
The speaker acknowledges personal biases and the need for respectful dialogue on controversial topics.
The lecture connects contraception ethics to broader issues like gender transition and end-of-life care, emphasizing covenantal medicine.
The Ethical and Religious Directives guide Catholic healthcare; Baptist hospitals lack an equivalent universal statement.
Freud and Gandhi both argued against artificial contraception on moral and natural-law grounds.

episodes.title: Thyroid Disorders - Dr. Amanda Lucashu, DO
episodes.speaker: Unknown
episodes.abstract: Dr. Amanda Lucashu introduces herself as new faculty and reviews thyroid disorders. She presents a case of a 38-year-old female with fatigue and constipation, leading to a diagnosis of primary hypothyroidism (TSH 22.3, low free T4). Management includes starting levothyroxine 25-50 mcg, titrating to a goal TSH in the upper normal range, and monitoring every 4-6 weeks after dose changes. Pregnancy requires a 30-50% dose increase with monthly TSH checks, and asymptomatic screening is debated (ATA recommends every 5 years starting at 35; USPSTF recommends against).
key_points: Hypothyroidism presents with fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation, and increased menstrual flow; delayed deep tendon reflex relaxation is a classic exam finding.
Initial labs for suspected hypothyroidism should include TSH and free T4; antibody testing (e.g., anti-TPO) is not routinely needed for primary hypothyroidism.
Levothyroxine starting dose is 25-50 mcg daily, with lower doses for elderly patients; titrate based on TSH every 4-6 weeks.
Levothyroxine should be taken on an empty stomach in the morning, consistently, and separated from medications like omeprazole, calcium, and iron that impair absorption.
Goal TSH in non-pregnant adults is the upper half of the normal range (e.g., 0.5-4.0 mIU/L) to avoid overcorrection, which can cause angina, atrial fibrillation, and osteoporosis.
T3 (liothyronine) is not recommended over T4 monotherapy due to rapid absorption and short half-life leading to inconsistent levels.
Once stable on levothyroxine, TSH should be rechecked every 6-12 months; dose adjustments require recheck in 4-6 weeks.

In pregnancy, levothyroxine dose must be increased by 30-50% immediately upon confirmation; TSH should be checked monthly and kept in trimester-specific lower normal range to prevent congenital hypothyroidism.
Drugs that can elevate TSH include metoclopramide, lithium, amiodarone, and antipsychotics; these should be considered in patients requiring unexpectedly high levothyroxine doses.

Asymptomatic screening for thyroid disease is recommended by the American Thyroid Association (every 5 years starting at age 35) but not by the USPSTF; a low threshold for TSH testing in symptomatic patients is appropriate.
Subclinical hypothyroidism usually requires no treatment; exceptions include symptoms, TSH >10, family history, pregnancy plans, or positive antibodies.
TSH is the first-line screening test for thyroid dysfunction; if abnormal, add free T4 and T3.

episodes.title: Trauma Informed Care
episodes.speaker: Unknown
episodes.abstract: Sarah Gad, human trafficking program manager, explains why healthcare workers are uniquely positioned to identify victims of human trafficking. She defines trafficking broadly to include familial exploitation, coercion for labor or sex, and control through documents or substances. The talk outlines red flags such as delay in seeking care, inconsistent stories, multiple phones, branding tattoos, and third-party document control. She emphasizes trauma-informed responses, including quick removal from waiting rooms to prevent trafficker interference, and describes the hospital's advocate program for long-term support.
key_points: Healthcare workers are often the only professionals who encounter victims alone, making the hospital a critical identification site.
Human trafficking includes not only cross-border smuggling but also familial exploitation, such as parents trading children for rent or drugs.
Red flags include delay in seeking medical care, inconsistent stories, fear/anxiety in waiting rooms, and agitation about staying.
Branding tattoos (e.g., trafficker's name, barcodes) are common; victims are reluctant to discuss them.
Third-party control of documents (passports, birth certificates) can be used to control victims, even for minors.
Multiple cell phones, with one always connected to a trafficker, indicate surveillance.
Victims often have extensive psychiatric and substance abuse histories.
Minors exploited for commercial sex are automatically considered trafficking victims regardless of coercion.
Quick removal from waiting rooms is crucial to prevent traffickers from finding victims.
The hospital's advocate program helps victims with long-term needs like housing, job placement, and legal assistance.
Most human trafficking victims in Oklahoma are local, born and raised in the state, not transient.
Red flags include inappropriate belongings for weather, inability to leave, and working extremely long hours for little money.

episodes.title: Tuberculosis - Kyle Jones, DO
episodes.speaker: Unknown
episodes.abstract: This lecture presents a real-world case of pulmonary tuberculosis that was initially misdiagnosed as malignancy due to a cavitary lung lesion on CT. The case highlights diagnostic delays caused by false-negative TB skin test and sputum culture, and the importance of using QuantiFERON blood testing, especially in symptomatic patients with risk factors. The speaker reviews risk factors for TB (cough >2 weeks, weight loss, fever, origin from high-prevalence countries), classic upper-lobe cavitary findings, and the RIPE (rifampin, isoniazid, ethambutol, pyrazinamide) regimen with directly observed therapy. Key lessons include the need for close communication with public health departments, vigilance for TB in refugees and immigrants, and the pitfalls of relying on skin testing alone.
key_points: Cough lasting more than 2–4 weeks, especially with weight loss, fever, and night sweats, should raise suspicion for TB.
TB most commonly affects the upper lobes of the lungs due to higher oxygen content.
The QuantiFERON gold blood test is more reliable than the PPD skin test in certain populations, including those with prior BCG vaccination or immunocompromise.
Sputum culture and GeneXpert PCR are the mainstays of active TB diagnosis; PCR is more sensitive than AFB smear.
Initial TB treatment is a four-drug regimen (rifampin, isoniazid, ethambutol, pyrazinamide) for 2 months, followed by rifampin and isoniazid for 4–7 months.
Directly observed therapy (DOT) is recommended to ensure adherence and reduce transmission.
Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, requiring baseline and monthly visual acuity monitoring.
Latent TB infection is treated with a single drug (e.g., 9 months of isoniazid) to prevent progression to active disease.
Missed or delayed diagnosis can occur when TB is mistaken for malignancy, COVID-19, or community-acquired pneumonia.
Public health departments play a critical role in contact tracing, sputum collection, and patient follow-up.
TB is transmitted only from individuals with active pulmonary disease.
Latent TB infection occurs when macrophages and T cells successfully contain the bacteria in granulomas.

episodes.title: Two Cases with Dr. Lawrence Lee
episodes.speaker: Unknown
episodes.abstract: This lecture uses a case-based approach to teach systematic evaluation of abdominal pain. The presenter emphasizes patient-centered history-taking, including not interrupting and using OPQRST. The case of a 42-year-old with epigastric pain and vomiting leads to a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis, with discussion of differential diagnoses and appropriate workup. Key teaching points include considering life-threatening causes like AAA and mesenteric ischemia, and the importance of not missing gallstone pancreatitis. The lecture also highlights the challenge of a poor historian and the role of supportive care in pancreatitis management.
key_points: Do not interrupt patients; let them speak for up to five minutes before redirecting with direct questions.
Use OPQRST to systematically characterize pain after the patient's initial story.
Consider a broad differential for abdominal pain including AAA, mesenteric ischemia, and malignancy, especially with chronic symptoms.
For acute pancreatitis, check lipase, CMP, and obtain a right upper quadrant ultrasound to evaluate for gallstones.
Causes of pancreatitis include gallstones, alcohol, medications, hypertriglyceridemia, autoimmune disease, malignancy, infection, and trauma.
A poor historian may require observation and time to clarify the diagnosis; avoid premature closure.
Supportive care (IV fluids, analgesics, antiemetics) is the mainstay of acute pancreatitis management.
NSAID use and alcohol are common contributors to gastritis and peptic ulcer disease; always ask about them.
EGD is indicated for suspected gastric ulcer or gastritis, especially with chronic symptoms and NSAID use.
Always ask about trauma, even if not volunteered, as it can be a cause of pancreatitis.
Antibiotics in acute pancreatitis are indicated only for necrotizing pancreatitis involving >30% of the pancreas or for a pancreatic abscess; otherwise, they are not beneficial and carry risks.
MRCP is indicated specifically to rule in or rule out choledocholithiasis, prompted by a dilated common bile duct and/or elevated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase.

pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Cardiovascular Risk& Reduction

pearls.text: For hypertriglyceridemia with ASCVD risk >2%, Vascepa (icosapent ethyl) is first-line; if unaffordable, use omega-3 fatty acids.
pearls.verbatim: So Vascepa has got the best evidence for patients that have both hypertriglyceridemia and elevated risk. So if their ACVD score is less than two percent Vascepa, and if they can't afford Vascepa, then omega three fatty acids.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Cardiovascular Risk& Reduction

pearls.text: USPSTF recommends aspirin for primary prevention only in adults aged 40-60 with ASCVD risk >10% and low bleeding risk; no aspirin for primary prevention after age 60.
pearls.verbatim: USPSTF says age 40 60, greater than ten percent risk, low risk of bleeding. But it should be individualized because the potential benefit is small. So they say no one 60 for primary prevention.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Cardiovascular Risk& Reduction

pearls.text: For patients who refuse insulin due to fear of hypoglycemia, consider switching to a long-acting insulin alone or a sulfonylurea to achieve at least some glycemic improvement.
pearls.verbatim: What if I only use the long acting insulin? Because, say, they're averaging 200. So that's better than averaging 500.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Care for the un-homed with Dr. Carroll

pearls.text: The Tulsa Healthcare Coverage Project partners with OU to screen homeless individuals for Medicaid eligibility.
pearls.verbatim: we have people from the Tulsa Healthcare Coverage Project. They partner with OU, but they go around town to one of our clients and screen people too to see who qualifies for Medicaid.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Care for the un-homed with Dr. Carroll

pearls.text: Maintain Medicaid credentialing to write prescriptions for unhoused patients and ensure payment.
pearls.verbatim: I'm still Medicaid credentialed. So a lot of these people, I can still I can still write scripts and get it paid for for them.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Care for the un-homed with Dr. Carroll

pearls.text: Basal cell carcinoma can metastasize; do not rely on the adage that it never does.
pearls.verbatim: Basal cell carcinoma never metastasizes? Oh, it never, never, never metastasizes. It does. I've seen at least four.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Care for the un-homed with Dr. Carroll

pearls.text: Refer diabetic patients with A1C over 8 to programs that provide fresh produce and cooking classes.
pearls.verbatim: Crossover clinic in North Tulsa has a a program where any of my diabetics on the North Side that have an A1C over eight, they'll sign them up for fresh produce and cooking classes.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Care for the un-homed with Dr. Carroll

pearls.text: Do not allow patients with chronic pain to occupy day beds meant for those with acute illness like pneumonia.
pearls.verbatim: we just don't do that because need to be up, and we need to leave those spots available for people with, like, pneumonia.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Care for the un-homed with Dr. Carroll

pearls.text: ICS inhalers increase pneumonia risk; do not jump to triple therapy (Trelegy) without considering this risk, and de-escalate ICS if patient is stable.
pearls.verbatim: They increase the risk of pneumonia. So that's why we don't just jump to Trelegy every time because people can get pneumonia more frequently.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: Never use ICS monotherapy (e.g., Flovent) for COPD; always combine with a LABA.
pearls.verbatim: don't ever put somebody on COPD with, like, Flovent or something. It's just ICS because it's just... Don't do that. Never ever do it.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: Screen all COPD patients for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency at least once, as recommended by WHO.
pearls.verbatim: WHO recommends screening all people with COPD at least once.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: Prescribe long-term oxygen therapy for COPD patients with resting SpO2 <88% or PaO2 <55 mmHg; target SpO2 ≥90%.
pearls.verbatim: Oxygen therapy. So it does prevent mortality in people that are severely hypoxic. So that's people that are less than eighty eight percent on remeron. Right? For those, if you happen to get an ABG, it's less than fifty five. Those are the kind of people that it's gonna prevent mortality. So mortality, whatever. And then you want the oxygen to be greater than or equal to 90.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: Consider Daliresp for patients on Trelegy with exacerbations only if they have severe COPD (by spirometry), chronic bronchitis, and at least one exacerbation in the past year.
pearls.verbatim: if somebody's on Trelegy already and they're having exacerbations or having too many exacerbations, you can consider Daliresp, PDE4 inhibitor. The criteria to be on it, though, is they have to have had at least one exacerbation in the last year, which I imagine the reason that you'd wanna start it. Right? Start it on people that are stable. But if people are still having exacerbations, you have to make sure they have severe COPD. So you really need spirometry to get this one going and have to have chronic bronchitis.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: For exacerbations despite triple therapy in patients who are not currently smoking, consider adding azithromycin.
pearls.verbatim: you can add azithromycin to that in people that are former smokers. Really, I'd probably leave that up to palm. That's probably my scope. That's probably not gonna change my practice any, but it's something that you can do. And if people don't have chronic bronchitis but they're getting exacerbations on Trelegy, you can just do azithromycin for people that aren't smoking currently.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: Use the COPD Pocket Consult Guide app to show patients inhaler technique videos for any device.
pearls.verbatim: The COPD pocket consult guide is an app on your phone. I got it. I used it for this lecture. And what it has on it is cool videos. So if you if you have a patient and you're starting them on a rizomat and wanna show them how to use it instead of talking to the pharmacist, there's this inhale... There's the inhaler education. It's got all the videos for every kind of inhaler on it, like quick videos.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: For a patient with group B COPD (symptomatic but zero or one exacerbation) who cannot use their current LAMA device, switch to a different device like the Ellipta rather than abandoning the drug class.
pearls.verbatim: So what's another LAMA that you could suggest? I need, like, brand name and device type. Okay. Yes. Good job. You could try a different device like the Ellipta
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COPD - Dr. Matt Haney

pearls.text: Order anti-spike antibody tests to assess vaccine response; nucleocapsid antibodies are only made after infection and are often low and short-lived, so they can falsely suggest no prior infection.
pearls.verbatim: the test you need to order is order the anti spike. Don't order this. I'll tell you why in a minute unless unless you got... You're gonna use it in a very clever way.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COVID Update, Vaccines, Antibody Tests - Dr. Gerald Miller, PhD

pearls.text: Nucleocapsid antibody is only present in about 36% of patients after six months, so a negative result does not rule out prior infection.
pearls.verbatim: it's only gonna be around for thirty six per... Thirty six percent of the patients after six months.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COVID Update, Vaccines, Antibody Tests - Dr. Gerald Miller, PhD

pearls.text: After infection, wait at least 30 days before administering the first vaccine dose.
pearls.verbatim: you wait thirty days, at least thirty days to vaccinate.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COVID Update, Vaccines, Antibody Tests - Dr. Gerald Miller, PhD

pearls.text: For patients with prior infection and vaccination, wait six months before checking a spike antibody titer to guide further management.
pearls.verbatim: wait about six months, and you go back in, and you do a titer.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: COVID Update, Vaccines, Antibody Tests - Dr. Gerald Miller, PhD

pearls.text: Use the POUND mnemonic to quickly screen for migraine in a patient with headache: Pulsatile quality, One-day duration, Unilateral, Nausea/vomiting, Disabling intensity.
pearls.verbatim: p, pulsatile quality. O, one day in duration or it's a long time, u, unilateral, thin, nausea or vomiting, and d, disabling intensity.
pearls.speaker: Cyr
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cyr on Headaches 6/25/26

pearls.text: Ask about activity tolerance: 'If I told you to run around the clinic, would you feel the same, better, or worse?' Migraine worsens with routine physical activity.
pearls.verbatim: if I told you to go run around this clinic, would you feel the same, better, or worse? And it's like, when I have a migraine, you... Like, mm-mm.
pearls.speaker: Cyr
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cyr on Headaches 6/25/26

pearls.text: Common migraine triggers include stress, lack of sleep, missed meals, weather changes, neck pain, bright sun, dehydration, caffeine (too much or too little), processed foods, and hormone changes like menses.
pearls.verbatim: Stress, lack of sleep. I woke up two hours late. Is that changing how I'm living my life? Yes. Interrupted sleep... Depressed mood. Anxiety. Skip a meal. Very variable weather. Storm... Humidity above 80% also... Neck pain, alcohol, bright, sun, or dehydration... Caffeine, so, like, too little or too much.
pearls.speaker: Cyr
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cyr on Headaches 6/25/26

pearls.text: Limit triptan use to avoid rebound headaches — the speaker's personal experience of 20 triptans per month was identified as excessive and contributed to medication overuse headache.
pearls.verbatim: I was probably taking twenty triptans a month. That's bad... and you're having rebound headaches.
pearls.speaker: Cyr
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cyr on Headaches 6/25/26

pearls.text: Give a triptan a fair chance—try it at least six times before concluding it doesn't work, and ensure the patient takes it at the beginning of the headache.
pearls.verbatim: give it a fair chance and make sure, like, someone's taking it at the beginning of their headache.
pearls.speaker: Cyr
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cyr on Headaches 6/25/26

pearls.text: Set a goal to reduce acute medication use gradually, e.g., from 12 to 6 triptans per month.
pearls.verbatim: set a goal... maybe if your goal is 12 and eventually your goal is, like, six a month.
pearls.speaker: Cyr
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cyr on Headaches 6/25/26

pearls.text: Patients in early recovery have never learned to manage even a headache, so they may present with exaggerated complaints. Teach basic self-soothing and symptom management.
pearls.verbatim: They've never learned how to manage even a headache.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: Suboxone is allowed in the program for patients who started it in jail, but they must be transparent about its use. It is not a first-line option for all.
pearls.verbatim: we do allow some for suboxone in some cases. They just have to know when they're doing this. And those came to us. They get on suboxone in jail.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: Monthly court reports are a common trigger for anxiety that manifests as headaches or stomach issues. Ask about upcoming court dates when evaluating somatic complaints.
pearls.verbatim: they have a court report monthly. And so if they're having anxiety around that, a lot of the times that can manifest in headaches, stomach issues, things like that.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: Patients may request unrelated medical record reviews or other 'side quests' to avoid uncomfortable programming. Recognize this as a potential avoidance behavior.
pearls.verbatim: they'll pop out a GED and come to me and be like, you know, I... Can you look up my medical records from 2004? Like, I think there might have been... It's, like, some random stuff like that. And then you get a message like, where is so and so? Like, they're on a little side quest over here because they don't wanna be wherever they were.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: In early recovery, ADHD-like symptoms are often due to dopamine depletion from abstinence, not true ADHD. Avoid misdiagnosing and prescribing stimulants.
pearls.verbatim: I think I have ADHD, but I think it's more that your brain is dopamine depressed right now because you're not getting the drugs that your brain wants to.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: Zofran will cause a false positive on urine drug screens, so avoid it in this population.
pearls.verbatim: Zofran will affect their UAs, which is a bummer because it's a good medicine.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: The program uses a random color-coded urine drug screen system six days a week to monitor compliance.
pearls.verbatim: the women are on a color system, and it's a random UA color line that they call every morning.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: A diluted urine sample from apple cider vinegar is treated as a positive test for drug use.
pearls.verbatim: if they show to be diluted on their UA, we have no choice but to assume that that is an attempt to mislead us, and it counts as a positive.
pearls.speaker: Dianne Hughes
pearls.episode_title: Dianne Hughes on WIR

pearls.text: A patient can meet DSM criteria for depression or anxiety yet be functioning fine and not bothered by it; in such cases, the physician must consider whether intervention is needed and respect the patient's insight.
pearls.verbatim: But you do have people come in for... Who can be diagnosably depressed or diagnosably anxious or something like that based on the meeting with the number of criteria, but they could be functioning in a way that's quite fine that they're not having a problem with it. Then what do you do?
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Discernment & Perspective

pearls.text: When a patient presents with cough and green sputum, consider not only bacterial pneumonia but also environmental factors like air quality from nearby industrial mills.
pearls.verbatim: For many years, I lived in Northwest Indiana, and everybody in Northwest Indiana had had... Not everybody, but a lot of people, there's a large instance of respiratory problems there. Why? Because all the mills, all the the jillions, there's a bunch of mills up there, and the wind comes sweeping down to that part of Indiana. It just kinda... And so it just kinda locks in this bad air quality.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Discernment & Perspective

pearls.text: When discerning consolation vs. desolation, look beyond emotions: evaluate growth in faith, hope, and love, and engagement with God—not just the presence of pleasant or unpleasant feelings.
pearls.verbatim: What's important to understand is that emotions are not the only indicators of consolation and desolation.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Discernment & Perspective

pearls.text: Community coming together during suffering can dramatically reduce requests for pain and sleep medication, as observed by Paul Brand during wartime.
pearls.verbatim: He realized patients that were in the hospital but could help other patients to help the patients that were, like, really, really sick. And he said that the request for pain medication and sleep medication dramatically dropped.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Discernment & Perspective

pearls.text: Doubling the dose of phenytoin can cause the level to jump from 6 to 30 due to zero-order kinetics.
pearls.verbatim: doubling that dose of your Dilantin can cause your level goes from six to 30.
pearls.speaker: Abdo
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Abdo on Common Acute Vestibular Syndromes

pearls.text: Abrupt onset of dizziness while walking with imbalance is highly suggestive of stroke.
pearls.verbatim: Abrupt onset while walking in the house with imbalance, what is this? While walking? Somebody who abruptly has dizziness, they're walking. I'm walking right now, and all of sudden, I get dizzy, and I have trouble walking. Stroke.
pearls.speaker: Abdo
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Abdo on Common Acute Vestibular Syndromes

pearls.text: Direction-changing nystagmus on gaze testing is a central sign and suggests stroke.
pearls.verbatim: Now when we look the other direction, nystagmus changes direction. Right? You guys see that? Yeah. So when you see this, it indicates what? Central.
pearls.speaker: Abdo
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Abdo on Common Acute Vestibular Syndromes

pearls.text: A vertical skew deviation on cover-uncover testing is highly suggestive of a central (stroke) etiology.
pearls.verbatim: If you see this, your patient probably has stroke.
pearls.speaker: Abdo
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Abdo on Common Acute Vestibular Syndromes

pearls.text: For the Dix-Hallpike, the head must be extended at least 20 degrees off the bed; use a shoulder roll if needed to achieve proper extension.
pearls.verbatim: At least 20 degrees. Can you do, like, a little under their shoulder to kind of pop them up? I do that sometimes in the ED. Okay. So, you know, put him on the shoulder. You gotta find a way to to get that head extension back there
pearls.speaker: Abdo
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Abdo on Common Acute Vestibular Syndromes

pearls.text: Patients with abrupt onset dizziness and consistent nystagmus plus vascular risk factors should be treated as stroke even if MRI is negative.
pearls.verbatim: Patients who present with abrupt onset dizziness, nice... Dizziness, and they have consistent nystagmus. Even if they look like this, I'm gonna treat... And they have vascular risk factors, I'm gonna treat them as a stroke.
pearls.speaker: Abdo
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Abdo on Common Acute Vestibular Syndromes

pearls.text: Always consider extrinsic causes of shoulder pain such as cervical radiculopathy, MI, hepatobiliary disease, pancreatitis, splenic injury, lung pathology, and herpes zoster before focusing on intrinsic shoulder disorders.
pearls.verbatim: Yes. MI. MI? Okay. Yeah. Absolutely. Cervical arthritis or cervical Yeah. Cervical spondylitis, cervical nerve compression, C5, C6 most commonly, but others can cause it. ...It's hepatobiliary would be even more. MI, and then splenic injury. Mhmm. Alright? So injury to the spleen. So just keep those things in mind because you can be fooled, and you don't wanna be fooled.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: Type IV–VI AC separations require urgent orthopedic referral: type IV has posterior displacement of the clavicle into the trapezius; type V has superior displacement with 2–3 times normal CC distance; type VI has inferior dislocation into the subacromial space.
pearls.verbatim: Four, you get a complete dislocation with posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into the trapezius. So it looks really strange, and I'll show you what that looks on X-ray. Five, you get a superior dislocation of the joint of one of... Of one to three times the normal spacing, increasing the CC, cricocorticoid ligament distance by two or three times. ...and then the last one, six, is a complete dislocation with inferior... So inferior dislocation of the distal clavicle.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: For type III AC separation, consider surgical referral for young athletes or manual laborers who need full shoulder mobility; older or sedentary patients can often heal conservatively.
pearls.verbatim: If you have a patient, though, who doesn't need to do it, they're gonna heal up. If you let this go on somebody who's in athletics and they wanna get back sooner rather than later or their job depends on their mobility, you wanna get them the best care you can get them the quickest. So that would be why you send an orthopedist.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: Scapular winging from long thoracic nerve injury typically heals with conservative treatment; no urgent intervention is needed.
pearls.verbatim: And that's a contusion of ... thoracic nerve. Yeah. So serratus anterior muscle is disrupted, so it just doesn't hold it in. Right? It's pretty cool. That will heal on its own with just conservative treatment of that nerve, calming that nerve down.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: For impingement syndrome with preserved strength, a subacromial steroid injection is appropriate; if a rotator cuff tear is suspected, obtain an MRI before injecting.
pearls.verbatim: I would say if you think they have a rotator cuff tear before you do an injection, I would get an MRI. I'd wanna know, is there a tear or not? If they have strength and you're pretty confident in your testing and you think it's impingement syndrome, then you can do a subacromial injection of steroids.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: Refer patients with adhesive capsulitis early if they are losing mobility, because lost time cannot be regained.
pearls.verbatim: So that's one that I I look for help earlier rather than later because if you lose more and more time, you never get it back.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: For recurrent impingement syndrome without a rotator cuff tear, a repeat injection can be given to get the patient over the hump.
pearls.verbatim: I test them again. It's clearly impingement syndrome. No rate rotator cuff tear. And then I would. Yeah. Get them over the hump again.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: Use age 40 as a cutoff: patients over 40 are more likely to have GH osteoarthritis, adhesive capsulitis, or rotator cuff tear; those under 40 are more likely to have tendinopathy.
pearls.verbatim: So just be on your guard for anybody forty years older. They could they could have these things. They're much more likely is what I'm trying to say. If they're younger than 40, they're much more likely to have a tendinopathy, rotator cuff tear, and these other things.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: AC separation grades 3 and above need orthopedic referral; grades 1 and 2 do not.
pearls.verbatim: Three or above. Three, maybe. Four and above, absolutely. One and two, definitely not.
pearls.speaker: Acker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Acker on Shoulder Disorders & Examination

pearls.text: Sleep deprivation is defined as 24+ hours without sleep or less than 5 hours per night for consecutive nights; use this to identify when you or a colleague may be impaired.
pearls.verbatim: they defined it as twenty four plus hours without sleep or less than five hours of sleep per night for consecutive nights.
pearls.speaker: Amanda Nichols
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amanda Nichols on Sleep Deprivation

pearls.text: Monitor for signs of sleep deprivation in yourself and colleagues: decreased vigilance, memory impairment, cognitive dysfunction, mood changes, and gross motor performance decline.
pearls.verbatim: decreased vigilance, memory, cognitive function, mood, and gross motor performance
pearls.speaker: Amanda Nichols
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amanda Nichols on Sleep Deprivation

pearls.text: Avoid alcohol and caffeine before bed to prevent disruption of sleep quality.
pearls.verbatim: avoiding alcohol and caffeine before bed
pearls.speaker: Amanda Nichols
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amanda Nichols on Sleep Deprivation

pearls.text: If you cannot fall asleep within 30 minutes, get out of bed and do something else to avoid conditioning wakefulness with the bedroom.
pearls.verbatim: getting out of bed and doing something else if not asleep within thirty minutes
pearls.speaker: Amanda Nichols
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amanda Nichols on Sleep Deprivation

pearls.text: Treat caffeine as a medicine: avoid it before sleep and after naps, and use it only when most fatigued to maximize benefit and minimize sleep disruption.
pearls.verbatim: view it as a medicine, not as a food. Avoid it before sleep and after naps. And then use it when most fatigued.
pearls.speaker: Amanda Nichols
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amanda Nichols on Sleep Deprivation

pearls.text: One milligram of buprenorphine is approximately equivalent to 20 mg of OxyContin; avoid starting in opioid-naive patients due to high potency.
pearls.verbatim: at very low doses, like one milligram of buprenorphine, it's very strong. So, like, you know, one milligram of buprenorphine is, like, you know, like, twenty milligram OxyContin. So you have to be careful. You don't wanna start this on opioid naive people.
pearls.speaker: Amell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amell on Opioid Stewardship 5/14/26

pearls.text: For microdosing induction, start with 0.5 mg buprenorphine BID (using quartered tablets or Belbuca 300 mcg) while continuing the full agonist.
pearls.verbatim: you start point five milligram pure buprenorphine. That's some... If if your hospital will allow you to quarter the tablets or the films, you can give point five milligram Subutex.
pearls.speaker: Amell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amell on Opioid Stewardship 5/14/26

pearls.text: For patients at high risk of leaving AMA, use a slower cross-taper and allow higher oral Dilaudid temporarily during the transition, but avoid IV Dilaudid.
pearls.verbatim: for some, you might wanna do a slower cross taper for someone that's, like, really high risk for leaving. And, you know, you should never just give a bunch of IV Dilaudid doses, but you can go up higher on oral Dilaudid if they need during this cross titration.
pearls.speaker: Amell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amell on Opioid Stewardship 5/14/26

pearls.text: When converting from Norco 10 mg q6, start with quarter-dose buprenorphine (e.g., 0.5 mg) while continuing Norco, then increase buprenorphine after a few days.
pearls.verbatim: you could start with, like, you know, the quarter the dose, you know, in the beginning and continuing the Norco. And then after a few days, you know, they they take two of the bupes.
pearls.speaker: Amell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Amell on Opioid Stewardship 5/14/26

pearls.text: If a patient's parent had hearing loss starting in their 60s, begin screening the patient 10 years earlier.
pearls.verbatim: Well, my dad had hearing loss, but it started in his sixties. Okay. They noticed it in the sixties. We're gonna start looking ten years earlier.
pearls.speaker: Anne Hogan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Anne Hogan on Hearing Loss 3/12/26

pearls.text: Scarred eardrums (tympanosclerosis) do not cause hearing loss; cholesteatomas, however, can cause conductive loss and require otologic evaluation.
pearls.verbatim: Scarred eardrums do not cause hearing loss. There is no correlation between hearing loss and tympanosclerosis or, like I said, monomeric eardrums. ... That is a pocket of ear wax and skin and debris from the ear from a weakened area of the eardrum that starts and push into the middle ear. That would cause a conductive hearing loss.
pearls.speaker: Anne Hogan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Anne Hogan on Hearing Loss 3/12/26

pearls.text: Use the free Mimi app on a smartphone to screen hearing in a quiet room; it provides decently accurate thresholds and configuration, which is helpful for patients with fluctuating hearing loss who cannot always come in for testing.
pearls.verbatim: There's an app called Mimi, m i m i, free app on that on any smartphone. You can actually screen your own hearing that way and test it. It's decently accurate with thresholds, at least with configuration. But you have to be in a really quiet room, that type of thing. I have that.
