pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: Intubating a patient with PE is dangerous because positive pressure increases intrathoracic pressure, worsening right ventricular strain and precipitating arrhythmia or death.
pearls.verbatim: Because you increase the intrathoracic pressure, creates more heart strain, makes them go into, like, arrhythmia, they die. Super dangerous.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: Use low PEEP (≤10 cm H2O) and high FiO2 when ventilating a patient with known or suspected PE to minimize hemodynamic compromise.
pearls.verbatim: you really get that FIO2 as high as you can and get that positive end-expiratory pressure as low as you can because you don't wanna increase the extra pressure. So 10 or less is kind of the the goal.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: Use two sprays per nostril twice daily for at least two weeks, then taper to once daily.
pearls.verbatim: Two sprays each nostril morning night.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Do not treat acute sinusitis with antibiotics unless symptoms have persisted for at least 10 days without improvement.
pearls.verbatim: The definition is ten days, so not seven days, not five days.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Avoid macrolides (e.g., Z-Pak) for sinusitis due to poor efficacy.
pearls.verbatim: Don't use Z Pak. Don't use macrolides.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Use high-dose amoxicillin-clavulanate (2 g twice daily) as first-line for sinusitis if patient has risk factors: age >65, recent hospitalization, antibiotics in past month, immunocompromised, diabetes, CAD.
pearls.verbatim: You just go straight to two grams twice a day, not the eight seventy five.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: In patients with pharyngitis and high-risk sexual behavior (MSM, oral sex), test for gonorrhea and chlamydia.
pearls.verbatim: If there's any concern for oral sex, MSM, you have to ask them about it and then culture it.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: If patients do not meet Centor criteria, do not test because you are not going to treat them for strep.
pearls.verbatim: If they don't meet the criteria, then don't do the test because you're not gonna treat them for it.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: For patients with Centor greater than 3 who have additional risk factors, treat despite a negative rapid test.
pearls.verbatim: Centor greater than three go additional risk factors.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Trust a negative rapid antigen test; do not routinely send a culture.
pearls.verbatim: If it's negative, trust that it's negative.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Consider mononucleosis when sore throat is severe and other tests are negative.
pearls.verbatim: If it's a really sore throat, you know, well, maybe it's mono.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Prescribe amoxicillin 500 mg twice daily for 10 days for streptococcal pharyngitis.
pearls.verbatim: Amoxicillin, this is ten days, five hundred milligrams twice a day.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Idiopathic neuropathy often has a spinal cause; order a lumbar MRI to check for a bulging or slipped disc.
pearls.verbatim: Especially check their back. That's probably the number one secondary reason neuropathy in the feet is people have a bulging disc or slipped disc or arthritic change in the back. So lumbar MRI is an easy way to identify that.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: If a diabetic patient has a septic joint or abscess, they may not mount a septic response; this is limb-threatening and needs urgent surgical drainage.
pearls.verbatim: If you have a septic joint or abscess, they're not gonna mount a septic response. That needs to be addressed surgically.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: In a diabetic patient with unilateral swelling and redness but no remembered injury, obtain an X-ray to rule out Charcot foot (dislocation/fracture) before assuming cellulitis.
pearls.verbatim: If you ever see a diabetic patient and they come in with unilateral swelling, redness. Even if they say, I don't remember entering it, take an X-ray. Don't just assume it's cellulitis because they may just have a dislocating foot, and they don't even know it.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Advise diabetic patients to inspect their feet daily; if they cannot bend down, use a mirror or a phone camera.
pearls.verbatim: If they can't bend down to look at look at... Have them lean a mirror up against the wall to where they just kinda, you know, sit down and hold their foot up and look or have a family member look at their foot or use the phone to take a picture.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: To check shoe fit at home, remove the insole, place it on the floor, and step on it. If the foot spills over the edge, the shoe is too narrow; if toes are closer than a thumb's width to the end, the shoe is too short.
pearls.verbatim: Take the insole out, put it on the floor, and step on it. If your foot falls off the side, then you know it's too narrow. Or when you step on it, if your toes are closer than a thumb's width to the end of that insole, it's too short.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Check shoe fit at every visit; improperly fitting shoes are a common cause of diabetic foot ulcers and reducing surgeries requires addressing this simple issue.
pearls.verbatim: I didn't used to check shoes, and there's a lot of surgeons that still don't. My surgery volume almost cut in half when I started checking shoe fit.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: For wound cleansing, use a hypochlorous solution (Vashe), diluted Betadine to the color of dark tea, or Hibiclens—avoid repeated application over granulating tissue.
pearls.verbatim: Wound wash like saline or Vashe, which is a hypochlorous solution, which is a great... Or even diluted Betadine. So patients don't have an iodine allergy, you can put Betadine down to where it's like a dark tea.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Obtain a deep wound culture (preferably tissue) before administering any antibiotics in the ED; a superficial swab is less reliable.
pearls.verbatim: try to do that before the ER, you know, gives them a shot of Rocephin or anything. It's best to get that culture early.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: In patients with a foot abscess, septic joint, gas on X-ray, or crepitus on palpation—those are surgical emergencies, not to be treated with antibiotics alone.
pearls.verbatim: All foot abscesses, septic joints, gas noticed on X-ray, or if you push on a foot or try to milk a wound and it's, like, crackly, crepitation on soft tissue, that's a surgical emergency.
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Use 5–6 cc of bupivacaine (Marcaine) for the digital block.
pearls.verbatim: Five to six cc's max is all you need
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Phenol is preferred for nail matrix ablation because it produces a superficial burn; avoid electrocautery or silver nitrate near the phalanx.
pearls.verbatim: phenol does a nice superficial burn, that's why it's good
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Avoid epinephrine in digital blocks for patients with known PAD, arterial disease, or diabetes.
pearls.verbatim: if they have known PAD or any suspicion of, you know, arterial disease or diabetes, I wouldn't do it
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Do not use roll-on tourniquets because they can be left in place under dressings; use a long elastic strip with a hemostat attached.
pearls.verbatim: don't use the roll on tourniquets
pearls.speaker: Beasley
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Beasley on Diabetic Foot Disease

pearls.text: Always ask about NSAID use, prior GI bleeds, peptic ulcer, and H. pylori history in patients with upper GI bleeding to assess perforation risk.
pearls.verbatim: Basic things are NSAID use, any history of upper GI bleeds, peptic ulcer, age, pylori history, those types of things. That just clues you in on, you know, what the risk of having a perforation, a big in their stomach.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Acute GI Concerns

pearls.text: In first-time pancreatitis, check a lipid panel to rule out hypertriglyceridemia; if triglycerides are in the thousands, you can treat with high-dose insulin drip or plasmapheresis to speed recovery.
pearls.verbatim: Check their lipid panel. Make sure they're not hypertriglyceridemia. Okay? Mhmm. The only reason I say that is because you can actually do something for that that patient. You put them on high dose insulin drip, and that can help them get over that pancreatitis faster.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Acute GI Concerns

pearls.text: Early enteral feeding in pancreatitis protects the mucosal barrier and reduces bacterial translocation; if no improvement after 48-72 hours and the patient becomes more bloated, call surgery to evaluate for abdominal compartment syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: early enteral feeding is thought to protect the mucosal barrier and reduce bacterial translocation. So that's why we do the enteral feeding. If after about forty eight to seventy two hours, they're not getting it better, actually getting more bloated, that's when you usually call surgery team to evaluate for abdominal compartment syndrome.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Acute GI Concerns

pearls.text: In septic patients with a ureteral stone and hydronephrosis, urgent urology consultation is needed because stent placement can trigger rapid deterioration from endotoxin release.
pearls.verbatim: if you see hydro and a stone and they're septic, those patients should probably come to the human. You just see a stone and they're septic, they don't necessarily have to come. You just see hydro and their septic, that isn't it. You have to have kind of all three of those things.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Acute GI Concerns

pearls.text: Pneumatosis intestinalis on CT indicates bowel ischemia; start heparin drip and call surgery, and be honest with the patient and family about the poor prognosis rather than leaving the bad news to the surgeon.
pearls.verbatim: You could probably put them on heparin drip and then call surgery. But what are telling the patient and family? He has lack of knowledge. Heparin Why drip? Do you think they had mesenteric ischemia? ... Be honest with your patients even if, you know, you you... By your first... By the end of your first year, you already know what's going on. You already know. You can tell what's gonna happen kinda down the road. Be honest with the patients even even whenever it's gonna be tough.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Acute GI Concerns

pearls.text: For small bowel obstruction without peritonitis, patients do not need ICU but require surgical consultation and possibly NG tube; however, if the patient is DNR/DNI and deteriorating, consider comfort-focused care instead of ICU transfer.
pearls.verbatim: Does that patient listen to ICU? No. No. They don't need to come to the ICU. They need a surgeon. They need a NG tube probably at some point if they start having nausea, vomiting. ... If they're DNR, DNI, there's not much that I can offer them that's different than what you guys can offer them if you're if you're in the
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Acute GI Concerns

pearls.text: For suspected asthma exacerbation, give albuterol first and reassess; if no improvement, step up therapy.
pearls.verbatim: It looks like asthma, seems like asthma, give them albuterol, and then reassess. It's not gonna be that hard. That's all it is. Just do the basic thing. And then if that doesn't work, step up.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Distress in Adults

pearls.text: Do not slow down compensatory tachypnea in DKA; it is the body's attempt to correct acidosis.
pearls.verbatim: You do not wanna slow that down. Okay? And then you're gonna have more problems on your hand. You're breathing fast because the problem is, in my mind, is when I was thinking of this case is somebody who's in DKA.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Distress in Adults

pearls.text: In a patient with chronic CO2 retention, a normal pH with low oxygen and high CO2 is their baseline; do not treat the hypoxia.
pearls.verbatim: If you see somebody like this, is that normal? No. What do think that is? Right? But their pH is normal. So this is... This is normal for them. I wouldn't treat this at all. I wouldn't give them oxygen. Well, maybe... Yeah. I wouldn't even give them oxygen. 85 is probably normal for them.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Distress in Adults

pearls.text: Absolute contraindications to BiPAP include GCS less than 7, vomiting, facial trauma, and cardiac arrest.
pearls.verbatim: GCS less than seven. Perfect. Anxious to get a mask on? That is a relative contraindication. Vomiting. Vomiting. K. Those are absolute ones. Facial trauma, vomiting, cardiac arrest.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Distress in Adults

pearls.text: Residents are responsible for ensuring DNR/DNI documentation, even if they cannot place the DNI order themselves.
pearls.verbatim: It is your responsibility, even though you're a resident, still your patient, still your responsibility to make sure if there are DNR and DNI that both orders are in.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Distress in Adults

pearls.text: Albumin for hypotension in ESRD is not helpful if albumin is between 3 and 4; only give albumin if the level is under 3.
pearls.verbatim: patients who have the albumin between three and four doesn't really help. It's it's no more different than giving some fluids. So if you're under three, that's that's when you usually give albumin.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Rapids, ICU Criteria 8/27/26

pearls.text: When using midodrine for hypotension, give it and see; if it works, it works, if not, stop.
pearls.verbatim: You can give it and just see. Usually, if if it works, it'll work. And if it doesn't, then I'll stop.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Rapids, ICU Criteria 8/27/26

pearls.text: For an unstable patient who is passing out or slumped, give electricity (cardioversion) regardless of rhythm.
pearls.verbatim: Unstable patient, doesn't matter what they're here for. Give them electricity.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Rapids, ICU Criteria 8/27/26

pearls.text: For stable AFib with RVR, give beta blockers; if you call EP they will say the same thing and see the patient in the morning.
pearls.verbatim: If you call EP, they'll say the same thing I will. Are they fine? Give them beta blockers. I'll see them in the morning.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Rapids, ICU Criteria 8/27/26

pearls.text: Address code status on every admission and daily rounds to ensure the patient's wishes are followed.
pearls.verbatim: Addressing it every time they're hospitalized and even every day on your rounds when you're in the hospital is is pretty important just to make sure that we're doing what the patient wants us to do.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Rapids, ICU Criteria 8/27/26

pearls.text: Communicate prognosis and goals of care directly at a fifth-grade education level to avoid confusion.
pearls.verbatim: Be very, very direct. Fifth grade education direct.
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Rapids, ICU Criteria 8/27/26

pearls.text: Use specific mortality rates (e.g., 97%) when delivering a dismal prognosis to make the severity clear.
pearls.verbatim: He had bleeds all the time with a mortality rate of ninety seven percent. I'd say this is an unsurvivable injury
pearls.speaker: Bhakta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bhakta on Rapids, ICU Criteria 8/27/26

pearls.text: IV iron should not be given in the first trimester due to lack of safety data; start at 13 weeks or later.
pearls.verbatim: For IV iron, it's... There's no safety data in the first trimester. So you want to give it 13 and above is when IV iron can be started.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: Avoid iron dextran in pregnancy and postpartum because it contains benzoyl alcohol and requires multiple doses.
pearls.verbatim: that one, because it has benzoyl alcohol in it and you have to give it multiple times, you actually don't wanna use it in pregnancy.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: After starting treatment for anemia, repeat CBC in 2-3 weeks to assess response.
pearls.verbatim: And then you re get the CBC in the twenty four to twenty eight week period, and then you treat if it meets criteria, and then you repeat again in two to three weeks.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: If anemia does not improve with oral iron, check ferritin, B12, and folate, and consider IV iron.
pearls.verbatim: If it improves, then you continue. If there's no change, then you can consider getting a ferritin B12 folate and making sure all that looks good, and then consider IV iron.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: Prescribe oral iron every other day, not twice daily, because hepcidin blocks absorption for 24 hours after a dose.
pearls.verbatim: Please don't give anybody BID. The backdrop about that is why we do it every other day is because the liver makes hepcidin, which blocks any other incoming iron because iron excess, the body has no other process to get rid of it. So to protect us for twenty four hours, hepcidin goes up, so you can't even absorb iron well after that. So it's just they're having worsening constipation for no reason.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: Treat folate deficiency in pregnancy with 1 mg folic acid daily.
pearls.verbatim: And you wanna supplement with one milligram of folic acid daily.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: In sickle cell disease, increase folate supplementation to 4 mg daily due to high red blood cell turnover.
pearls.verbatim: And the folate requirement is actually four milligrams daily instead of just the one because they have such of a high red blood cell turnover, higher than average.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: Ascension's algorithm for iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy: start IV iron if hemoglobin is less than 10 and ferritin is less than 30 in the second or third trimester.
pearls.verbatim: The thing is they go straight to IV iron. Your hemoglobin is less than 10 and ferritin is less than 30 in the second and third trimester, after getting to ferritin, they go straight to IV iron and then repeating labs four weeks after last dose.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: For iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy, target hemoglobin is greater than 11; overshooting that target is not dangerous and better prepares the patient for delivery.
pearls.verbatim: target would be more than 11. I think a lot of times in practice, it's tough. You overshoot that, and that's fine. When they have those up their store, they're prepared for delivery, it wouldn't be a problem.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Anemia of Pregnancy

pearls.text: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is contraindicated in breastfeeding mothers of infants younger than 2 months or who are immunocompromised due to risk of kernicterus.
pearls.verbatim: the cross is because babies who are less than two months and are immunocompromised, moms should not take Bactrim.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Breastfeeding

pearls.text: Breast milk can be left at room temperature for 4 hours (commonly accepted); refrigerated up to four days; once thawed (if not previously frozen), use within 1-2 hours.
pearls.verbatim: We made it to four. And then refrigerator up to four days, and then it can be further. ... once it's thawed and hasn't previously frozen, then one to two hours and up to a day.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Breastfeeding

pearls.text: HIV-positive mothers can breastfeed only if viral suppression is achieved during pregnancy and maintained postpartum; otherwise it is contraindicated.
pearls.verbatim: HIV mom is another one. If they're not on ART, ART has not been... Not achieved viral suppression during pregnancy, minimum throughout third trimester, or at the time of delivery, or is unable to maintain a viral suppression postpartum.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Breastfeeding

pearls.text: Use LactMed (a free NIH resource) to check drug safety in breastfeeding; it compiles drug levels in breast milk and summary recommendations.
pearls.verbatim: Is this safe in breastfeeding? It just goes through all of the drugs ... the drug levels that are passed through breast milk. Summary of if it should or should not be used.
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Breastfeeding

pearls.text: Preeclampsia can cause morbidity and maternal death.
pearls.verbatim: preeclampsia can cause morbidity and can also kill
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Effects of Vitamin D Supplementation and Pregnancy Outcomes: Pre-Eclampsia

pearls.text: The study did not control for other variables such as prenatal vitamin use or aspirin, which could confound outcomes.
pearls.verbatim: it didn't discuss, like, if they were taking prenatals, were they all taking the same one, were they on aspirin, any other variables that could be compounding the outcome
pearls.speaker: Bothwell
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bothwell on Effects of Vitamin D Supplementation and Pregnancy Outcomes: Pre-Eclampsia

pearls.text: The monthly payment on $400,000 in student debt at 7.5% interest over ten years is roughly $5,000 per month, a huge percentage of a starting physician's take-home pay.
pearls.verbatim: monthly payment on $400 at seven and a half percent is roughly $5 a month for ten years.
pearls.speaker: Brad Hardy
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Brad Hardy on Contracts, Coding, and Resident Financial Basics

pearls.text: Individual disability insurance policies are portable and should be purchased during residency because they become more expensive and harder to obtain after a diagnosis like diabetes or autoimmune disease.
pearls.verbatim: doing things now before you have something on your medical record is is is the time to do it.
pearls.speaker: Brad Hardy
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Brad Hardy on Contracts, Coding, and Resident Financial Basics

pearls.text: Don't mix investing with life insurance; use term life and invest separately.
pearls.verbatim: you really shouldn't mix investing with life insurance. Those are two separate things.
pearls.speaker: Brad Hardy
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Brad Hardy on Contracts, Coding, and Resident Financial Basics

pearls.text: Use Roth accounts now as a resident because you're not in your peak earnings years.
pearls.verbatim: Roth accounts would be a good idea to use right now just because you guys are not in your peak earnings years.
pearls.speaker: Brad Hardy
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Brad Hardy on Contracts, Coding, and Resident Financial Basics

pearls.text: Avoid buying the 'doctor house' right out of residency—it can become golden handcuffs.
pearls.verbatim: maybe don't buy the doctor house.
pearls.speaker: Brad Hardy
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Brad Hardy on Contracts, Coding, and Resident Financial Basics

pearls.text: Ask about tail coverage if you leave or are fired.
pearls.verbatim: What happens if you leave? Is there gonna be tail covers included?
pearls.speaker: Brad Hardy
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Brad Hardy on Contracts, Coding, and Resident Financial Basics

pearls.text: When taking a bleeding history, ask about normal periods off birth control to establish baseline.
pearls.verbatim: When you're comparing the abnormal to the normal, you want to get normal. You don't wanna get when they're on birth control pills.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding

pearls.text: Ask about number of pads/tampons used on the heaviest day to quantify menstrual bleeding.
pearls.verbatim: The two questions I use are how many pads or tampons used on the heaviest day.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding

pearls.text: Use high-estrogen birth control pills to increase SHBG and treat hirsutism in PCOS.
pearls.verbatim: One of the treatments for PCOS is to give birth control pills. Birth control pills are high estrogen. High estrogen goes to the liver and increases sex hormone binding globulin, binding the testosterone. This is a way of stopping hirsutism associated with PCOS.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding

pearls.text: After menarche, allow up to 2 years for cycles to regulate; if still irregular at 6 months (in a patient 18 months post-menarche), evaluate for chronic anovulation.
pearls.verbatim: If she comes back in six months and she's still irregular, then you begin to evaluate for chronic anovulation.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding

pearls.text: Postmenopausal bleeding at age 60 or older is suspicious for endometrial cancer.
pearls.verbatim: You have a woman coming into your office who's aged 60 and still menstruating problem, looks like. Could be endometrial cancer.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding

pearls.text: When evaluating infertility, always ask how long the patient has been trying; 2 years is a good time interval to define infertility.
pearls.verbatim: You always want, when you're considering infertility, to know how long have they been trying to become pregnant. Two years is a good time interval.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Chronic Anovulation, and PCOS

pearls.text: Always test for insulin resistance in suspected PCOS because 20-80% of women have both conditions, and treatment priority depends on which is more severe.
pearls.verbatim: The reason you want to do this, even if you suspect PCOS by itself, you should get an insulin resistance test. Twenty to eighty percent of women have both PCOS and insulin resistance.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Chronic Anovulation, and PCOS

pearls.text: If a PCOS patient has no periods, you must provoke withdrawal bleeding at least 2-3 times per year to prevent endometrial cancer.
pearls.verbatim: you can't let them go forever without having periods. You have to evacuate the uterus two or three times a year.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Chronic Anovulation, and PCOS

pearls.text: Use birth control pills not just for cycle regulation but to increase sex hormone-binding globulin, thereby lowering free testosterone and preventing new terminal hair growth.
pearls.verbatim: you can put a woman on birth control pills, not to regulate her periods necessarily, but to increase the sex hormone binding globulin to decrease the free testosterone so she stops getting conversion of villous hairs to terminal hairs.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Chronic Anovulation, and PCOS

pearls.text: Use the fasting glucose/insulin ratio to assess insulin resistance: normal fasting glucose ~100 mg/dL, normal fasting insulin ~20 µU/mL, giving a ratio of 5; a ratio below 5 is abnormal.
pearls.verbatim: So normal glucose is a 100. Normal insulin is 20. So what's the normal ratio? Five five five.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Chronic Anovulation, and PCOS

pearls.text: For severe insulin resistance (fasting ratio <5), start metformin 500 mg twice daily (morning and evening) to normalize insulin and promote ovulation.
pearls.verbatim: If you're gonna treat this person, you're probably gonna have to give them two five hundred milligram metformin a day, one in the morning and one in the evening.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Chronic Anovulation, and PCOS

pearls.text: A pragmatic fertility trick: give continuous birth control pills for 4 months to lower testosterone; many patients ovulate and conceive in the next 2-3 months after stopping.
pearls.verbatim: I have taken people with PCOS. I have given them continuous birth control pills for four months. Is that gonna do the testosterone? Lower it and then stop. Get pregnant in the next two or three months after you stop.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Abnormal Uterine Bleeding, Chronic Anovulation, and PCOS

pearls.text: Obtain a detailed sexual history: age at first intercourse and number of lifetime sexual partners help assess risk for sexually transmitted infections.
pearls.verbatim: Age of first intercourse, 14. Lifetime sexual partner, seven. What does that tell you? That she has high risk sexual behavior or she was in some not good relationships. Tells me that she's at high risk sexual behavior.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Adnexal Masses

pearls.text: For infertility, assess timing of intercourse; having sex every night from day 5-15 may reduce sperm count and decrease chances of conception.
pearls.verbatim: Another thing you can see is, well, we have sex every every night from day five to day 15. So what's the problem with that? It's not the egg. Only one egg. It's a sperm. A male makes only so many sperm, and they're stored. And if they ejaculate every night, we're reducing reservoir.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Adnexal Masses

pearls.text: Sudden, severe pelvic pain that migrates from the left to the right side indicates intraperitoneal fluid (blood) from a ruptured hemorrhagic cyst.
pearls.verbatim: The pain is sudden onset. It drives into the floor. Severe. It moved from the left to the right because the blood started in the left. And as it was released, it moved over to the right and irritated the peritoneum on the right side.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Adnexal Masses

pearls.text: A stable patient with a ruptured hemorrhagic ovarian cyst can be managed at home with observation for 2-3 days if pain is controlled.
pearls.verbatim: She's stable and the pain is controlled, she could probably be bothered at home. She would probably have to be told you would need to be home two or three days.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Adnexal Masses

pearls.text: Most women with ovarian cancer are symptomatic at diagnosis; do not rely on asymptomatic status to rule it out.
pearls.verbatim: Are most women symptomatic when they have... When they're diagnosed with ovarian cancer? Yes.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Adnexal Masses

pearls.text: A pedunculated uterine fibroid can be mistaken for an adnexal mass; include it in the differential.
pearls.verbatim: What could that something be? Ovary or the tube. Ovary tube or something different. Okay. Unculated uterine fibroid.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Adnexal Masses

pearls.text: When evaluating an adnexal mass, consider ovary, fallopian tube, or pedunculated fibroid as possibilities.
pearls.verbatim: What could that something be? Ovary or the tube. Ovary tube or something different.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Adnexal Masses

pearls.text: For recurrent bacterial vaginosis, give metronidazole for 1-2 days at first symptom to prevent full infection.
pearls.verbatim: You can give her metronidazole and have her take it as soon as she gets the first symptom for a day or two. Some women just have to take a day's worth. Some women have to take two days worth. But by doing that, you're giving her control.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Cervical Vaginal Infection

pearls.text: Use condoms and over-the-counter vaginal pH buffers to maintain pH below 4.5 and prevent bacterial vaginosis.
pearls.verbatim: So for semen, you use condoms. There's also... You can you can get over the counter buffers, vaginal buffers that can be used. Women will put in the vagina to buffer her pH to below 4.5.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Cervical Vaginal Infection

pearls.text: Candida glabrata is resistant to fluconazole; confirm with NAAT and treat with ibrexafungerp.
pearls.verbatim: Candida glabrata is the one that is resistant to diflucan. Across the board, resistant.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Cervical Vaginal Infection

pearls.text: For recurrent candidiasis, give fluconazole every 3 days for induction then weekly for 6 months.
pearls.verbatim: You're gonna manage it by the initial treatment, one every three days. And then you're gonna give one dose a week for six months.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Cervical Vaginal Infection

pearls.text: Menopause is defined as no period for one year; use this to counsel patients about timing.
pearls.verbatim: Once you have not had a period for one year, we call that menopause.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Chronic Anovulation & PCOS

pearls.text: Start combination birth control pills on the first day of the cycle because low estrogen in the first three days can make the pill ineffective if started later.
pearls.verbatim: The first two to three days of the cycle, days one, two, and three, estrogen is estrogen is very low. K? This is important when you're using birth control pills because this is first three days that you have to start your birth control pill. You don't start the birth control pills, particularly the low... Ones with low estrogen in the first three days, then that pill may not be effective that cycle. So it's best when you tell a woman to start her pills to wait for her cycle and start on the first day of her cycle.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Chronic Anovulation & PCOS

pearls.text: Hot flushes alone do not indicate perimenopause; perimenopause is defined by a change in menstrual periods.
pearls.verbatim: Hot flushes do not indicate the onset of perimenopause. You in your practice will have women come in in their thirties who have hot flushes. K? So it's not hot flushes. Menopause, by definition, currently is a change in the menstrual periods.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Chronic Anovulation & PCOS

pearls.text: Counsel perimenopausal women that average age of menopause is 52; 95% have reached menopause by age 54.
pearls.verbatim: The average age is 52. And if you're 48, you probably have four more years. On the other hand, if you have somebody come in at age 55, at age 54, ninety five percent of women have gone through menopause and become menopausal.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Chronic Anovulation & PCOS

pearls.text: Always ask about recent stress in a woman with secondary amenorrhea; it is a common cause of hypothalamic amenorrhea.
pearls.verbatim: I will tell you right now, you will see this woman, but you will fail to ask the question about stress. I know that because I did for years. But finally, I started asking the question. And almost always, they come up with an episode of stress.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Chronic Anovulation & PCOS

pearls.text: Palpate vaginal lesions for thickness; if present, biopsy.
pearls.verbatim: So you have to you have to use your fingers. You have to feel, and you have to biopsy.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Exam & Pathology 6/4/26

pearls.text: Always perform a pelvic exam for vaginal complaints; do not trust an ER evaluation without examination.
pearls.verbatim: What's the lesson to learn? Examined.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Exam & Pathology 6/4/26

pearls.text: A pigmented vulvar lesion with irregular borders and multiple colors (black, blue, red, white) is suspicious for melanoma; biopsy and refer simultaneously.
pearls.verbatim: That is nevus with many atypical features concerning for melanoma. ... Biopsy and refer at the same time?
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Exam Pathology 5/7/26

pearls.text: When examining a vulvar lesion, do not focus solely on one finding; you may miss a second pathology like herpes simplex adjacent to a melanoma.
pearls.verbatim: Sometimes you get so focused on one thing. It's something very obvious. ... You might have been looking at herpes simplex and ignore melanoma.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Exam Pathology 5/7/26

pearls.text: HPV warts are hard and firm on palpation, unlike normal papillae or skin tags which are soft; always palpate to differentiate.
pearls.verbatim: The difference is if you touch it with your finger, these are very hard, very firm.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Exam Pathology 5/7/26

pearls.text: Patients with lichen sclerosus need vulvar exams every six months to monitor for skin cancer; look for firm, raised lesions that burrow deep when you pinch the skin.
pearls.verbatim: So a person like this with this extensive lichen sclerosus, you would wanna see them about every six months. Mhmm. And just check to make sure that they're not skin cancer.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Exam Pathology 5/7/26

pearls.text: Lichen planus causes very tender eroded areas; look inside the mouth for white lacy cobwebs (Wickham striae) to help confirm diagnosis.
pearls.verbatim: Like in planus, what you do is you look inside the mouth. It's on the cheek. Whiteish cobwebs.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Exam Pathology 5/7/26

pearls.text: When in doubt about a vulvar lesion, perform a full-thickness punch biopsy to confirm diagnosis.
pearls.verbatim: If you're not sure, what do you do? Biops. Biops. Okay. As you can see now, it could be confusing.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: Lichen planus is distinguished from lichen sclerosus by purple plaques and oral involvement; check the mouth for white web-like lesions and geographic tongue.
pearls.verbatim: And so you look in the mouth, and you see these whitish web like lesions on the cheek and the geographic tongue. You put those two together, you have lichen planus.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: Urethral caruncles are benign polyps in older women that may bleed; usually no treatment needed unless they obstruct urination.
pearls.verbatim: These are urethral carnals. There are polyps coming out of the urethra. They're very common in older women. K. See them. K. And on the right, you see the black? That's because it's hemorrhaged. So sometimes they'll bleed, and that may bring the patient into you.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: Do not delay management for an ultrasound when abruption is suspected; clinical diagnosis using fetal heart tones and pain is more reliable.
pearls.verbatim: You really wanna make the diagnosis. Can show the location and the type. So, you know, retroplacental, I think that's a in that diagram, right behind the placenta, that's gonna present more risk.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: About 90% of placenta previas diagnosed early in the second trimester will resolve as the uterus expands, so reassure patients and do not induce unnecessary anxiety.
pearls.verbatim: If you look at second trimester ultrasound, you'll have a lot of placenta previas, a lot of low lying placentas. Know that ninety percent of those will go away.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: Painless bleeding in the second or third trimester should raise suspicion for placenta previa; about 90% of patients will have bleeding before labor.
pearls.verbatim: Classic presentation is painless bleeding in the second and third trimester. And about ninety percent will have a bleeding episode before the onset of labor.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: Repeat ultrasound at 32 weeks for placenta previa because 90% resolve by then.
pearls.verbatim: we wanna repeat the ultrasound by thirty two weeks. Like we said, ninety percent will resolve
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: In vasa previa, rapid vaginal bleeding after rupture of membranes is fetal blood; immediate cesarean delivery is needed.
pearls.verbatim: If you have a vasa previa and you have rapid bleeding, whose blood is that? That's the baby's blood. They're not gonna tolerate that. So you need... move towards delivery extra extra fast
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: Risk of uterine rupture is about 1% for a low transverse scar and about 10% for a classical vertical incision; do not recommend TOLAC with a classical scar.
pearls.verbatim: A low transverse or a low vertical scar, right about one percent risk. ... if they had a classical vertical incision or an eat up incision, then the risk goes up to almost one in ten.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: If the interval from the prior cesarean to the estimated due date is less than 18 months, do not recommend TOLAC.
pearls.verbatim: If it's been less than eighteen months between deliveries, then we don't really like to do a TOLAC.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 11/6/25

pearls.text: Palpate lesions to differentiate vesicles (soft, fluid-filled) from Fordyce spots (hard) and warts (hard, irregular).
pearls.verbatim: How are you gonna tell the difference? Oh, the fingers. Yeah. Palpate them. Yeah. Vessel's gonna be what? It's gonna give a little bit, like something inside. These don't... They're absolutely hard.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 9/4/25

pearls.text: Lichen planus causes pain (not itch) and erythema; always check the oral mucosa for characteristic findings.
pearls.verbatim: Lichen planus. Quite similar except there's more erythema in the area. Unlike the itch or lichen sclerosus, this is pain. Feel pain with this. And if you touch these areas, they're extremely painful. When we look inside the mouth, the vocal cavity, mouth webbing, tongue, has characteristic of lichen planus. So if you see lichen lichen... Think it's lichen sclerosis, you all always wanna check to make sure the mouth is clear.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 9/4/25

pearls.text: Herpes simplex presents with grouped vesicles, pustules, and erosions at different stages; a prodrome (tingling, pain, itch) is almost always present.
pearls.verbatim: Herpes simplex almost always starts with what? A prodrome. Almost always, a patient will tell you that they felt something. Could be pain. Could be itch. Could be a tingle, and then they notice the lesion. This is pretty... I use it as primary for the diagnosis. Got it. The other thing is that you have stages. You have pustules, k, that are clear, white. Excuse me. You have clear vesicles, then you have pustules. Then you have the tops coming off them. You have eroded areas. K? Typical presentation is that you have groups. K? And, usually, you will see at least two of those three presentations present.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination Pathology 9/4/25

pearls.text: Skene's gland cysts are benign blocked glands; only incise and drain if needed, and consider placing a catheter to keep the duct open.
pearls.verbatim: The only incise and kind of operate As if you may have in my incise and drain. Yeah. Only when, like, only needed. Sometimes you can put a catheter in there and keep them open for a while.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination & Pathology

pearls.text: Gartner duct cysts are embryologic remnants that can extend deep into the abdomen; do not operate or drain because you may end up near the kidney.
pearls.verbatim: The problem if you fuss with them is you don't know how far that cyst goes up into the abdomen. If you start to do surgery on it or drain it, you don't know where you'll end up. You end up next to the kidney. So it's best to leave it alone.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination & Pathology

pearls.text: To examine for urethral diverticulum, place your finger against the anterior vaginal wall and milk the urethra downward; you will feel a bump.
pearls.verbatim: How can you examine for diverticulum? It's a maneuver. It's a simple maneuver. You just tip your finger against the roof. I'm caught. And then empty. You... All the urethra down, you feel a bump.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination & Pathology

pearls.text: For a first-time Bartholin gland abscess, use a Word catheter for drainage.
pearls.verbatim: First time you do what? Word catheter.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination & Pathology

pearls.text: Always perform a vulvar exam; patients with vaginal discharge may have serious pathology missed if not examined.
pearls.verbatim: She's been to two emergency rooms for vaginal discharge. She was treated vaginal discharge in both emergency rooms. They never examined her.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Female Vulva Examination & Pathology

pearls.text: When doing a bimanual exam, do not dig down; use your vaginal fingers to push the cervix upward to bring the uterus toward the abdominal wall.
pearls.verbatim: You don't... You're not trying to press down and dig down to find it. You need to bring the uterus to you with your fingers.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on GYN Adnexal Mass

pearls.text: When an ultrasound reports 'complex cyst', consider it abnormal and potentially malignant; do not try to stage it yourself—just note 'complex' or 'simple'.
pearls.verbatim: Look for the word simple or complex in your office. . . . If you have an ultrasound report that says the cyst is complex, it's one, two, three. It's abnormal, and it's most likely could be cancer.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on GYN Adnexal Mass

pearls.text: For severe dysmenorrhea keeping patient out of school, naproxen may not help; use combined oral contraceptives to thin endometrium and reduce prostaglandins.
pearls.verbatim: Using naproxen doesn't help much for severe. So you wanna do something like a birth control pill.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on GYN Inservice Review 10/2/25

pearls.text: Chronic anovulation requires evaluation for both PCOS and insulin resistance; treat the primary driver first.
pearls.verbatim: Best to evaluate PCOS and insulin resistance, to see what is causing... What the primary cause. If they're both are causal and insulin resistance is more severe, then you start by treating insulin resistance. If they're both causal, PCOS is the primary driver, then you just treat PCOS.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on GYN Inservice Review 10/2/25

pearls.text: Submucosal fibroids cause heavy menstrual bleeding; intramural and subserosal fibroids typically do not.
pearls.verbatim: Which of those three cause heavy breathing? Mucousal. Intramural doesn't. Subserosal doesn't.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on GYN Inservice Review 10/2/25

pearls.text: For symptomatic fibroids in a patient wanting to avoid hysterectomy, uterine artery embolization is the non-surgical option.
pearls.verbatim: Do an embolization. It's the only procedure you have to do that's not surgical.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on GYN Inservice Review 10/2/25

pearls.text: For breast pain, ask if it is cyclic or random; cyclic is almost always physiologic and can be managed conservatively.
pearls.verbatim: Cyclic or is it random? She's a Sleepical. Physiologic. It's cyclic. K. So you've immediately cut your differential considerably.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on GYN Inservice Review 10/2/25

pearls.text: Low-dose birth control pills (15-25 mcg) must be started on the first day of menses; starting even three days late may allow FSH to trigger follicle formation.
pearls.verbatim: On the low dose birth control pills, which are fifteen, to twenty five micrograms. It's absolutely important that they be given on the first day. Give them three... Even three days late, and the FSH has already been triggered.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: For dysmenorrhea or menorrhagia, select a strong progestin (group 1 or 2) to thin the endometrium and reduce prostaglandins.
pearls.verbatim: if you have somebody who has heavy menstrual bleeding, we want to give them a birth control pill to minimize bleeding, you're gonna pick a high progestin.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: For patients with acne, avoid levonorgestrel or norgestrel (strong androgen) and choose a low-androgen progestin like desogestrel or norgestimate.
pearls.verbatim: if you have a person wanting birth control pills and she has problems with acne, you're not going to give her levonorgestrel. You're gonna wanna pick something, the serum.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: Breakthrough bleeding in the first half of the cycle indicates low estrogen or high progestin; manage by increasing estrogen or decreasing progestin.
pearls.verbatim: If they spot in the first half of the cycle, then they're low estrogen or high progesterone. So you wanna either increase the estrogen or decrease the progesterone.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: Breakthrough bleeding in the second half of the cycle indicates high estrogen or low progestin; manage by decreasing estrogen or increasing progestin.
pearls.verbatim: Close the second half of the cycle. Decrease the estrogen, which is the opposite of the first half. We'll say somebody's on a b and it's caught the second half of the cycle. Move on to a c. Increase the estrogen.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: In women over 40, use low-dose estrogen (group B or C) to minimize hypertension risk; in younger women (15-25), use 35 mcg estrogen for reliability.
pearls.verbatim: Into the forties, you should use low dose. The worst is also true, I think. When are you... When is your reproductive system most active? In his twenties. Fifteen to 35. Okay. Probably fifteen to twenties. Right? Fifteen to twenty. So it's probably not wise to give a low dose estrogen, very low dose estrogen in that age group.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: In perimenopausal women desiring cycle control, start a low-dose combined oral contraceptive, possibly with a third-generation progestin.
pearls.verbatim: if you think they're able to pill, then you probably start them on it. And so what would you pick? I'll do a c. C. With the lowest, that's impossible. And then you might want a third-generation progestin now.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: Half of women reach menopause by age 52, and 95% by age 54; use these ages as benchmarks for considering discontinuation of contraception.
pearls.verbatim: So at 52 or 54, and pick a time.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: To assess if menopause has occurred after stopping hormonal contraception, the patient must be willing to stop for a full month.
pearls.verbatim: You have to stop for a month. You can't just, you know, couple weeks. They have to be committed enough to stop for a month.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: Advise patients at age 48 to plan a time to stop contraception and observe; most will not need to restart.
pearls.verbatim: The age 48. You do work at a time. Yep. You have to... In your practice, you need to figure out how to do that and choose something different.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 4/9/26

pearls.text: Start combination birth control pills on the first day of the cycle to ensure efficacy.
pearls.verbatim: So if you ever have a question of when to start a birth control pill, start on the first day of the cycle.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 3/5/26

pearls.text: With low-dose estrogen pills, starting on the first day is critical; waiting until the second or third day may cause failure.
pearls.verbatim: You have to be sure that they start on the first day because if you wait till the second or third day, it's probably not gonna work for you.
pearls.speaker: Calvert
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Calvert on Hormonal Contraception 3/5/26

pearls.text: Avoid the contraceptive patch in women with BMI >30 because it is not effective.
pearls.verbatim: Somebody BMI above thirty shouldn't use this method. It's not gonna be effective.

pearls.text: Viscosupplementation must be injected into the joint space; it is worthless if extra-articular, so use ultrasound guidance.
pearls.verbatim: Because if I don't get this in the joint, it's gonna be completely worthless.
pearls.speaker: Cunningham
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cunningham on Osteoarthritis of the Knee 5/21/26

pearls.text: Use leukocyte-poor PRP (double spin to remove white blood cells) for knee osteoarthritis.
pearls.verbatim: I tend to do leukocyte four, which means you get a double spin and get those leukocytes out of there.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cunningham on Osteoarthritis of the Knee 5/21/26

pearls.text: If the patient has pain during a knee injection, you likely hit the fat pad; redirect the needle to avoid it.
pearls.verbatim: And it shouldn't really hurt if you get in that joint capsule. If they're having pain, you probably missed.
pearls.speaker: Cunningham
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cunningham on Osteoarthritis of the Knee 5/21/26

pearls.text: For knee injections, use a 22-gauge, 1.5-inch needle, which is usually sufficient.

pearls.text: When aspirating a knee effusion, if you leave the needle in place and swap syringes, you confirm you are in the joint space before injecting steroid.

If they have a fusion on their knee, which lots of times with arthritis, you'll feel it, I'll aspirate that first, and I'll just leave the needle in, take off the syringe, and put a steroid in. That way, you got the fluid off. You know you're in the joint space, so you're gonna go right in there.
pearls.speaker: Cunningham
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cunningham on Osteoarthritis of the Knee 5/21/26

pearls.text: After a steroid knee injection, advise patients to take it easy for a day or two and avoid heavy squats, but no strict weight-bearing restriction.
pearls.verbatim: I usually tell them take it easy for a day or two. Okay. But I don't I don't limit them too much, and I want You don't need me on weight, man. I I just... pearls.episode_title: Dr. Cunningham on Osteoarthritis of the Knee 5/21/26

pearls.text: Pulmonary rehabilitation improves FEV1 and lung function as much as starting another pharmaceutical, and it addresses deconditioning that medications cannot.
pearls.verbatim: the pulmonary rehab is actually improving FEV1s and lung function just as much as starting another pharmaceutical
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: For oxygen qualification, check resting and ambulatory oxygen saturation; desaturation below 88% is the key threshold.
pearls.verbatim: you're looking for desaturation below 88%
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Roflumilast (Daliresp) commonly causes GI side effects; starting at half the dose for 1-2 weeks then increasing to full dose may improve tolerability.
pearls.verbatim: it was out for a couple years before people realized, well, you start fifty percent the dose, and then after a week or two of therapy, you increase it to the full
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Regular ICS use increases pneumonia risk (evidence level A); consider discontinuing ICS during hospitalization for COPD exacerbation with pneumonia.
pearls.verbatim: Regular treatment with the ICS increases the risk of pneumonia. Here it is in the guidelines, evidence level a
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Initiate ICS in COPD when eosinophilia is greater than 300 cells per microliter.
pearls.verbatim: if you're gonna measure the eosinophilia is greater than 300 cells per microliter
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Refer for lung transplant evaluation before DLCO drops below 20% or FEV1 below 20% predicted, because the evaluation takes time and patients may become ineligible.
pearls.verbatim: I'd rather get them to a transplant sitter before they become ineligible to have a transplant because the waiting list, number one. And secondly, there's this huge evaluation that goes on
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Dr. Dolin's preferred COPD action plan steroid taper: prednisone 40 mg x3 days, then 30 mg x3, 20 mg x3, 10 mg x3, then stop.
pearls.verbatim: I will usually do 40 of prednisone for three days and then thirty for three days, twenty for three days, and ten for three days, and then stop
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: For asthma, follow patients every three months until exacerbations are controlled and rescue inhaler use is no more than once or twice a month.
pearls.verbatim: I generally follow those folks every three months until I know they're not having exacerbations and they're not having to use their inhaler therapy for rescue more than once a month or twice a month
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: For COPD exacerbation, prescribe azithromycin 250 mg: two pills on day 1, then one pill daily for 4 days (total 6 pills).
pearls.verbatim: two hundred fifty milligrams of azithromycin, two pills on the first day, and then one pill a day for four days thereafter
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: For COPD exacerbation, use doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days.
pearls.verbatim: one hundred milligrams twice a day, usually for seven days
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: A negative ion bronchoscopy does not rule out lung cancer; the patient is not done and needs further evaluation.
pearls.verbatim: if you have a nodule and your path comes back negative on an ion procedure, you're not done. You you just got a nondiagnostic
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: If inpatient COPD exacerbation fails outpatient therapy and has purulent phlegm, obtain a sputum culture.
pearls.verbatim: if they have purulent phlegm production, get a sputum culture
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Taper IV steroids by 50% per day; 20 mg methylprednisolone q8h is equivalent to about 60 mg prednisone.
pearls.verbatim: twenty milligrams of solubadril every eight hours is roughly equivalent to sixty milligrams of prednisone
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: For acute asthma exacerbation in the ICU, give IV magnesium 4-6 grams for smooth muscle relaxation; limit to 2-3 doses.
pearls.verbatim: four grams, six grams to try and induce muscle relaxation
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Use peak expiratory flow monitoring with personal best and zone levels (green/yellow/red) instead of FeNO for asthma home monitoring.
pearls.verbatim: I'm still okay doing peak expiratory flows and having someone's personal best and then they're kinda zone and then their red zone as far as their airflow limitation
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Start montelukast (Singulair) if IgE >30; order RAST allergy testing before starting to avoid needing to hold the drug for weeks.
pearls.verbatim: if the IgE level is greater than 30, then I'll I'll start them on Singulair. And that in and of itself, a lot of times, is very helpful. And from an allergy immunology standpoint, you you gotta get the RAST testing and the allergy stuff done before you put them on the Singulair. Otherwise, you have to hold it for weeks before you send them for testing
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: Refer patients to allergy-immunology for biologics like Xolair or when they need more than antihistamines and montelukast.
pearls.verbatim: when they get beyond the Zyrtec, Claritin, Allegra, Singulair stage and their, you know, allergy panels light up, allergy immunology is where I'm sending them
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease & Asthma

pearls.text: If a patient has both sleep apnea and periodic limb movements, treat the apnea first; often the leg movements resolve.
pearls.verbatim: A lot of times, if we treat the apnea, everything else just kinda falls into place and smooths out.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: For sleep aid in the lab, prescribe Zolpidem 5 mg thirty minutes before sleep.
pearls.verbatim: The most common one we prescribe is Zolpidem, a five milligram pill, to take thirty minutes before sleep.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: For insurance to cover CPAP equipment, a follow-up visit must occur within an 8 to 12 week window after starting therapy.
pearls.verbatim: it's an eight to twelve week window to
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: For inpatients with COPD exacerbation or heart failure, avoid a chronic PAP order; order an acute titration study instead to let the lab choose the mode and settings.
pearls.verbatim: If they have a a diagnosis where, you know, they're in for a COPD exacerbation or heart failure or something else, I would steer clear of the chronic order and put more acute and let them titrate.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: The best initial sleep study order is a split-night study, which can diagnose and titrate PAP in one night.
pearls.verbatim: In general, the best thing to order is gonna be a split night.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: Transition from CPAP to BiPAP when required pressure exceeds 16 cm H2O, so patients do not have to exhale against high resistance.
pearls.verbatim: But we start using BiPAPs when we get an excess of 16 centimeters of water pressure because we don't want the patients to have to exhale against all that air.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: If a patient cannot tolerate CPAP above 10 cm but still has AHI ~20, switch to BiPAP for comfort.
pearls.verbatim: Sometimes we get patients in the lab, and they're like, oh my gosh. Above a pressure of 10, they... They're like, this is too high, but their index is still, like, 20 an hour. So we'll switch them over to a BiPAP for comfort so that they don't feel like they're having to exhale against all that air.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: Avoid automatically ordering a CT scan for every patient with abdominal pain out of fear of missing something; this is defensive medicine, not good clinical reasoning.
pearls.verbatim: Why does every patient with abdominal pain that goes to the ER get a CT scan? So you don't miss something. And if you miss something, something bad could happen. And if that something bad happens, you're gonna get in trouble.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Resist the urge to repeat brain imaging on a patient with recurrent altered mental status if a recent scan was stable; doing so is driven by fear, not medical necessity.
pearls.verbatim: I've seen patients come in with altered mental status. It's the fifth presentation in twelve months. We're gonna scan their brain again just in case the brain tumor grew since the last scan six weeks ago. No. It didn't. I'm gonna do it.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Use the truck oil-check analogy to encourage men to get preventive care: 'You don't wait for the red light; you check the oil regularly. With your body, you only have one, so check it.'
pearls.verbatim: Do you ever check the oil? Oh, yeah. Every three months. Like clockwork. Why do you check the oil in your truck? Oh, I want my truck to run good. You don't wait for the red light. You don't wait for the smoke. You don't wait for the... But with your own body, you don't check the oil.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: When a patient is non-compliant, don't get offended. Instead, recognize that they either don't trust you or are scared of the treatment, and it is their right to refuse.
pearls.verbatim: If somebody doesn't do what I'm recommending, either they don't trust me or they're scared of the treatment. Something else going in there, and I think that's their right to do it.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: COVID-19 vaccines were pushed based on preventing transmission, but later evidence showed they may decrease severe disease in at-risk people without preventing infection or transmission.
pearls.verbatim: it was pushed. That was the number one push. But then we said, well, it doesn't really... It doesn't prevent infection nor does it prevent transmission. It may decrease the incidence of severe disease in at risk people.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Ivermectin is a very safe, cheap, generic medication used widely for parasites, but its off-label use for COVID-19 remains unproven; patients may request it based on anecdotal reports.
pearls.verbatim: When we lived in Africa, we give it to everybody all the time. I mean, it's it's a very common, very safe, very cheap, very generic medicine.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Methamphetamine is now involved in more overdose/poisoning deaths than opioids in Oklahoma, reflecting the fourth wave of the opioid epidemic (psychostimulant-opioid mixtures).
pearls.verbatim: Now they're calling the fourth wave kind of a psychostimulant with opioid mixture. And this is particularly true for Oklahoma. So you'll see that methamphetamine now is actually involved in more of a overdose slash poisoning deaths than opioids now in the state of Oklahoma.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: The X-waiver for buprenorphine has been eliminated; only a DEA license is needed to prescribe it for opioid use disorder.
pearls.verbatim: Now we've gotten rid of the ex waiver for buprenorphine, which is great. Don't need our ex waiver. You just need a VA license to prescribe buprenorphine for addiction.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Only 20-30% of individuals with opioid use disorder remain abstinent at 12 months without medication treatment; white-knuckling alone does not work.
pearls.verbatim: Without treatment, only twenty to thirty percent of people are sober at twelve months out. Okay. So that means they quit cold therapy. They... Even if they did therapy or counseling without medication support, you're only getting a twenty to thirty percent success rate.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Mortality ratio for opioid use disorder drops from 6-fold to below 2-fold when patients have access to medication-assisted treatment—withholding it is unethical.
pearls.verbatim: Those who struggle with opioid use disorder had a six time fold risk of mortality. ... When they have access to medication assisted treatment, their mortality ratio goes down below two. So this is the reason why medication assisted treatment is the gold standard for opioid use disorder. And if you're not offering it, it is unethical.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Buprenorphine is a partial agonist that caps mu-opioid receptor activation, making it very hard to overdose on alone—overdose risk increases only when mixed with other substances.
pearls.verbatim: Partial agonist, buprenorphine. Buprenorphine, no matter when you get to a high dose, it caps the the activity of that receptor. K? So no matter how much you get after that, receptor's not... There's nothing where you can hit on that receptor. This is one reason why it's really hard to overdose on buprenorphine because you're not you're not getting the receptor enough to get that respiratory depression.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: When buprenorphine occupies mu-opioid receptors, heroin cannot displace it due to buprenorphine's high binding affinity, providing overdose protection and blocking euphoria.
pearls.verbatim: Buprenorphine binds the receptors with a really high affinity, so very tightly. So heroin can't knock them out. So if your receptors are full of buprenorphine and you do some heroin, you don't even feel it.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone) contains naloxone as an anti-injection deterrent; if taken sublingually as directed, the naloxone is inert, but if injected it becomes bioavailable and can cause withdrawal.
pearls.verbatim: Naloxone is not very bio... Bioavailable under the tongue. So the idea is that it's not really... It's like inert. Right? It's not really helping. But it is bioavailable if you inject it. So it's an anti injection agent.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Sublocade (monthly buprenorphine injection) can be used as a tapering agent because it self-tapers over months, avoiding the withdrawal and cravings seen with tablet tapers.
pearls.verbatim: it's been good at as a tapering agent as well because with the tabs, you know, you can only get it so small. And so people still have some withdrawal cravings even if I'm using, like, the tabs of the films. With this, it just self self tapered over months.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: When tapering buprenorphine, the risk of return to use increases; clinicians should only taper if the patient is motivated and aware of this risk.
pearls.verbatim: What the research says is that when you start tapering, return to use goes up. So as we taper, your risk of returning use is gonna go up.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: For patients on Suboxone who experience headaches or nausea, have them rinse their mouth after the film dissolves to reduce swallowed naloxone; if symptoms persist, switch to the mono product (Subutex).
pearls.verbatim: first, I have them rinse their mouth out after the suboxone. So so you're not supposed see, like, ten minutes before and after. Make sure it's completely resolved, dissolved, and then rinse your mouth out because sometimes they're swallowing it and ends up sitting their stomach They're absorbing some of the naloxone through the GI system.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Extended-release naltrexone (Vivitrol) requires 7-10 days of opioid abstinence before initiation; otherwise, it will precipitate severe withdrawal.
pearls.verbatim: You have to be opioid free for seven to ten days before you can get it. That's the really hard part here is getting opioids for seven to ten days.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: In the COMBINE study, naltrexone plus CBT and medical management improved outcomes; acamprosate did not add benefit over medical management alone.
pearls.verbatim: Naltrexone and CBT added to medical management improved outcomes over placebo medical management alone. And acamprosate in this study didn't really add benefit to naltrexone or CBT and was not more effective than medical management alone.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Brixadi (new buprenorphine injection) can be given weekly or monthly; a patient can get the injection immediately after tolerating a single 4 mg sublingual dose with a 7-day window.
pearls.verbatim: So they shall just recommend seven day window.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Patients with substance use disorder often have delayed brain development; expecting full high-level recovery on day one without medication assistance is unrealistic and not how other chronic diseases are treated.
pearls.verbatim: even older people who have substance use disorder, their brain development got delayed. So you're asking them to have high level functioning recovery on day one without any assistance. I don't know about you, but just that's not how we do anything else in health care, and we need to train these patients the same way.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Sexual side effects (anorgasmia) from SSRIs typically occur at higher doses; inform patients that there are options to manage or switch.
pearls.verbatim: Sexual side effects, anorgasmia being the most common. And I say, hey. That usually doesn't happen till we really push the dose up high. And if it does, I have ways to maybe counteract that, or we can switch.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Black box warning for SSRIs in adolescents: increased suicidal ideation, not behavior; discuss with patients.
pearls.verbatim: There is a black box warning for psychiatric issues, especially in adolescence. Right? So the black box warning is increased suicidality. It doesn't appear to actually increase suicidal behavior, just suicidal thoughts.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Do not prescribe an SSRI and SNRI together due to risk of serotonin syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: SSRIs and SNRI should never be prescribed at the same time for another event unless your prostate brain... Yeah. This would be... Don't ever... I don't ever run me in the ED, and I see that you so on venlafaxine and sertraline. Like, no. Don't do it.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Bupropion can counteract sexual side effects from SSRIs; consider adding it if a patient is responding well but has sexual dysfunction.
pearls.verbatim: bupropion tends to counteract sexual side effects. So if someone's really, like, responding to this or either having sexual side effects, think about adding bupropion.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression
