pearls.text: Consider treating subclinical hypothyroidism (TSH high-normal) in depression; targeting TSH closer to 1 may improve response.
pearls.verbatim: One study in adolescence said if they get if they titrated TSH to get closer to one, they had a much better response in depression. And so, you know, we think, oh, TSH is four and a half. You know? It's within normal limits. Well, if someone is, like, kinda up... Getting to the upper level of normal, but they're depressed, you might wanna consider treating depression.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: For first-episode depression, treat for 6-12 months after remission; recurrence rate is 44% within 2 years.
pearls.verbatim: first episode, six months to one year is appropriate if we're in some remissions, and you can kind of taper off. The recurrence rate after a first depressive episode in two years is forty four percent, at least forty percent recurrence within two years.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: ECT is the most effective treatment for depression; consider after 3-4 failed trials or sooner for psychotic or severe depression.
pearls.verbatim: ECT can be considered after they're treatment resistant. K? It is the most effective treatment we still have for depression.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Avoid combining SSRIs and SNRIs; they are in the same class and should not be used together.
pearls.verbatim: I do SSRIs and SNRIs in the same class, and you will never put through the same class.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: For patients on citalopram or escitalopram, do not exceed FDA dosing to avoid QTc prolongation; routine outpatient EKGs are not necessary.
pearls.verbatim: I'm not going above FDA dosing on citalopramide or Lexapro. Just not gonna do it. Now if they do have some cardiac history and I am worried about that, I might just pull in the cardiologist anyway to see why. But, generally, I'm not doing that a ton.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Bupropion is contraindicated in patients with a history of seizures or active alcohol withdrawal due to lowered seizure threshold.
pearls.verbatim: Only if they have a history of no seizures. So even though alcohol withdrawal could potentially increase their risk for seizures, if they haven't had any active and you're kinda treating them, I would tell them, hey. This medication potentially could throw your seizure threshold.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Use propranolol or hydroxyzine as bridging therapy to provide relief while an antidepressant takes effect.
pearls.verbatim: I try to use propranolol or hydroxyzine to give them some degree of relief while the antidepressant can work.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Benzodiazepines worsen anxiety long-term and should never be used as a long-term treatment for anxiety.
pearls.verbatim: It makes anxiety worse long term. So it's never indicative for anxiety long term. It's always short term.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Check for concurrent opioid use in elderly patients on benzodiazepines; combination is a never event.
pearls.verbatim: I wanna make sure they're not on an opioid. Right? Because if they're on an opioid, that's just a... Could be a very never event.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: For anxiety in panic disorder, use hydroxyzine, buspirone, or propranolol as alternatives to benzodiazepines.
pearls.verbatim: I use hydroxyzine, bispar, propranolol.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Bupropion is contraindicated in active bulimia due to seizure risk.
pearls.verbatim: bupropion would be contraindicated in that scenario. There's some controversy of, like, does bupropion actually lower seizure threshold? But still, at this point, it's considered a contraindication.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Consider vilazodone or vortioxetine for patients who experience sexual side effects from SSRIs.
pearls.verbatim: vilazodone and vilazodone have a little less sexual side effects too
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Take SSRIs in the morning to reduce sexual side effects.
pearls.verbatim: if you can try to take it in the morning sometimes, that can help avoid it.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: For SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction, add cyproheptadine or sildenafil.
pearls.verbatim: have tried cyproheptadine, serotonin antagonist. Like, for some reason, it doesn't completely counteract the depressive side effects, but helps with the sexual side effects.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Gabapentin is useful for lingering anxiety in patients recovering from alcohol use disorder.
pearls.verbatim: my patients that are recovering from alcohol, it's kind of that lingering anxiety that comes with the alcohol. So I like gabapentin a lot.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Avoid benzodiazepines in patients with active alcohol use due to risk of respiratory depression.
pearls.verbatim: So you don't wanna be in a situation where she's giving her a benzo, and you know she adopts all. Right? And if something happens there, you're at risk too.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: 25-40% of occlusive MIs are missed by strict STEMI criteria; any degree of ST elevation in inferior leads with aVL depression may indicate occlusion.
pearls.verbatim: twenty five to thirty percent of in STEMI patients are found to have total occlusion on delayed cardiac catheterization
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Hyperacute T waves are tall, symmetric, and disproportionate to QRS amplitude, often from local potassium release by infarcted myocytes; they are a subtle sign of occlusion.
pearls.verbatim: infarcted infarcted cardiac myocytes are giving off local potassium and just locally making the T waves bigger.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Anterior ST depression in V1–V4 is a posterior MI until proven otherwise; obtain posterior leads V7–V9.
pearls.verbatim: if you see anteriorly in this anterior septal v one through v four, if you see anteriorly that they are having ST depression, that's that's a posterior MI until proven otherwise
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Brilinta (ticagrelor) offers 6–10% lower reocclusion rate compared to Plavix after stenting; switch after first month for cost.
pearls.verbatim: Brilinta has a better mortality rate if they're gonna get a stent. Or I I don't think it's mortality. I think it's reocclusion morbidity. It's something like six to ten percent less reocclusion.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Give thrombolytics if PCI cannot be performed within 90 minutes of STEMI identification; this is the legal standard.
pearls.verbatim: if from the time the STEMI was identified, whether EMS or when they walked in the door, if from the time the STEMI was identified to ninety minutes later, it's not gonna be possible to get them a stent, whether in your hospital or another one. They get thrombolytics.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Obtain serial EKGs at 0, 15, and 30 minutes for any patient with suspected occlusive MI.
pearls.verbatim: You really should be getting one at time zero, one... Fifteen minutes, one at thirty minutes.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Ventricular paced rhythms use the same Sgarbossa criteria as left bundle branch block for detecting ischemia.
pearls.verbatim: a ventricular paced rhythm looks the exact same as a left bundle, and it applies perfectly in a paced rhythm too. The exact same criteria.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Nitroglycerin is unlikely to relieve pain in occlusive STEMI and may drop blood pressure, worsening ischemia and killing more myocytes; avoid it in suspected STEMI.
pearls.verbatim: nitroglycerin, all you're likely to do when you give nitro to someone who you know is having an occlusive MI is drop their blood pressure. Highly unlikely you're going to get them pain free if they have big tombstone STEMI. Highly unlikely you're going to get them pain free. And there's at least a decent chance... if you drop their pressure from one forty to one ten by giving them a dose of nitro, going to kill more myocytes.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Do not rely on atypical chest pain features to rule out ACS if the patient looks ill; patients in pain often cannot describe symptoms accurately.
pearls.verbatim: we overuse and overdepend on atypical chest pain given the number of of people that have atypical symptoms. If someone is suffering, they are not in the right mind to give you a clear answer on the exact nature of their pain. People use the word sharp to mean use the word sharp to mean it it it hurts bad. And so I would not bank on on atypical symptoms if the patient looks bad.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: A recent negative stress test does not rule out plaque rupture; it only indicates no ischemia at that moment and should not be used as a warranty.
pearls.verbatim: the Journal of the American College of Cardiology gave people a one year warranty on their heart if they've had a recent negative stress test. But we have plenty of anecdotal experience and literature that that was probably an inappropriate guideline. All it does is tell you you didn't have ischemia in that moment.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Repeat the EKG early and often; if the patient looks bad, call cardiology because you cannot know everything.
pearls.verbatim: Repeat the EKG early and often. If the patient looks bad in front of you, call cardiology because we can't know everything.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Suspect anaphylaxis primarily based on history; look for a rash or swollen lips if the patient is obtunded.
pearls.verbatim: If you suspect anaphylaxis just based on history. Almost exclusively on history.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Vasopressors can be given through an IO; if you need to start them, go straight through the deltoid (humeral site).
pearls.verbatim: If you need to start vasopressors, like, get them get them going. Just go straight through the deltoid.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Start vasopressors early if the patient does not respond to fluids; it is better to normalize blood pressure and then titrate off.
pearls.verbatim: Start vasopressors. You so much rather get their blood pressure normal and then titrate off the vasopressors.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Set a MAP goal of 65 mmHg to give a cushion, but a MAP of 60 is the minimum needed to perfuse critical organs.
pearls.verbatim: we set a MAP of 65 as the goal to give just a little cushion.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: If MAP is 50 and you delay vasopressors while giving fluids, two hours later the patient may have AKI from underperfused kidneys. Start vasopressors early rather than fiddling with slow IV fluids.
pearls.verbatim: if their map is 50 and you're like, well, let's see where we're at after this first bolus. I'm like, well, let's see where we're at for the second bolus. And suddenly two hours have gone by, and then tomorrow they have an AKI, and you're like, what happened? They're like, well, we we didn't perfuse their kidneys.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Warm shock means peripheral vasodilation (alpha receptors not working); the patient feels warm to the touch. Cold shock means vasoconstriction (e.g., from poor cardiac output); the patient feels cold and clammy.
pearls.verbatim: If your alpha receptors are not working, are your blood vessels going to be vasoconstricted or vasodilated? Vasodilated. And if your blood vessels are vasodilated, are you going to feel warm or cold on your skin? Warm.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Phenylephrine (Neo-Synephrine) is a pure alpha agonist. It is used for MAP pushes in neurogenic shock or in patients with strong hearts, but not in cardiogenic shock because it adds afterload without inotropy.
pearls.verbatim: The pure alpha, no beta at all, also goes by Neo-Synephrine, is not used a lot. ... most of the time, neo is used in someone who has a good heart, strong heart, not in any degree of cardiogenic shock.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Code-dose epinephrine is 1 mg (1000 mcg) IV push, which is roughly 1000 times the infusion rate of 1 mcg/min. This massive dose can cause shock-resistant V-fib, especially if given before defibrillation.
pearls.verbatim: if you maxed out epi, forty micrograms over sixty seconds, not even forty micrograms at once, You max that at the forty micrograms every So they're getting roughly, like, one point five mic something. So you're giving almost a thousand times that in, like, a one second push in a code.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: In refractory V-fib after multiple epinephrine doses, consider giving esmolol (a beta blocker) and then shocking, rather than more epinephrine.
pearls.verbatim: I got someone back by giving esmolol, a beta blocker, when they were in refractory ventricular fibrillation (V-fib). The EMS truck had given six or eight of epi and couldn't couldn't get them back with the shocks. So I gave a bolus of esmolol and then shocked them.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: A milligram of epinephrine is the same whether diluted in 1 mL or 10 mL; concentration does not change the total dose. The anaphylaxis vial (1 mg in 1 mL) can be used IV in a code because you are pushing the same 1 mg dose.
pearls.verbatim: If you put a milligram of epinephrine in a ten ml syringe or a milligram of epinephrine in a one ml syringe, which one has more epinephrine? Doesn't Same. Matter. You're about to... A milligram is a milligram is a milligram, whether it's been diluted and an extra nine ccs of saline or not.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Educate patients with life-threatening allergies to use their EpiPen immediately at the first sign of airway compromise—they are the only ones who can save themselves.
pearls.verbatim: the second you feel your throat closing, the second you realize your tongue is huge or you might not be able to breathe, call 911 and give yourself your epinephrine. You are the only person that can save yourself.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Dose norepinephrine by the MAP deficit: start at 20 mcg/min if MAP is 45, 10 mcg/min if MAP is 55.
pearls.verbatim: I start with however many points I need to make up on their map. So if their map is 45, like, we got a lot of distance to cover, then just start them at 20. That make sense? If their map is 55, just start them at ten.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: The concept of 'renal-dose dopamine' to vasodilate renal vasculature has been shown to be ineffective since the early 2000s; do not use it.
pearls.verbatim: it's been demonstrated in... Probably since the two thousands that that was all theoretical and didn't actually work.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: Milrinone is a good inotrope option for cardiogenic shock when the patient has atrial fibrillation or is prone to tachycardia, but its long half-life makes rapid titration difficult.
pearls.verbatim: if you wanna give an inotrope but they're, like, already A fib, RBR, or prone to tachypnea, milrinone is a really good option.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on Approach to Undifferentiated Shock

pearls.text: For seizure patients on missed meds (Kepprapenia), give Keppra and discharge; for breakthrough seizures on medication or multiple seizures in days, admit or call neurologist.
pearls.verbatim: if it's just keppra penia that they seized from, then give them Keppra and go send them home. Like, if if you don't if you don't take your meds, you cease. Like, that's that's an easy one.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: For TIA, use ABCD2 score to risk-stratify; high score warrants admission or starting aspirin and statin if patient refuses.
pearls.verbatim: if their ABCD2 score is high and a TIA, like, as soon as it's completely resolved, you're encouraging them to stay. And if they won't stay for whatever reason, you're probably starting them on aspirin and or antilipidemic
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: For chest pain, stable angina can go home; unstable angina (new, worse, or at rest) requires admission. Use HEART score if uncertain.
pearls.verbatim: if this is stable angina for them, then they can go. And if you're try... If you don't know if it's stable angina or unstable angina, you do a heart score and figure out their risk factors and say, like, well, listen. I don't know what happened.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Use open evidence by copying your HPI and asking 'what are the three emergencies I need to rule out' to ensure no critical diagnosis is missed.
pearls.verbatim: cheat code in 2026 is that you can take your HPI, copy paste it into open evidence and say, what are the three emergencies I need to make sure I've ruled out?
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Perform Carnett's test for abdominal pain: have patient flex abs; if pain worsens with flexion, it suggests abdominal wall pathology rather than visceral origin.
pearls.verbatim: It's where you flex, have them flex their abs. If that makes their abdominal pain worse, it's suggestive of an abdominal wall pathology.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: For mystery back pain, distinguish piriformis syndrome (lateral buttock pain, responds to stretching) from sacroiliitis (pain directly over SI joint, treat with NSAIDs).
pearls.verbatim: If you're more convincing, if it's more lateral, it's probably more piriformis. If it's, like, right on the SI joint, you probably get more sacroiliitis.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Vertical nystagmus (up or down beating) is never normal in vertigo and indicates central (brain stem) pathology.
pearls.verbatim: any degree of vertical nystagmus. They look up or look down, and their eyes are beating up or down. That's that's a central vertigo brain stem issue.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: If you cannot complete an urgent stroke workup in clinic within an appropriate timeline (e.g., over a holiday weekend), send the patient to the emergency department.
pearls.verbatim: if we can't intersect downward trajectory and get that workup done in an appropriate timeline, send them in.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: A negative Dix-Hallpike maneuver does not rule out BPPV because it only tests one of three semicircular canals.
pearls.verbatim: just because they have a negative Dix-Hallpike does not rule out BPPV.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Start pressors before you know the cause of hypotension to prevent organ injury; Levophed is the right choice when the etiology is unclear.
pearls.verbatim: I start pressors all the time before I know why I'm starting pressors because I don't want their organs to die.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Create a personal cheat sheet for emergency medications (sedation, RSI, status epilepticus, hypoglycemia) and keep it in your pocket.
pearls.verbatim: It was literally just a folded piece of paper that lived in my pocket every day for two years that I would have my sedation drugs, my status epilepticus drugs, my hypoglycemia agents, my RSI meds.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Pressors can be infused through a peripheral IV safely for 24 hours; central lines are not an emergency.
pearls.verbatim: Pressors can run through a peripheral line for twenty four hours.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: When learning ultrasound-guided central lines, expect to miss the first 10 times – after that, you will likely succeed.
pearls.verbatim: Once you've missed it 10 times in a row, you probably won't miss it again after that.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Sublingual nitro 0.4 mg q5min equals 80 mcg/min average, so a nitro drip for flash pulmonary edema should start above that to be more effective.
pearls.verbatim: the sublingual nitro, which is four hundred given every five minutes, you divide that out, that average is eighty mics a minute.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: For flash pulmonary edema with hypertension, start BiPAP and a nitro drip at 200-400 mcg/min – the patient will improve in 8 minutes.
pearls.verbatim: If you start BiPAP and a nitro drip, they'll be better in eight minutes, and you'll look like a genius. But the nitro drip starts at about 200, maybe 300, maybe 400.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Nitroglycerin has a 90-second half-life, so you can safely start high-dose; if pressure drops, just cut the drip.
pearls.verbatim: the half life of nitro is, like, ninety seconds. If they... If it drops their pressure, we'll cut it. But start them on high dose nitro.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ER Q&A 9/23/26

pearls.text: Oral vancomycin has no systemic absorption; use it only for C. difficile colitis, not for skin or soft tissue infections.
pearls.verbatim: oral vancomycin. Would I use that for a skin infection? No. No GI absorption of oral vancomycin
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Antibiotics

pearls.text: Susceptibility to cefazolin (a first-generation cephalosporin) means you can use oral cephalexin (Keflex) because they are in the same class.
pearls.verbatim: if it's susceptible to cefazolin... Well, cefazolin's an IV drug. If I wanna use a PO first generation cephalosporin, like Keflex? Would I use that? Yeah. Even though they didn't test Keflex, is in the same class. I can use it.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Antibiotics

pearls.text: When a culture shows an unexpected organism like Enterobacter, consult a reference (e.g., Sanford Guide) before susceptibilities return to avoid continuing a wrong empiric antibiotic.
pearls.verbatim: I use the sandbird guide, and it's got this beautiful tape
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Antibiotics

pearls.text: Enterococcus faecalis is universally resistant to cephalosporins; never use a cephalosporin for enterococcal infections even if the susceptibility report appears to show susceptibility.
pearls.verbatim: enterococcus does not have any susceptibility to cephalosporins across the board
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Antibiotics

pearls.text: Automatically consult ID for endocarditis and osteomyelitis as they require prolonged antibiotic courses and specialist management.
pearls.verbatim: infectious endocarditis, osteomyelitis, those are definitely two clinical scenarios where we're almost always, I would say, always consulting infectious disease
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Antibiotics

pearls.text: When a patient with recurrent infections keeps returning despite correct antibiotics per the susceptibility report, stop and question whether the MIC data is reliable or if resistance has emerged.
pearls.verbatim: if something's just not going way it should be going, stop and ask yourself. Yep. You know, maybe I should call an IV consult and see what I need to do differently.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Antibiotics

pearls.text: Uncontrolled diabetes (hyperglycemia) is dangerous and may warrant delivery at 37-38 weeks per MFM recommendation.
pearls.verbatim: if that diabetes is out of control. That hyperglycemia can be dangerous. And so based on their control, a little bit vague, but MFM will often tell us thirty eight weeks, thirty seven weeks, depending on their condition.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Induction of Labor 4/9/26

pearls.text: Oral misoprostol 25 mcg is a weak induction agent; consider combination methods.
pearls.verbatim: You can also use twenty five of oral. It's kinda weak sauce.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Induction of Labor 4/9/26

pearls.text: When performing knee injections, inject a couple centimeters above the patella with the knee near full extension to access the joint capsule and avoid ligaments.
pearls.verbatim: you can inject a couple centimeters above the patella, and you're still in the joint capsule. So that's why a lot of injection... In fact, we have that knee just about in... With a slight flexion, but most... Almost straight 180 degrees extension that pushes this fluid up into here. You have a space to inject, and you're not near any ligaments.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Knee Injuries

pearls.text: The quadriceps active test uses the patient's own quadriceps to reduce a posteriorly sagging tibia; if the tibia moves forward, it confirms PCL injury.
pearls.verbatim: This is called the quadriceps active test activation test. Okay? Oh, and it pulls it up. It's back in a second. Look for the tibial sac sign.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Knee Injuries

pearls.text: The frog-leg maneuver for LCL involves flexing the knee and applying varus stress; you can palpate the LCL as a bowstring across the lateral joint.
pearls.verbatim: So that position allows you... If pushing on the knee, creates a varus stress. And if the LCL is compromised or torn, the lateral compartment will gap. And so that's what the frog leg does.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Knee Injuries

pearls.text: Check urine albumin-creatinine ratio (ACR) in all CKD patients with diabetes to assess risk of progression.
pearls.verbatim: all the guideline recommendations for CKD, especially those with diabetes, are gonna have you be checking your ACR, basically, your urine albumin creatinine ratio so that you can see the risk of progression
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Outpatient Management of Kidney Disease

pearls.text: Renally dose all medications for CKD patients to avoid toxicity.
pearls.verbatim: We are gonna renally dose our medications.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Outpatient Management of Kidney Disease

pearls.text: Hold ACE/ARB if serum potassium exceeds 5.5 mEq/L.
pearls.verbatim: You can want to hold off if your potassium's over 5.5.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Outpatient Management of Kidney Disease

pearls.text: If GFR drops by more than 30% after starting an ACE/ARB, consider changing or stopping the medication.
pearls.verbatim: If your GFR drops by more than 30% when you start that ACE or ARB, you you would wanna consider changing it, stopping it.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Outpatient Management of Kidney Disease

pearls.text: Consider finerenone (nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist) for stage 3-4 CKD to reduce GFR decline and ESRD risk.
pearls.verbatim: This is a selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. This is a newer agent, but it does have benefits for reducing the risk of sustained GFR decline. This is a big game changer for stage three, stage four CKD patients because it is halting the progression.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Outpatient Management of Kidney Disease

pearls.text: In CKD with diabetes, start an SGLT2 inhibitor and metformin.
pearls.verbatim: Get them on a SGLT2. Metformin is also indicated and recommended for these patients.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Outpatient Management of Kidney Disease

pearls.text: The quad screen (AFP tetra) screens for neural tube defects, which cell-free DNA does not; this is a key difference when choosing a screening test.
pearls.verbatim: The only difference is quad screen would would also give you the risk of neuro tube defects as well, which genetic testing doesn't.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: The quad screen has a sensitivity of only 75% for trisomy 21 in women under 35 and 80% in those over 35; these numbers are substantially lower than cell-free DNA.
pearls.verbatim: The sensitivity for those 35 was not great. 75% over 35, still not great. Only eighty percent.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: When counseling a patient with a thickened nuchal fold on anatomy scan, use a calm, scripted approach: explain the finding, its association with trisomy 21, and the plan for specialist referral.
pearls.verbatim: Your anatomy scan showed a thickened nuchal fold. This can be associated with tristamine twenty one, and I'm gonna refer you to our specialist to evaluate that further.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: If a finding like pyelectasis is confirmed resolved by MFM, do not carry it forward in the chart; it creates unnecessary confusion and stress for the patient later in pregnancy.
pearls.verbatim: If MFM says there's no problem with this, we should just not carry that forward because it's creating confusion.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: The fetal components of cell-free DNA are derived from placental trophoblasts released from cells undergoing programmed cell death.
pearls.verbatim: The fetal components of the cell free DNA is derived from placental trophoblasts that are released into the maternal circulations from cells undergoing programmed cell death.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: If a cell-free DNA result shows a single monosomy or more than one aneuploidy, consider occult maternal malignancy as a possible source.
pearls.verbatim: If a single a single monosomy or more than one aneuploidy is detected in cell free DNA result, the incidence of malignancy is increased.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: In the setting of a screen-negative result, discuss residual risk—the chance that an abnormality may still be present.
pearls.verbatim: In the setting of a screen negative or low risk test result, discussion should include the concept of residual risk, which is defined as the chance that an abnormality may still be present even if the test result is screen negative.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: For a positive test, counsel on positive predictive value and options for additional testing to clarify risk.
pearls.verbatim: In the case of a result indicating decreased risk, counseling should provide information regarding the likelihood the fetus has a particular condition, I. E, the positive predictive value and the options for additional testing if desired to further clarify this risk.
pearls.speaker: Ganzer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer on Prenatal Screening for Chromosomal Abnormalities of the Fetus 9/4/25

pearls.text: For GDM A2, classification includes use of insulin or oral agents—both are A2. If no medication is needed, it is GDM A1.
pearls.verbatim: So GDM a one versus someone with gestational diabetes who's not on medication, diet control, a two. But it's insulin or oral... It's still a two.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: Routine GDM screening is at 24-28 weeks; for high-risk patients (BMI >25, first-degree relative with diabetes), screen earlier at 16-20 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: Six to twenty eight. Louder? Six to twenty eight weeks ... twenty four to twenty eight is the normal recommended general screening. ... early screening ... probably 16 to 20 is more ideal.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: Do not use A1c for GDM screening in pregnancy—it is artificially low due to anemia and RBC turnover, and it does not reflect the dynamic glucose changes.
pearls.verbatim: a one c is artificially low in any context in which there's a higher turnover of RBCs. ... why we don't use A1c in pregnancy because we have a dynamic process happening.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: After delivery, stop all insulin for true GDM patients because the placental source of insulin resistance is gone; check postpartum glucose to rule out overt diabetes.
pearls.verbatim: why after delivery, I can just stop all their insulin and say, it's okay. ... That placenta is gone. Their their glucose intolerance just, like, vanishes if it's true GDM.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: Glucosuria alone is not diagnostic of GDM; it can reflect diet or pregnancy physiology. If consistent 3+ glucose is seen after a normal GTT, counsel on diet, but don't retest automatically.
pearls.verbatim: glucosuria is weird because how often have you seen positive glucose on your UA and they have a normal GTT? ... I honestly don't get too worried about glucosuria if I have normal, like, GTTs.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: One-step screening for GDM diagnoses twice as many patients and doubles pharmacotherapy use without improving maternal or neonatal outcomes.
pearls.verbatim: One step approach diagnosed twice as many patients with GBM. K? And it resulted in twice as many patients receiving antihyperglycemic pharmacotherapy without a clear benefit in outcome.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: If diet-controlled GDM fails after two weeks, initiate pharmacotherapy; further delay is unlikely to achieve control.
pearls.verbatim: I usually give them two weeks tempting diet. I I counsel them the first week. The second week is like, you know, okay. We gotta do better. Here we go. We're starting on medication. Sometimes that's enough to, like, push them into getting a better diet. But by week two, if they're not controlled by diet, you're you're probably not gonna get them diet. So second week into this uncontrolled in the direction of medications.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: With co-management, check out directly via phone to your co-managing faculty after the visit and before the patient leaves.
pearls.verbatim: with co management, you are checking out directly via phone to your co managing faculty after the visit before the patient leaves.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: Insulin is first-line pharmacotherapy for GDM because it is easier to titrate as glucose intolerance worsens in pregnancy.
pearls.verbatim: first line, we'll start with insulin. Remember that curve with the slope? Think of how many increments of metformin doses you have available to you. Many. You're like, I'm done. Right? That's why insulin is a lot more reliable and useful.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: If MFM is not performing antepartum testing for A2 GDM, the obstetrics team must ensure it is done.
pearls.verbatim: if MFM's not doing it, we're doing it. Somebody's gotta be doing it.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: In labor, use rotating fluids (D5LR when glucose <100, LR when >100) to target maternal glucose <110 mg/dL and avoid neonatal hypoglycemia.
pearls.verbatim: The idea of rotating fluids is... Actually, most laboring women do better with D5LR, but we turn that D5 off when their sugar is above a 100. So the rotating fluids is because sometimes the TDM patients become a little bit hyperglycemic, and we need to switch to regular LR. K? But when they're under a 100, we don't want them to have that sugar that's... That's needed for labor available.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Ganzer Overviews Gestational Diabetes

pearls.text: The clinician's history is the gold standard for syphilis diagnosis; challenge lab results that don't fit.
pearls.verbatim: You are the gold standard with your clinical history, and you have that good clinical history to match that with the data that we give you. And when that data doesn't match, if it's syphilis, call me and challenge it.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Untreated pregnant women pass syphilis to the fetus in 80% of cases; use RPR on the newborn, not treponemal antibody.
pearls.verbatim: Untreated pregnant women, they will pass that infection onto eighty percent of the cases. So you've got to get in mind is that the gold standard for you is in terms of dealing with that newborn is gonna be an RPR.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: The chancre is painless and heals in 2-6 weeks; it may be absent in some patients, so don't discount syphilis based on exam alone.
pearls.verbatim: That lesion that occurs is a painless lesion. It is... It depends about it where it's at, but it's still a painless lesion, and it does not develop in every case.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: The serofast phenomenon: treated patients may have persistent low titers (1:1-1:4) that do not clear with further treatment.
pearls.verbatim: There's a situation called a seropast on these patients who have syphilis. You treat them, and those titers will come down to a one to one, one to two, maybe even a one to four, and they won't go any lower no matter how many times you treat them.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: 25% of late-stage syphilis patients lose RPR reactivity; a negative RPR does not rule out active infection in this group.
pearls.verbatim: Twenty five percent of those patients who are in late stage disease and you're depending on an RPR, not gonna happen because twenty five percent of those patients will lose their RPR in late stage disease.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: In the reverse algorithm, if treponemal antibody is reactive but RPR is nonreactive and index is less than 9, do a second treponemal test to rule out false positive.
pearls.verbatim: If the RPR is nonreactive is that what we're gonna do, if this index up here less than nine, we're gonna do another treponemal antibody of a diamond ear away here. Another treponemal antibody to determine this is a true positive.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Once a patient is known treponemal antibody positive, never order another treponemal antibody test; use RPR to follow treatment response.
pearls.verbatim: Don't ever order another treponemal antibody. Don't even waste your money.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: After treatment, order a nontreponemal antibody (RPR) and monitor the decline in titer to assess response.
pearls.verbatim: You order a nontreponemal antibody, and that's an RPR, and you're gonna watch that decrease.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: If you suspect a false-negative syphilis test, wait 2-4 weeks and retest.
pearls.verbatim: you wait two, three, four weeks and retest them.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: In advanced syphilis, 25% of patients are RPR negative, so a negative RPR does not rule out disease.
pearls.verbatim: remembering that twenty five percent of the patients with advanced disease will be negative for RPR.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Order a syphilis antibody screen rather than RPR for initial screening; the lab will reflex to confirmatory testing.
pearls.verbatim: Order syphilis antibody and leave the driving test.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Always read the footnote on syphilis results; the lab adds specific notes about false positives.
pearls.verbatim: Always read your footnote on syphilis. Always read your footnote because we... I will write some things on there that will be specific.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: In tertiary syphilis, 25% of patients have no RPR reactivity; do not be fooled by a negative RPR.
pearls.verbatim: in tertiary, you're gonna see twenty five percent of those patients who do not have any RPRs. Don't be fooled.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: If treponemal antibody is nonreactive after a reactive screen, it was a false positive.
pearls.verbatim: if the... Sheppenemal antibody is nonreactive, then in fact, it was a false positive.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Prozone phenomenon: if antibody excess prevents agglutination, labs must titer RPR out to at least 1:2048 to avoid false negatives.
pearls.verbatim: prozone... if all of the sites are covered with an antibody, there's no way for the antibody to cross link from one antigen to another to cause the agglutination. And a lot of labs will only do the three twenty, maybe six forty. We go to 2,048.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: In pregnant women, do not forget to perform treponemal testing (TPPA) for syphilis.
pearls.verbatim: remember the syphilis, the treponemal PUPA on pregnant women. Don't you dare forget that
pearls.speaker: Gerald C Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Once a patient has been treated and is treponemal antibody positive, never order another treponemal antibody test; use only RPR to monitor for reinfection.
pearls.verbatim: Don't ever order another treponemal antibody. Don't even waste your money.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C. Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C. Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Serofast is defined as RPR titer that decreases to 1:2 and remains stable on repeat testing; no further treatment is needed.
pearls.verbatim: And then you see it get down to one to two. You're gonna be tempted two or three months or a few weeks to do another nontreponemal. And it's still one to two. That is what? Stay at one to two. What is that? SeroFast.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C. Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C. Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Order syphilis antibody screen; the lab will reflex to RPR and TPPA if needed. Do not order a treponemal antibody separately.
pearls.verbatim: Order syphilis antibody and leave the driving test.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C. Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C. Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Always read the footnote on syphilis lab reports; it may contain specific information about false-positive or inconclusive results.
pearls.verbatim: Always read your footnote on syphilis. Always read your footnote because we... I will write some things on there that will be specific.
pearls.speaker: Gerald C. Miller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Gerald C. Miller on Syphilis Testing Tools and Interpretation of Results

pearls.text: Distinguish physician-assisted death (medical aid in dying) from hospice care that provides pain relief at the end of life.
pearls.verbatim: The physician causing the death of a patient. Correct. And we've gotta distinguish that from a physician helping in hospice care providing pain.
pearls.speaker: Glaser
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Glaser on Medical Advocacy 6/11/26

pearls.text: Start advocacy efforts with prayer, seeking wise counsel, and listening.
pearls.verbatim: First steps is pray. Seek and listen. Wise counsel.
pearls.speaker: Glaser
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Glaser on Medical Advocacy 6/11/26

pearls.text: If a patient fails escitalopram, do not switch to citalopram (isomer) as they are chemically similar.
pearls.verbatim: if you have one and someone fails that one, it's a good chance that they're probably not going to well on citalopram if you've already tried escitalopram or vice versa.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: For elderly patients, do not exceed escitalopram 10 mg or citalopram 20 mg.
pearls.verbatim: With elderly, a lot of times, you try not to go above ten milligrams for escitalopram and twenty milligrams for citalopram.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: For PMDD, consider intermittent fluoxetine: take two days before period until period ends.
pearls.verbatim: I had a patient who only took fluoxetine, like, two days before starting her period until her period was done.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Start SSRIs at a quarter dose for 1-2 weeks to improve GI tolerability before moving to half dose.
pearls.verbatim: I'll put them on, like, the half dose of something, but have them cut it in half for the quarter dose and do that for, like, a week or two and then have them start taking the the the half dose.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Use cross-titration with fluoxetine (long half-life) to help discontinue SNRIs.
pearls.verbatim: cross titrating fluoxetine is a good one for trying to get people off of because there's not a lot of withdrawal.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Bupropion 450 mg is rarely covered; prescribe 300 mg plus 150 mg to achieve the dose.
pearls.verbatim: bupropion comes in one fifty, three hundred, and four fifty. But the four fifty, you'll never get covered, so you'd have to prescribe three hundred and one fifty.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Before starting bupropion, screen for bipolar disorder and stabilize mood with an atypical antipsychotic if needed to prevent mania.
pearls.verbatim: For bipolar specifically, you need to start on some kind of, like, atypical antipsychotic is usually Abilify or Seroquel or Zyprexa or something like that to to stabilize their mood before you prompt them to have a manic episode.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Start buspirone at 7.5 mg twice daily (half a 15 mg tablet) for one week, then increase to 15 mg twice daily. Maximum 30 mg twice daily may be used.
pearls.verbatim: the fifteen and tell them to cut it in half and just do that. And I have one patient where for... I'll start on the 15, cut it in half for one week, and then they bump it up to the 15
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Trazodone is cheap and effective for insomnia but increases fall risk, especially in elderly patients; use low doses.
pearls.verbatim: trazodone ... cheap and it works, and usually, they use a low dose. Now it does increase your risk of falling.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Abruptly stopping high-dose benzodiazepines—especially Xanax—can cause withdrawal seizures.
pearls.verbatim: If you're on, like, high doses and you try to stop all of a sudden abruptly, especially the Xanax, then withdrawal seizures are bad.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: For patients with paradoxical crying or worsening depression on SSRIs/SNRIs, consider Trintellix (vortioxetine) because it modulates serotonin differently.
pearls.verbatim: I will say that if I've done everything possible and I can't figure it out, I'll try Trintellix. So that one works with the kind of serotonin, but it works differently than the SSRIs, and that sometimes is the one, for some people.
pearls.speaker: Greer
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greer on Anxiety & Depression 5/7/26

pearls.text: Do not treat aortic stenosis like CHF exacerbation; aggressive diuresis can cause decompensation and be difficult to reverse.
pearls.verbatim: You can't treat aortic stenosis like CHF exacerbation. It's completely separate. And it's all about hemodynamics, and they'll do worse. They'll decompensate if you pull too much fluid off.
pearls.speaker: Greta Warta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greta Warta on Valve Diseases 11/6/25

pearls.text: Listen to heart, lungs, and carotids every single patient visit because a murmur or bruit may be detected only on one occasion and missing it can lead to stroke.
pearls.verbatim: You wanna listen to every single patient every single time because there can be changes.
pearls.speaker: Greta Warta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greta Warta on Valve Diseases 11/6/25

pearls.text: In patients with bicuspid aortic valve, monitor the thoracic aorta diameter because they may need earlier surgical repair (4.5 cm) compared to others (5.0 cm).
pearls.verbatim: If someone has a bicuspid valve, you wanna look at their... You wanna watch, measure, and look at their aorta, the thoracic aorta, because that's where it could be different too.
pearls.speaker: Greta Warta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greta Warta on Valve Diseases 11/6/25

pearls.text: Target BP in aortic stenosis patients: keep systolic around 130-140 and diastolic around 80; avoid aggressive lowering to 120/70 as in SPRINT.
pearls.verbatim: I would say on something like, you know, one thirty to forty, eighty over 80, something like that. So don't go according to, like, sprint guidelines. Like, don't go... Don't drive it down to, like, one twenty over 70.
pearls.speaker: Greta Warta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greta Warta on Valve Diseases 11/6/25

pearls.text: When peak gradient does not meet severe criteria but aortic valve area does, err on the side of caution and consider the stenosis severe.
pearls.verbatim: So if your peak gradient doesn't meet severe criteria, the aortic valve area does, any felt severe? I would. And erring on the side of caution.
pearls.speaker: Greta Warta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greta Warta on Valve Diseases 11/6/25

pearls.text: Methamphetamine use can lead to dilated cardiomyopathy and stasis, predisposing to left ventricular thrombus formation.
pearls.verbatim: meth use can cause your heart to become weakened. And when your heart's weak, it's not moving. And when it becomes stagnant, that's when thrombus can be denied
pearls.speaker: Greta Warta
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greta Warta on Valve Diseases 11/6/25

pearls.text: For suspected miscarriage, follow up in one week until resolution; the only exception is if the miscarriage is already complete and you are just checking hCG to rule out gestational trophoblastic disease.
pearls.verbatim: If I have a patient that I believe may be having a miscarriage, I'm gonna see that patient or have them seen at least one week until that is resolved. Okay? The only time I may go a little longer is if I already think the miscarriage is complete, and I'm just checking an HCG to make sure there's no gestational trophoblastic disease.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: In prolonged miscarriage (2-3 months with retained products), infection is unusual; hemorrhage is the main concern.
pearls.verbatim: I don't think I've ever seen a lady that had, you know, true, like, endometritis or chorioamnionitis or anything like that with the miscarriage. And I've seen people that are, like, two, three months out. They've still got products, but they don't have an infection. ... Mostly what we're worried about is hemorrhage.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: For Rh-negative patients with miscarriage, give Rhogam; evidence is weak (class C) but the risk of alloimmunization is serious.
pearls.verbatim: If the patient is Rh negative, I would give them Rhogam. It's questionable. It's like class C evidence or whatever, it's kinda weak evidence, but rhogam is not very harmful, if it is at all. And if you have a person that becomes alloimmunized than a mother, then you probably not going to ever be able to have a child again.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: For medical management, instruct patients to place 4 misoprostol 200 mcg tablets vaginally, lie down for 30 minutes, and expect bleeding/cramping within 2-4 hours lasting 3-5 hours.
pearls.verbatim: Place four two hundred milligram misoprostol tabs in the vagina. You're usually gonna start lay down for thirty minutes. Usually gonna start having heavy bleeding or cramping within two to four hours. And this usually lasts for three to five hours.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: ER precautions for patients after misoprostol: bleeding >2 pads per hour for 2 hours, fever >101°F, chills, foul discharge, anemia symptoms, or uncontrolled pain.
pearls.verbatim: If it's greater than one zero one, if they have anemia signs and symptoms, if their cramps aren't controlled by medication or if they're bleeding two pads or more for an hour, they need to go to the hospital.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: When performing transvaginal ultrasound, always have the patient empty her bladder to avoid a common mistake.
pearls.verbatim: I forgot to tell her to empty her bladder. Such a rookie mistake. Y'all be like me. And I apologize profusely.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: Measure crown-rump length in the longest view of the fetus without limbs or yolk sac, and average three measurements.
pearls.verbatim: You measure a crown rump length in the... Basically, the longest view of the fetus. So you're gonna rotate your probe usually at least a 180 degrees and find the longest view of the fetus without limbs or yolk sac. And then you're go... And you're gonna measure that three times to get an average.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: For early pregnancy with no fetal pole seen at 6 weeks 2 days, counsel that it may be normal and schedule follow-up in two weeks.
pearls.verbatim: She's measuring six weeks, two days. What are you gonna say? Congratulations. Everything may be normal. We don't see a baby yet, but that may be normal.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: Use biparietal diameter for dating when the fetus is too large for crown-rump length, e.g., around 12 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: Measure the biparietal diameter. You'd be age twelve weeks, four days.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: Don't let the sun set on an ectopic pregnancy; send patients with significant pain to the ER or for same-day ultrasound.
pearls.verbatim: Don't let the sun set on an ectopic pregnancy. Make sure you send them to the ER that day or get an ultrasound that day for having significant pain.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on 1st TM Pregnancy

pearls.text: Document presentation by ultrasound at the 36-week visit; offering it when doing GBS screening is a good way to ensure it gets done.
pearls.verbatim: ACOG says to document by the thirty six week visit, which, you know, we say thirty five weeks is a good time to check it.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on Management of Fetal Malpresentation in the Third Trimester 8/13/26

pearls.text: Before ECV, get a full ultrasound workup: type of breech, head flexion/extension, estimated fetal weight, AFI, placental location, and rule out anomalies.
pearls.verbatim: So we gotta figure out what type of breach. You can try to see if the head is flexed or extended. Try to see estimated fetal weight.
pearls.speaker: Greuel
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Greuel on Management of Fetal Malpresentation in the Third Trimester 8/13/26

pearls.text: For patients who need delivery before 39 weeks for other indications, admit them directly and plan ECV followed by induction or cesarean if needed.
pearls.verbatim: If the patient is ready to be delivered, if they're thirty nine plus weeks or, let's say, MFM says deliver them at thirty eight weeks or thirty seven weeks for some indication. Right? And they're breech, then you can basically admit them and say, we're gonna induce...

pearls.text: Culture is the gold standard for TB diagnosis and drug susceptibility testing, but takes 3–6 weeks on solid media; a negative culture does not 100% rule out disease.

pearls.text: Sputum cultures should be obtained monthly until two are negative; conversion to negative is the key objective measure of treatment response.

pearls.text: Isoniazid's most common adverse reaction is peripheral neuropathy; co-administer vitamin B6 to prevent it.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kaleigh Winters on PNG & Tuberculosis 2/29/26

pearls.text: Baseline LFTs and monitoring are recommended for TB treatment only in high-risk patients; hold therapy if LFTs exceed three times the upper limit of normal.

pearls.text: Patients not improving or worsening in the first two months of treatment should be reevaluated: new sputum specimen, adherence check, symptom/exam review, and repeat chest X-ray.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kaleigh Winters on PNG & Tuberculosis 2/29/26

pearls.text: When ordering an endoscopy for GERD evaluation, do not routinely stop the PPI before the procedure; the GI specialist can decide whether to hold therapy to maximize diagnostic yield.

pearls.text: Alarm symptoms that require urgent endoscopy: unexplained weight loss, dysphagia/odynophagia, iron deficiency anemia, persistent vomiting, GI cancer in first-degree relative, new onset dyspepsia at age 60 or older.

And so you wouldn't treat them and open them up to the antibiotics, hassle treatment. So you have to get a stool test.

And then because there is some concern about b twelve and magnesium deficiencies with chronic PPI use, go ahead and magnesium and b twelve levels.

pearls.text: Alarm signs for EGD in GERD patients: unintentional weight loss, progressive dysphagia, odynophagia, early satiety, unexplained vomiting, GI bleeding, and iron deficiency anemia in men or postmenopausal women.
pearls.verbatim: When we're taking those histories for GERD, we always make sure we follow these alarmed signs. Wanna look for them and ask for them. Unintentional weight loss. Now you kinda have to spell that out these days. It's not on GLP-1s or other diets, but unintentional weight loss. Progressive dysphagia. I'm not gonna say just dysphagia, any dysphagia because you could run across that patient that says, yeah. I have it every so often, and it's been happening for years. You don't have any other lung symptoms. So that's not the one that I'm really concerned about. It's the one that's progressive, like, that happened... Usually happened every few months, and now it's happening every week and getting worse with food getting stuck. Odynophage. If it's painful, then we need to... That's a long sentence we need to look at right away. Early satiety. They can't finish their sandwich. They have to share it. The unexplained vomiting or GI bleeding coming up from the top or down. And then anytime you see iron deficiency anemia in a male male period, they just shouldn't have iron deficiency anemia.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: For acute heartburn, liquid antacids (Maalox, Mylanta, Tums, Rolaids) work within 5 minutes; PPIs take 2-3 hours and are not good for PRN use.
pearls.verbatim: If you've got a bout of heartburn, is liquid Maalox, Mylanta, Tums or Rolaid's, take care of it within five minutes. Or if you're at home, don't have any of that, you get called baking soda and water.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: For patients on long-term PPIs, check magnesium periodically (FDA recommendation) and use calcium citrate (not carbonate) because higher gastric pH reduces carbonate absorption.
pearls.verbatim: FDA recommends mag level periodically. I usually do a chem fourteen plus mag as boss. That's my protocol. There is osteopenia and fractures increased risk with use of PPIs over two years, particularly petite women's category that is really risk.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: Do not start a PPI trial for extraesophageal symptoms (cough, chest pain) without classic heartburn or regurgitation; work up chest pain first.
pearls.verbatim: If you don't have that hint of heartburn or reflux symptoms, then don't just start them on a trial. You need to work up the chest pain.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: For test of cure after H. pylori treatment, stop PPI for 2 weeks before testing.
pearls.verbatim: get them off of that for two weeks before you do the test of cure.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: For non-English speaking patients prescribed H. pylori therapy, schedule a follow-up visit to explain importance and dosing; consider giving Zofran for nausea.

pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: Do not substitute doxycycline for tetracycline in H. pylori quadruple therapy; it is a common error.

pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: When retreating H. pylori, do not reuse the same antibiotics from the first course.
pearls.verbatim: don't use the same antibiotics you used the first time around.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: After two H. pylori treatment failures, refer for EGD with culture and sensitivity.
pearls.verbatim: if there's two failures, you have to take them to EDD and get a culture and sensitivity.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: Wait at least one month after completing H. pylori therapy before testing for cure.
pearls.verbatim: Give it at least a month.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on GERD, Gastritis, and PUD

pearls.text: Post-feed upright positioning for 20-30 minutes helps decrease reflux; stop to burp once or twice during a bottle feeding.
pearls.verbatim: hold the baby in the upright position for twenty to thirty minutes as they're transitioning, getting rid of that air that they've got trapped from from nippling.
pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on Infant Gastroesophageal 4/16/26

pearls.text: Do not add thickener to breast milk; amylase in breast milk dissolves it too fast and it becomes thin again.

pearls.speaker: Keller
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on Infant Gastroesophageal 4/16/26

pearls.text: If blood is bright red per rectum, consider proctocolitis; if there is blood in vomitus or stools, consider cow's milk protein allergy.
pearls.verbatim: If you see blood in the vomitus, it can indicate esophagitis, pyloric stenosis, or cow's milk protein allergy. And, also, look at both ends. So if you're having blood out the the other end, it could be an allergy as well.

pearls.text: PPIs are only helpful for erosive esophagitis; they do not strengthen the lower esophageal sphincter and do not treat passive reflux.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Keller on Infant Gastroesophageal 4/16/26

pearls.text: Nexium (esomeprazole) delayed-release granules come in 2.5, 5, and 10 mg packets; mix with 1 teaspoon of water, let thicken, then draw into syringe and administer along the side of the mouth.

Wait a couple minutes because it thickens up, and then you suck it up with a syringe and pop it in the sides of their mouth so that they'll get it down.

pearls.text: Nicotine relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter, so caregivers should be counseled to stop smoking.

pearls.text: The tapering process can cause anxiety, withdrawal, and rebound anxiety depending on speed; warn patients and go slowly.

pearls.text: Taper benzodiazepines slowly; patients may not attribute reduced family arguments to the medication but will notice benefits.

pearls.text: Counsel patients on the risk of serotonin syndrome when starting serotonergic medications.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: Most benzodiazepines have a 20-30 minute onset, but panic attacks last only minutes, so PRN benzodiazepines do not work acutely.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.verbatim: Bruising on the torso, ears, and neck in children less than four are predictive of child abuse. Ten four are useful mnemonic. For identifying child abuse, that's force of ear, neck, and four for children less than four.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn

pearls.text: For benzodiazepine tapering, switch to a long-acting agent and then gradually taper.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: When tapering alprazolam (Xanax), consider reducing the dose slightly before switching to a long-acting benzodiazepine to improve patient adherence.
pearls.verbatim: Sometimes with Xanax, as I mentioned in my video lecture, depending on how high it is, Xanax is just super reinforcing. I might I might use Xanax a little bit first and kinda... Because many people really, really dodged to their Xanax. So if I can kinda get them on board with the plan and not switch them right off the gate, bring that down just a little bit, then convert them, and then finish the taper.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: Malignant hyperthermia presents with rigidity and antipsychotic use, whereas clonus points to serotonin syndrome; rigidity with antipsychotics should prompt consideration of neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: With malignant hyperthermia, you're usually having antipsychotics on board is what causes it. You have, like, rigidity. So clonus, serotonin drugs, serotonin syndrome, rigidity in the presence of antipsychotics, like comatose, you're thinking malignant hyperthermia.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: Asking about suicide does not increase suicide risk; most patients who complete suicide saw a primary care physician within 90 days, so screening is essential.
pearls.verbatim: Actually, most people who do complete suicide saw a primary care physician, like, within ninety days of their attempt. So ask and screen for it. Really important in primary care.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: Naltrexone for alcohol use disorder: start at 25 mg weekly to avoid GI upset, then increase to 50 mg; safe if LFTs are less than 3 times upper limit of normal; can be initiated even if patient is still drinking.
pearls.verbatim: Twenty five milligrams per week. They go up to fifty because it can make your stomach upset. Generally, they should be off alcohol. If I can get them kind of backed off a little bit, I'll start naltrexone if their LFTs are okay. He's not, like, less than three times up the level of normal. I'm still drinking. I will go ahead and get it started.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: Sleep medications develop tolerance quickly; consider drug holidays (e.g., weekends off) or cycling to maintain efficacy; CBT-I remains first-line treatment.
pearls.verbatim: It's just most of your, like, sleep drugs, your body just gets adjusted to them pretty quickly for anything that has, like, a sedative hypnotic effect. ... If I can get them to, like, take the weekends off or, you know, take, you know, take a couple days in the week that maybe they can... A little rough rougher night of sleep just to try to limit some of the tolerance you're gonna experience with with sleep meds.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: For depression partial response to an SSRI, maximize the SSRI dose first, then add bupropion (Wellbutrin) as augmentation; bupropion does not contribute to serotonin syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: If they're, like, partial response to SSRI, I usually make sure they're on, like, the max dose of the SSRI, then I'll add the p bupropion. Absolutely. Like Welloft, Wellbutrin, plus Zoloft is kind of a good combo. ... And Wellbutrin does not work on serotonin, so it's not gonna contribute to serotonin syndrome.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: In children, treat anxiety and depression first before treating ADHD, because attention problems are hallmark of untreated mood disorders.
pearls.verbatim: Generally, the the approach in psychiatry is you manage anxiety, depression first before you manage ADHD. So you want mood and anxiety to be stable before you start treating ADHD.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on IHI FM Board Review (9/11/25)

pearls.text: Before considering stimulants for attention problems, evaluate sleep—poor sleep is a common contributing factor.
pearls.verbatim: I think a lot of it is poor sleep related. So a lot of times, I'm I'm really asking about sleep before I'm thinking about stimulants and other things.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Use the STOP-BANG questionnaire to screen for obstructive sleep apnea based on snoring, tiredness, observed apneas, blood pressure, BMI, age, neck circumference, and gender.
pearls.verbatim: This screens for obstructive sleep apnea based on snoring, tiredness, observed apneas, blood pressure, BMI, age, neck circumference, and gender.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: For trouble falling asleep, use a short-acting benzodiazepine with a short half-life to avoid lingering daytime sedation.
pearls.verbatim: If they're having trouble falling asleep and not staying asleep, then you might use a short one with a short half life so it's not going linger throughout the day.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Do not exceed 10 mg of melatonin; higher doses provide no additional benefit.
pearls.verbatim: there's definitely not anything to support anything above ten milligrams. So once you're getting there, you're just spending a lot of money for no reason. So ten milligram would be the the cap.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Use generic doxepin 10 mg for sleep maintenance; the on-label 6 mg dose is expensive.
pearls.verbatim: Doxepin actually has an on label use at six milligrams, which is really expensive. So I just use the ten milligram tabs, which are generic.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Do not assume a normal BMI excludes sleep apnea; screening is necessary regardless of body habitus.
pearls.verbatim: So that's why you need to kind of do your screening and not just assume, you know, if their BMI is normal, they're not... They don't have sleep apnea. Because that that happens quite frequently too.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: When suspecting narcolepsy, refer to sleep medicine to confirm diagnosis due to the controlled nature of treatments like modafinil and sodium oxybate.
pearls.verbatim: But, generally, for me, when I'm suspecting this, like, I'm trying to get them into a sleep medicine, right, to make sure my diagnosis is correct.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: REM sleep behavior disorder may be an early sign of neurodegenerative disease like Parkinson's; consider it a red flag.
pearls.verbatim: And it's important to be able to recognize this because we're we're seeing more and more that RVD might be a harbinger for other disease processes. One of those might be, like, neurodegenerative links. It's been associated with diseases such as Parkinson's and other dementias.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: In restless legs syndrome, check iron panel and consider iron supplementation as first step.
pearls.verbatim: It's been linked to iron deficiency. So checking iron panel, maybe even supplementing with iron to see if it benefits.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Avoid sedatives in patients with sleep apnea or restless legs syndrome as they worsen these disorders.
pearls.verbatim: Sedatives. Worsens sleep apnea, restless leg, and other sleep disorders.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Monitor sleep when prescribing antidepressants; they can cause insomnia, worsen sleep disorders, and induce parasomnias.
pearls.verbatim: antidepressants can cause insomnia, worsen sleep disorders, and induce non REM and REM parasomnia. So keeping an eye on how their sleep's going if you're prescribing an antidepressant.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: For Wellbutrin SR dosed twice daily, the second dose must be given between noon and 3 PM to avoid sleep disruption.
pearls.verbatim: Wellbutrin SR, commonly prescribed twice a day. That second dose needs to be between noon and three, usually. Don't want it in QHS. You'll impact sleep.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Opioids can induce central sleep apnea, and opioid withdrawal can cause restless legs syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: Opioids can induce a central sleep apnea. And opioid withdrawal can cause restless leg syndrome.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Use Mother to Baby website to check drug safety in pregnancy and obtain patient handouts for informed consent.
pearls.verbatim: I recommend going to mother to baby. That's the website that really gives you a lot of pregnancy data for different drugs. So if you need to check on if a drug's safe in pregnancy, if you wanna use, like, Benadryl or you wanna use a benzo, you can give a mother to baby kind of review that information. I believe they also have patient handouts that educate on that medication too so then you can document the informed consent process
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Kelly Dunn on Sleep Disorders
