Whose temperature is, like, 30, I don't know, thirty, thirty, and they're in cardiac arrest because they were outside for too long, You have to do these invasive warming measures to warm them up.
pearls.speaker: Nicole Tipton
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Nicole Tipton on Environmental Exposures 11/20/25

pearls.text: Preexisting structural brain issues (cortical atrophy, dementia, stroke history, TBI, Parkinson's, meningitis) make patients more susceptible to delirium when medically ill; the weakest link breaks first.
pearls.verbatim: And a attending of mine always told me that the weakest link in the chain is the first to break. So if they have cognitive impairment from just diffuse cortical dementia, that's the thing that falls apart first.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: The Monro-Kellie doctrine explains that cellular damage begets more damage via edema, hypoperfusion, and secondary infarction, leading to herniation if not contained.
pearls.verbatim: So you can have any form of herniation occur anywhere from mass effect from any of these disruptive processes that will eventually lead you down to the terminal herniation.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Consciousness requires three components: bilateral cortices (bulb), thalami (switch), and reticular activating system (cord); loss of any one knocks out consciousness.
pearls.verbatim: if you try to understand it from the neuroanatomical concept, you're gonna run away screaming. It's very, very simple. You need three components intact for consciousness to be intact on a very boil down level. The cortex or both cortices need to be working. So the globes, thalami need to be working, and reticular activating system, which is not exactly a structure.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For delirium prevention, keep patients mobile during the day, turn lights on, ensure glasses and hearing aids are used, and maintain day-night orientation.
pearls.verbatim: When you walk in a room during the daylight, the lights on or off often? Off. Is that good for a delirious? No. No. K. When you walk in, is that person laid up in bed, or are they out in the chair usually. Mobility. Sitting in the dark all day. Are they often... We're we're taking care of mostly the elderly. The elderly have different with vision, the difficulties with vision. Are they wearing their glasses or their hearing aids? It's like being a prisoner of your own body.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Subarachnoid hemorrhage causes coma through diffuse cerebral irritation and edema, not just focal mass effect.
pearls.verbatim: Subarachnoids, that's more diffuse process. So often there are comas. Subdurals, if they're big enough.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: In a comatose patient, a blown pupil signals uncal herniation and increased ICP; if the patient is awake, consider topical agents like albuterol or scopolamine patches.
pearls.verbatim: Remember that this is a sign of increased ICP. Thus, if that patient is awake talking to you, they're not herniating.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Forced eye deviation: if eyes look away from the flaccid side, it's a stroke; if they look toward the flaccid side, it's a seizure.
pearls.verbatim: If they are looking away from the plegic side, so flaccid right looking away, the stroke. If it's looking towards the flaccid side, they're having a seizure.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For coma workup, start with CT without contrast for acute anatomical lesions; if CT is clear, get MRI for subtle causes like meningitis, anoxic injury, or cerebral edema.
pearls.verbatim: CT without Swine without. If you have a hemorrhagic. I have gray hemorrhagic. Blood. I'll dress up the same. Good. So stat CT, immediate pursuit once the ABCs are stabilized. It shows you acute anatomical anatomical lesions, space occupying lesions that are threatening that person's life.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Coma masquerades include locked-in syndrome from Guillain-Barré or myasthenic crisis, residual paralysis, sedation, botulism, and hypoglycemia; always consider if imaging and metabolic workup are negative.
pearls.verbatim: So Residual paralysis paralysis without sedation. So in fellowship, I have... I had a case where we were in your credit fellowship. We got called down to the the medical ICU to evaluate a patient for brain death. He had no brain stem reflexes. He was on a ventilator. He's been, I think, for days. So we get down there and evaluate this guy, and we're going through our checklist. We have a checklist for brain death. And I start reviewing his CT, and his CAT scans are totally normal. And one of the priorities for brain death declaration is that he must have a CAT scan that explains the patient's coma. They must have a devastating. This guy's CAT scan is normal. So already, we're like, woah. Hold on. Long story short, we diagnosed this guy with severe Guillain-Barré syndrome.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Consider infiltrative cardiomyopathy due to cardiac metastases when a patient has heart failure symptoms but normal initial echocardiogram.
pearls.verbatim: This explains why there was no systolic dysfunction on the echo. There was no diastole, no valvular problems. But this person looked very CHF y.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For carcinoid syndrome symptoms, somatostatin analogs like octreotide are first-line therapy, and chromogranin levels are used to monitor response.
pearls.verbatim: octreotide monthly, and then we're tracking chromogranin levels as the objective measure to see, is this person responding to our therapy?
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For diagnosing neuroendocrine tumors, order a 24-hour urine 5-HIAA level and serum chromogranin, which has 96% specificity.
pearls.verbatim: Get also a twenty four hour urine HIAA level. Serum chromogranin. It has a 96% specificity for neuroendocrine tumors.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: A positive chromogranin indicates neuroendocrine tumor with 80% sensitivity; a negative test does not rule out disease.
pearls.verbatim: 80% sensitivity is when if it's positive, you have it.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For suspected neuroendocrine tumors, order a CT of the abdomen and pelvis because most are colonic in origin.
pearls.verbatim: So get a CT of the abdomen and pelvis because most neuroendocrine tumors are colonic in origin.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: If concerned for hepatic neuroendocrine metastases, order an MRI of the liver.
pearls.verbatim: And then if you're concerned about hepatic NETs, do an MRI.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: When a patient with neuroendocrine tumor is discharged and declines hospice, order a PET scan to identify malignant disease.
pearls.verbatim: If you're discharging them and they don't wanna do hospice, get them to do a PET scan.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For carcinoid flushing, advise patients to avoid triggers like alcohol and use somatostatin analogs.
pearls.verbatim: If they have flushing, tell them to avoid the things that we talked about. Use this alcohol, etcetera. And then, again, somatostatin analogs.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For carcinoid diarrhea, treat with somatostatin analogs and antidiarrheals.
pearls.verbatim: Diarrhea, obvious things like somatostatin analogs again and the diarrheals.
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Screen first-degree relatives of patients with neuroendocrine tumors per colon cancer guidelines: colonoscopy starting 10 years before the age of diagnosis of the affected relative.
pearls.verbatim: Same guidelines as colon cancer. So ten years before the age of diagnosis of a first degree for screening. A colonoscopy
pearls.speaker: Okeefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Okeefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For seizures in cerebral malaria, skip Valium because it causes excessive sedation; start with phenobarb 20 mg/kg.
pearls.verbatim: I skip Valium because it makes it too sedated. I start with phenobarb twenty mg per kg.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: Give IV artesunate for severe malaria before the test result returns; give three doses then switch to Coartem.
pearls.verbatim: We give IV artesunate three doses, and then we go to Coartem.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: For suspected typhoid with abdominal tenderness, admit for serial abdominal exams to detect perforation.
pearls.verbatim: Serial abdominal exams. Admit her.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: Do not just tell staff a patient needs to go to the ER; physically walk them there to avoid 30–60 minute delays.
pearls.verbatim: I learned don't say, 'oh, she needs to go to the ER' because then it happens thirty to sixty minutes later. I... We walked together to the ER
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: In severe malnutrition, monitor electrolytes, give vitamins, and start prophylactic antibiotics during refeeding.
pearls.verbatim: We have a feeding protocol. We're watching their electrolytes carefully. They also get tons of vitamins. They also get prophylactic antibiotics.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: In neonates <32 weeks gestational age, use an NG tube because they lack the suck-swallow-breathe reflex.
pearls.verbatim: If they're less than 32 gestational age, which we try to do our Ballard scores to get the approximate age because moms don't know how how far along they were. You're gonna do NG tube if it's less than 32 because neurologically, they're not developed enough to know that suck, suck, swallow, breathe, neurologic rhythm, and reflex.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: For neonates 32–34 weeks, consider NG tube with trial of PO feeding sitting up; >34 weeks can usually feed orally.
pearls.verbatim: In that thirty two to thirty four weeks, you've got some gray area. Probably, you'll just do an NG tube and watch them and and see how they do. Try to have mom feed them sitting up. And then at greater than 34, you can usually do a PO.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: Use ultrasound to differentiate a bladder clot from a congenital tumor by rolling the patient; if the mass moves with position change, it is likely a clot.
pearls.verbatim: I keep that probe on. I have her move, and it moves with her. So... Oh my god. Good. Good. Not a congenital tumor.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: When troponin is unavailable, use echocardiography to look for regional wall motion abnormalities to diagnose MI.
pearls.verbatim: I can't get a troponin because we those. So what are two ways that I can look for an MI? Echo. What am I looking for in my echo? Regional wall motion abnormality.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: When a patient seizes after a medication, treat the underlying cause (e.g., hypoperfusion) rather than giving a seizure medication.
pearls.verbatim: I did not give him a seizure med because I'm like, no. We're just gonna treat the cause, not the symptoms.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: For excessive secretions in a pediatric patient, consider using glycopyrrolate; it can be effective and safe in children.
pearls.verbatim: I looked up. I was like, why not? It's worth a shot. I'll see if we've got glycopyrrolate on our formulary. We did. I looked up. Can you give it to kids on up to date? Yes. You can. And I found the dosing, and I ordered it.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: Missionary physicians should be prepared to treat a wide variety of conditions, as they function as an 'everything hospitalist' in resource-limited settings.
pearls.verbatim: He took my IHRI experience of three years as an adult hospitalist in a super huge hospital to prepare me to be an everything hospitalist treating all kinds of crazy things in the middle of nowhere.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: When considering malaria prevention, assess whether the local population will actually use mosquito nets, as cultural barriers may render them ineffective.
pearls.verbatim: Would people... Would people even use malaria mosquito nets if we gave them to them? Because, you know, there's no point in buying mosquito nets if they're not gonna use them.
pearls.speaker: Papp speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Papp speaks on Medicine and Missions

pearls.text: If a patient in the developing world presents with vague symptoms and you detect a liver rub on auscultation, you can give a very certain prognosis of advanced hepatoma.
pearls.verbatim: So it was not rare to put my hand on the belly and know... And then take my stethoscope and listen, and then I could tell them what was gonna happen with a very high degree of certainty, and it wasn't good news. He got cancer of the liver.
pearls.speaker: Patrick
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Patrick on Ethics and Morals

pearls.text: Do not shorten the dying period unnecessarily; patients use that time for deep reconciliation, which is an important spiritual need.
pearls.verbatim: So when we shorten the dying period, which, of course, the bureaucrats want because spend most of our money in the last bit of our lives, that doesn't has... That doesn't have to be the case.
pearls.speaker: Patrick
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Patrick on Ethics and Morals

pearls.text: When a patient hands over trust completely — as when you become a patient yourself — do not question the physician's competence; accept that they are in charge.
pearls.verbatim: I agreed to become a patient without saying a word because, obviously, the next thing that happened was a lumbar puncture. I didn't even ask who was gonna do it and how many they'd done. I had handed over.
pearls.speaker: Patrick
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Patrick on Ethics and Morals

pearls.text: If a physician does not fear judgment after death, patients have reason to fear their doctor, especially during their medical lifetime, because they will be pressurized by financial incentives.
pearls.verbatim: What they realized was if your doctor does not fear judgment after death, you've got good reason to start fearing your doctor, especially during your medical lifetime, because you will be pressurized by the money changers that you're not having enough people get made.
pearls.speaker: Patrick
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Patrick on Ethics and Morals

pearls.text: When waking up, say the Lord's Prayer twice: once by rote, then ask God to stop you somewhere in the prayer to think about during the day as a guard against distraction.
pearls.verbatim: When you wake up in the morning, before you move, say the Lord's prayer twice. Once by rote, and then ask him to stop you somewhere in the prayer for you to think about during the day so that when you come to a moment when you could go off into fantasy or whatever, you don't.
pearls.speaker: Patrick
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Patrick on Ethics and Morals

pearls.text: Eugenics in IVF—selecting against certain diseases—implies that some people should not exist, which is a dangerous presumption against God's creation.
pearls.verbatim: Eugenics says we know who the best people are, and we'll get rid of the bad ones. Are you daring to say to God that he's putting people into the world who wouldn't... Shouldn't be here?
pearls.speaker: Patrick
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Patrick on Ethics and Morals

pearls.text: Modern medicine has more pain control options than ever; fear of pain and death should not drive us to abandon effective palliative care.
pearls.verbatim: We have more control over pain than we've ever had in the history of medicine, and yet we're fussing in the way that we are now fearing pain and death.
pearls.speaker: Patrick
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Patrick on Ethics and Morals

pearls.text: Nocturia is often the first and most bothersome symptom in BPH; use it as a screening question.
pearls.verbatim: Nocturia is usually thought of as kind of a cardinal symptom, probably the one that happens first before some of these physical symptoms occur. And so often, that's kind of my screening question and usually the one that bothers folks the most.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Always perform a digital rectal exam in patients presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms; it is not optional.
pearls.verbatim: do you have to check the prostate if a patient comes in with lower urinary tract symptoms? Yes. A hundred percent of the time. Please do not come and tell me that this patient has lower urinary tract symptoms and then not tell me their prostate is normal, and it's not nodular.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: In patients with very low PSA (<0.1), suspect hypogonadism and check testosterone levels.
pearls.verbatim: when the PSA is really low like that, make sure you're thinking about testosterone. K? So a lot of those men who have extremely low PSAs are gonna be hypogonadal. They're gonna have low, low T.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Use double voiding: empty the bladder, wait a few minutes (e.g., brush teeth), then empty again to reduce post-void residual before bed.
pearls.verbatim: Double voiding is literally what it is. It's empty your bladder. Go brush your teeth. Empty your bladder again. Right? Ten minutes, five minutes.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: For men with nocturia, give alpha-1 antagonists at bedtime to maximize effect during sleep.
pearls.verbatim: And we often do give these drugs at bedtime if patients are having mostly nocturia, they seem to help more when they're kind of on board during the night.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Five-alpha reductase inhibitors take 2–4 months to significantly reduce prostate volume; do not expect rapid improvement.
pearls.verbatim: Because these take usually two to three to four months, really, before you see significant gland volume decrease.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: BPH is a true hyperplasia (increase in cell number), not hypertrophy (increase in cell size); correct the old terminology.
pearls.verbatim: It is technically a hyperplasia. So in the old days, we used benign prostatic hypertrophy. But if you think, if you look under the microscope, this is actually a true hyperplasia.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Use the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) as a validated instrument to quantify and characterize LUTS in clinical practice.
pearls.verbatim: The International Prostate Symptom Score is is a validated instrument used to kind of quantify and characterize the symptoms.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Define intermittency as stopping and starting several times during urination.
pearls.verbatim: How often have you found you stopped and started again several times? That's called intermittency.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Define urgency as difficulty postponing urination; ask if the patient feels they will leak if they don't get to a bathroom immediately.
pearls.verbatim: How often have you found it difficult to postpone urination? That's urgency.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Ask about weak urinary stream and straining to start or maintain urination, which indicates obstructive symptoms.
pearls.verbatim: How often have you had a weak urinary stream? Straining, how often have you had to strain to start urination or to keep urination going?
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

pearls.text: Avoid caffeine within 30 minutes before measuring blood pressure; this is a common error in clinic.
pearls.verbatim: The big one that I think we mess up here is the caffeine.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: For elderly frail patients, relax the BP target to avoid falls; for robust elderly, maintain the 130/80 target.
pearls.verbatim: If they're frail and, you know, falling, etcetera, that's a different equation or a different discussion.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: Communicate BP targets to patients as 'the 120s over 70s' rather than '130/80' to avoid them accepting higher readings.
pearls.verbatim: I want you in the one twenties over seventies. That's where I want you to be with your blood pressure.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: For stage 2 hypertension, initiate combination therapy with an ARB and amlodipine rather than monotherapy.
pearls.verbatim: For most in stage two, I will start an ARB with amlodipine.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: Prefer long-acting ARBs (e.g., olmesartan) over ACE inhibitors to avoid the risk of cough or angioedema that burns the entire RAS class.
pearls.verbatim: Why do I use an ARB a night with lisinopril? And you just Cough. ... you've burned the ACE and probably the ARB ... So I just don't even give it a chance.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: Use a potassium chloride salt substitute to simultaneously reduce sodium and increase potassium, lowering BP by up to 10 mmHg.
pearls.verbatim: A potassium chloride salt substitute will do both of these things. So I often talk with my blood pressure patients. Just use a salt substitute. These are not CKD4 people.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: For well-controlled hypertension, ask patients to check BP at home 2-3 times per month as 'spot checks'.
pearls.verbatim: I generally ask them to do it a couple times a month, two, three times a month. I use the word spot check.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: When titrating medications, have patients check BP twice in the morning after voiding (sitting 5 min before breakfast) and twice at bedtime, recording both numbers.
pearls.verbatim: Sit for five minutes. Check your blood pressure twice. I wanna know both those numbers. And then I want you to do that same thing at bedtime.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: When starting an ARB, a creatinine rise up to 30% is expected and indicates the medication is lowering hyperfiltration; a greater rise may indicate bilateral renal artery stenosis.
pearls.verbatim: If it jumps more than 30%, it could be they are one of these renal artery stenosis people, maybe even bilateral.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: Wrist cuffs are usually falsely high; only use them if the patient's arm is too large for an arm cuff.
pearls.verbatim: What about wrist cuffs? There you go. People's getting Falsely high. They're usually falsely high. The only reason you would use a wrist cuff is if they're so beefy, you can't get a big enough arm cuff and at least have something.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: When changing medication, have patients check BP 2-3 times per week, e.g., Monday, Wednesday, Friday, with two measurements each morning and night.
pearls.verbatim: When I'm changing medication, I'll do two or three times a week. I'll often say Monday, Wednesday, Friday, something like that. Two measurements morning, two measurements at night.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: When starting an ARB, a mild rise in creatinine is expected and will stabilize at a higher level; do not discontinue the medication.
pearls.verbatim: It'll go there. It'll stay there. It'll restabilize at that higher level.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: A potassium level up to 5.5 is acceptable when using an ARB; hypertension specialists will wait for that threshold before intervening.
pearls.verbatim: They'll wait for that potassium to get to 5.5 as their number before.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: If hyperkalemia occurs on an ARB, use potassium binders to keep the patient on the ARB rather than discontinuing it.
pearls.verbatim: They put them on potassium binders. Didn't drop their ARB.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hyperextension

pearls.text: Only use a wrist cuff if the patient's arm is too large to fit an arm cuff; wrist cuffs are otherwise inaccurate.
pearls.verbatim: The only reason I would use a wrist cuff is if the patient's arm is so large that they can't find a cuff that will actually go around their arm.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypertension 2.12.26

pearls.text: For stage 2 hypertension, remember the mnemonic 'Stage two, start two' to initiate dual therapy.
pearls.verbatim: Stage two, start two.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypertension 2.12.26

pearls.text: For stage 2 hypertension, start dual therapy with an ARB and amlodipine (the workhorse calcium channel blocker).
pearls.verbatim: ARB and a non dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker, the workhorse is amlodipine in our country.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypertension 2.12.26

pearls.text: Before referring resistant hypertension to a specialist, complete a sleep study, renin activity, and consider renal artery stenosis to avoid missing secondary causes.
pearls.verbatim: If you send your resistant hypertension patients to the cardiologist or nephrologist and you haven't done a sleep study and a renin activity and least thought about renal artery stenosis... That's a really bad form.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypertension 2.12.26

pearls.text: Use a long-acting ARB (e.g., olmesartan, telmisartan) rather than a short-acting one to ensure 24-hour coverage.
pearls.verbatim: put them on a long acting ARB, please.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypertension 2.12.26

pearls.text: Never use PRN antihypertensives; they are not supported by data and can cause harm.
pearls.verbatim: PRN and antihypertensives are not supported in any data that I am aware of. And so don't do that, please.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypertension 2.12.26

pearls.text: Erectile dysfunction is mostly vascular (blood pressure, diabetes) and often does not improve with testosterone; avoid creating an expectation that T will fix it.
pearls.verbatim: Erectile dysfunction is complicated. Right? It's a messy symptom because there's a lot of other pathology that causes it. It's actually mostly vascular. There's a little bit of T involvement, there's some crossover, but it's mostly vascular. Mostly blood pressure and diabetes and blood vessels that are sick. And so it doesn't... And often doesn't get better with T.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: If initial total T is low or borderline, repeat the level in 2-3 weeks and order total T, SHBG, free T, FSH, and LH to confirm and classify the hypogonadism.
pearls.verbatim: I start with a total T. Alright? Total T measures total circulating testosterone, which includes bound and free. ... So I get that first. If I get a low number or a borderline low number, I repeat that level a second time, about two weeks later, two, three weeks later. This is my this is my practice is what I do. With that, I order the rest of the testosterone tests. I will order a total and an SHBG. I usually will add an FSH and LH at that point and then other stuff.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: The standard total testosterone order in Cerner is an older assay that is inaccurate at low levels; use LCMS total testosterone for accuracy.
pearls.verbatim: So if you order total testosterone, you're gonna get an older version of that test. It's not a horrible test, but it's not very accurate at low levels of testosterone, which is where you're... Where you need it to be accurate.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: For patients with BMI >35, prediabetes, and sedentary lifestyle, order the full total/free/SHBG panel upfront because they likely have functional hypogonadism.
pearls.verbatim: So if a person comes to me and their BMI is thirty five and they've got prediabetes and they're sedentary, I just do the whole deal. I do the total free SHBG panel because they're probably... I'm gonna probably wanna know that.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Testosterone increases risk of pulmonary embolism; avoid in patients with a history of PE or hypercoagulable state.
pearls.verbatim: they do have an increased risk, and this was PE, actually, the higher risk of PE. And so when a patient comes in, they have a history of PE or they have a hypercoagulable state or there's something else, no T. Don't get T.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Testosterone is absolutely contraindicated in men who want to remain fertile because exogenous T shuts off FSH and LH, causing testicular atrophy and azoospermia.
pearls.verbatim: You cannot give this to a 30 year old guy and not tell him you're... You can't have a child if you do this. You're gonna be sterile. Right? Why? Think of the physiology. Giving you exogenous testosterone. And what does that do? Shuts off FSH and LH. Right? And what happens to the Sertoli cells? They just go to sleep.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Start testosterone cypionate at 100 mg IM weekly; avoid every-2-week dosing because the washout makes patients feel poorly.
pearls.verbatim: I start people a hundred milligrams per week. You will see it written at two hundred every two weeks or a hundred every two weeks. The kinetics of the... Both of these forms of testosterone are such that they really do have a washout. So I don't do the two week, even though that's written on there. I just find that that that washout makes patients feel very funny and not very good.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Gel testosterone carries risk of transference to children; counsel patients to avoid skin-to-skin contact after application.
pearls.verbatim: Remember, there's transference of this, so if they have kids and they're holding a kid, the kid's gonna get a bunch of tea. They may not want that. Probably don't want that.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: When hematocrit rises above 54, switch from IM to gel; the lower total dose and steady state often correct the issue.
pearls.verbatim: So often, you will see that one change we make when a person gets a a crit that's above 54 is they'll move them... We'll move them to a gel.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Monitor labs every 2-3 months the first year, then annually once stable; insurance requires documentation of symptom improvement.
pearls.verbatim: And then about every two to three months, the first year is is the general rule in terms of insurance coverage. And then once they're at a stable dose, you can do an annual lab.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Start testosterone at 100 mg weekly IM, check mid-dose (3-4 days after injection) and target a level of 450-600.
pearls.verbatim: So I start them hundred milligrams weekly. I wait four to six cycles. So four to six weeks is what we think it takes to get to steady state on that dose. And then I check mid dose. So if they give their shot on Monday, then I'm drawing their t on Thursday. K? Three to four days after. And I'm looking basically for five hundred, four fifty to six hundred.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: If PSA goes over 4 or jumps by 1.5 or more, refer to urology; it is not necessarily cancer but warrants monitoring.
pearls.verbatim: If it goes over four, you send over the urologist, and then they usually watch them with you. So they they just start doing repeat PSAs, etcetera. Or if they jump by one and a half, that's not a person that goes from one and a half to 40. Right? If that that wasn't your testosterone, number one. And number two, that's not the same. That's the person that needs to go right away.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Hematocrit above 54 on testosterone is a high-risk situation for heart attack, stroke, or clot; it is your responsibility to manage it.
pearls.verbatim: Being on T with a hemorrhagic rate over 54, I mean, that is a very high risk situation for developing a heart attack, a stroke, or some kind of clot, and it is your fault. So that is not something you wanna do.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Anabolic steroid use is a common cause of primary hypogonadism; young bodybuilders may have very low testosterone and irreversible testicular damage.
pearls.verbatim: So even even like gym bros that have been using anabolic steroids, that is a very common cause of finding primary hypogoninism. We didn't talk about that. So I have several young young bodybuilders that their Ts are a hundred and hundred fifty because they've used it their whole life, and they have no they have no testicle left, and they're just done.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Use a patient's complaint of low testosterone as an opening to discuss lifestyle, diabetes, obesity, and mental health.
pearls.verbatim: So when they come in and they're like, I don't have any energy. I'm fatigued, whatever. I think it's my tea. That is like an open door. Depressed? You, you know, you... Are you just having a horrible life? Are you diabetic? Are you obese? I mean, it is a way in, especially men, that opens up the things that are truly important.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Hypogonadism 10/16/25

pearls.text: Class 3 obesity is defined as BMI over 40; use this classification instead of 'morbid obesity'.
pearls.verbatim: Class three is is what? BMI over 40.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: In obese patients (e.g., BMI 35, age 32), check A1C because the risk of diabetes is 7x in men and 12x in women.
pearls.verbatim: When you have the obese patient that comes in, their BMI is thirty five, and they're 32 years old, the right thing to do is check their A1C because they have a seven times or 12 times risk of being a diabetic.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: The first presentation of heart attack (ASCVD) is often sudden death, not chest pain.
pearls.verbatim: What's the first presentation for heart attack? Sudden death.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Do not use the term 'morbid obesity'; it is stigmatizing and harmful. Use class 3 obesity instead.
pearls.verbatim: Please do not use the term morbid obesity. Okay? It is a stigmatizing term.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Be aware that medications like mirtazapine can cause significant weight gain; consider stopping them if appropriate.
pearls.verbatim: The psychiatrist put her on mirtazapine. She gained a whole bunch of weight, and she has all kinds of eating disorder problems. And she came in, and I I was like, your psychiatrist not talking to you about this drug? She's like, no. So I said, well, let's stop that first.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: In patients with Down syndrome or cerebral palsy, obesity rates are ~80% due to sedentary lifestyle; screen proactively.
pearls.verbatim: Down syndrome, CP, the folks that you see, those people stay sedentary. Obesity rates are, like, eighty percent in that population.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Sign up for apps like Noom or Weight Watchers yourself to understand what you recommend; you don't need to lose weight but need to know the tool.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: If you prescribe orlistat (Xenical) without warning the patient to eat a low-fat meal, they will experience oily fecal incontinence, often after passing gas, and will never trust the drug again.
pearls.verbatim: if you write them for Xenical and you don't tell them to eat a low fat meal It leaks. They will think they're gonna pass a little gas, and it's not gas.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Patients will often hide their use of Ozempic or Mounjaro because of strong stigma and internal shame; they feel like failures if they lose weight with medication.
pearls.verbatim: Patients will hide from you the fact that they're taking Ozempic or Mounjaro from the, you know, back alley, whatever. They will hide it because the stigma is really strong. And they also carry their own internal stigma. They do not wanna talk about this. They're embarrassed. They feel like if they lose weight with medication, they're a failure.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: When starting a GLP-1 agonist, tell the patient to eat half of what they normally eat; if still hungry, they can eat a little more. If they try to eat their usual amount, they will become sick.

pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.verbatim: Don't use trackers in eating disorders. Kinda goes without saying. These are patients who are tracking everything. And if you say, hey. Use a tracker. You make them sicker.
pearls.speaker: Place
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: Titrate GLP-1 agonists to the highest tolerable dose; do not stop at a low dose. Let the patient tell you when they cannot go higher.

pearls.verbatim: Once they're a goal weight, I start talking about backing them off. So every ten days, even every fourteen days. And it's okay to mix those with some phentermine or Topamax or whatever you wanna do.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.verbatim: if you write for Ozempic in a nondiabetic patient, it will be rejected. Right. Right. Right. Right. Every time.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Obesity

pearls.text: After CABG, about 30% of patients develop clinical major depressive disorder within a year, so consider starting an SSRI or SNRI preoperatively.

pearls.verbatim: What you're gonna put in here is the actual surgery that the patient's gonna have. Alright. So my guy, I have a... I had a 64 year old guy come in this morning. Gonna have a total knee. Then it come... It comes up with the CPT code of what he's actually gonna be having.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: Consider postponing elective surgery if the ACS risk calculator shows a serious complication risk of 10% or higher, and use the opportunity to optimize modifiable factors like A1c.
pearls.verbatim: If they're getting up in the ten percent or above serious complication, that's just kind of a rule of thumb that I that I kinda say, man, your A1c is 12, and you're... You know? Let's let's talk about how we can how we can postpone this.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: Screen functional capacity by asking if the patient can climb two flights of stairs without stopping (4 METs); this is the minimum needed to avoid a major adverse cardiac event during surgery.
pearls.verbatim: I screen with, can you climb up a flight of stairs? One flight of stairs is two minutes of work. Two flights of stairs is four minutes of work without stopping. Can you go up two flights of stairs without stopping without any chest pain, without falling down, without, right, filling the blank? Can you walk up a hill? Can you walk at ground level at four miles an hour?

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Place on Pre-Operative Assessment

pearls.text: Order a CBC for patients over 65 having major surgery; the white count is not helpful, but platelets matter if spinal anesthesia is planned.

How do we set your quit date the day you go have your surgery? Let's get all your nicotine and everything in place. Let's get you on your Chantix or whatever. And when you go in the hospital and have your surgery, never

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Santillano on OTC tips

pearls.speaker: Santillano
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Santillano on OTC tips

pearls.text: For diaper rash, early treatment with clotrimazole can prevent severe pain and crying; prescribe even if it didn't start fungal.
pearls.verbatim: if you have a kid who's prone to diaper infections, that probably as soon as they start having anything to do start putting on because it's really bad, and you don't want it to get to the pain and crying and all this other stuff. Early. Most people don't come in for a diaper rash until it's really bad, and always when they have a diaper rash, I'm prescribing it in a. Even if it didn't start off as a fungal infection, it's getting breakdown, and it almost always creates a fungal infection.
pearls.speaker: Santillano

pearls.text: Colace (docusate) is a cost-effective stool softener for patients starting opioids or iron; 120 tablets for $4.
pearls.verbatim: Colace, you can see that you can get, like, a 120 of a weight Colace for, I think, $4. So you can treat a lot more days.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Santillano on OTC tips

And go to Epcid for over two just to try to help those micronutrients that they're not absorbing well with.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Santillano on OTC tips

pearls.text: Benadryl overuse for insomnia may increase Alzheimer's risk; use at recommended doses.
pearls.verbatim: I don't know long term if you take Benadryl overdose if there's any, like, long term ramifications. I know that they've populated that maybe there's a higher incidence of Alzheimer's, which I think is enough.
pearls.speaker: Santillano
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Santillano on OTC tips

pearls.text: For unspecified anxiety, use ICD-10 code F41.9 rather than GAD (F41.1) if the diagnosis is uncertain, because GAD is a specific diagnosis that is hard to remove from the problem list.
pearls.verbatim: if you are not sure, I would rather you put F41.9 than put GAD. Because GAD is a very specific diagnosis. And once it's there, it's hard to take out of someone's mind.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: Acute stress disorder can be triggered by hearing about a life-threatening event in a friend or family member for adults, but PTSD requires direct exposure or witnessing.
pearls.verbatim: acute stress disorder, the the gait is wider than with PTSD. It's not only a timeline difference, but it's a wider gait. So, like, hearing about a friend or family who survived or who was in a very, like, life threatening car wreck or something can also trigger an acute stress disorder according to DSM. But for adults, that wouldn't be sufficient for PTSD diagnosis.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: In the first encounter for anxiety, the essential steps are to assess safety (suicidality, environmental threats) and rule out medical causes (e.g., heart attack, thyroid issues).
pearls.verbatim: What is essential? In that first appointment, What do you need to do? And, like, you need to check-in that first encounter when they present with anxiety. What's essential? Are they gonna hurt themselves? Are they safe? Are they gonna hurt themselves? Yeah. And I would say, are they safe? Because, also, there may be something threatening in their environment. So are they safe? Are they gonna hurt themselves? Are they at risk for someone else or some factor in their lives? And Uh-huh. Not to be silly, but, you know, also, are their vitals stable? Like, is this Yes. A little thing where they feel anxious, but they're having a heart attack? Yes. Are they actually sick? Yeah. We have to rule out any medical cause.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: Use the PC-PTSD-5 screener (5 items) early in differential; a score of 3 is positive for women, 4 for men in VA primary care samples.
pearls.verbatim: I would really look at a PTSD screener, which is a five item. It's called the PC PTSD five screener. A three is considered positive, especially for women. In VA samples, when primary care, four, they found for men had a better balance between sensitivity and specificity.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: Clonidine is not first-line for panic; avoid using it early in treatment.
pearls.verbatim: First of all, clonidine is not first line for panic, by the way. Alright. Just heads up.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: When a patient avoids medications due to perceived side effects (e.g., decreased libido), consider joining their narrative—like starting testosterone—and maximize its benefits rather than fighting it.
pearls.verbatim: So you as a clinician now have to make a choice. His story seems to be around testosterone. Whether that is accurate, like, actually gonna be his biggest bang for buck on initial treatment. That is his story, or at least he's behaving into that story.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: When a patient is on testosterone replacement and reports panic at the end of the cycle, consider lifestyle factors (exercise, diet) and maximize the treatment's benefits rather than adding new meds.
pearls.verbatim: I just think about lifestyle things too. Like, is he exercising? What's his diet like? Yes. Those do affect your hormones. Yes. So I think that would be a really good strategic clinical approach.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: On an IT exam, CBT is always the answer for behavioral medicine questions because it is a countable, evidence-based therapy.
pearls.verbatim: On an on an IT exam, what is always the answer for behavioral med stuff? CBT.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Adjustment, Anxiety, and Panic Differentials 10/9/25

pearls.text: Use the VA Whole Health infographics to visually map the areas of life that may impact a patient's experience of pain.
pearls.verbatim: The VA has this concept called whole health, the whole health approach in self management of pain. And their whole health materials actually map out in a couple of different infographics. These are the areas of life that may impact your experience pain
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: Voltaren gel is a safe topical NSAID that works for pain without causing heart attack, stroke, or kidney failure.
pearls.verbatim: Voltaren gel actually does work here. And it's not gonna cause you to have a heart attack or stroke and kidney failure.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: Avoid explaining pain purely through a biomedical model, as it can disempower patients by implying they have no control; instead, use pain neuroscience education to frame pain functionally.
pearls.verbatim: if we just explain it from a biomedical model, if we just explain it through anatomy, just explain it in that way, it can actually, like, be counterproductive in terms of their evaluation of ability to do life around their pain.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: If a patient has adopted the spoon theory as an identity (e.g., 'spoonie'), gently probe by asking how they evaluate their spoons each day to restore flexibility.
pearls.verbatim: I probably wouldn't directly go after it. Right. But I'd be like, oh, so when you think about how many spoons are left, how do you evaluate that?
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: Use the chronic pain values inventory to ask patients what they would be willing to endure pain for in order to achieve what matters most.
pearls.verbatim: The quality of life scale for chronic pain, the chronic pain values inventory, it kinda tape... Ties together, like, what is most important to you in managing What would you be willing... If you're here and it's, like, painful ahead of you, if you have to walk across, like, painful ground ahead of you to get to something you really care about, what would be worth going across that?
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: Use the adapted illness intrusiveness scale to assess how pain intrudes on the patient's life.
pearls.verbatim: Adapted illness intrusiveness is probably... I mean, it's it's been adapted in a lot of places. She's got a lot of specialty centers, but it's just saying how is life intruded or how is pain intruding on your life.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: Use templates like flare-up plans and goal setting worksheets to structure pain management.
pearls.verbatim: There are templates, things like flare up plans and goal setting worksheets.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: Refer to the VA brochure on communicating about chronic pain as a guide for physicians.
pearls.verbatim: the communicating about chronic pain, if you're struggling to talk to patients, that, like, brochure, that three to five page explanation is a great guide for physicians.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Chronic Pain

pearls.text: Consider an anxiety/adjustment disorder before using somatic symptom disorder; addressing underlying anxiety can often resolve health-focused concerns.
pearls.verbatim: I'm cautious about using the somatic symptom disorder unless I really have to. ...if we can kind of address the anxiety and address the health concern...
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Conversion Disorder

pearls.text: Antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs do not exclude a patient from needing a hematuria workup.
pearls.verbatim: Antiplatelet, anticoagulant drugs do not exclude you from working up somebody who has hematuria. Do not shock up the fact, oh, I pee blood well. He's just on Coumadin. It's fine. That's... Don't do that.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: If hematuria resolves with UTI treatment, repeat urinalysis after treatment to check for persistent microscopic hematuria.
pearls.verbatim: If somebody has gross hematuria, their hematuria goes away after treatment, it should be retested to see if they have persistent microscopic hematuria.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Recurrent UTIs can be a presentation of bladder cancer; consider referral if infections persist.
pearls.verbatim: It is extremely common for us to get a patient who's been treated for urinary tract infections for years. They now have muscle invasive bladder cancer because it was their bladder cancer.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: If a female patient has negative culture but persistent microscopic hematuria after UTI treatment, refer to urology.
pearls.verbatim: If you have a negative culture but hematuria, that should be referred over.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: When a patient presents with urinary symptoms, a DRE is a diagnostic test, not a screening test for prostate cancer.
pearls.verbatim: When somebody comes in and starts complaining about urinary symptoms, a digital rectal exam is no longer a screening test for prostate cancer.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Always counsel patients about retrograde ejaculation before starting Flomax; otherwise they will call in distress.
pearls.verbatim: If you do not talk to them about it, the vasculitum will call your office afterward and say, you broke me. What the going on? Tell them it's gonna happen. Ensure them that orgasm still feels the same.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Finasteride has a 20% risk of significant, sometimes irreversible sexual dysfunction; avoid it in sexually active men.
pearls.verbatim: about twenty percent of men who take these medications will have significant and sometimes irreversible sexual dysfunction, okay? So if you tell a guy that there's a one in five chance, and he's 55 years old that he will have significant and sometimes irreversible sexual dysfunction if you take this medication, they will not take it.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: When first-line prostate-targeted therapy fails, consider bladder overactivity rather than assuming prostate disease is the sole cause.
pearls.verbatim: I tend to target the prostate first. And if I don't get anywhere with targeting the prostate gland with those medications we just discussed, I start to think about bladder overactivity.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Even with a normal MRI, prostate biopsy is still warranted because about 20% of clinically significant cancers are missed.
pearls.verbatim: We will biopsy patients with normal MRI because this is about twenty percent of clinically significant prostate cancers.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: For men aged 55-70, check PSA only if they have urinary symptoms or a family history of prostate cancer; otherwise, do not check it.
pearls.verbatim: if they're of the age 55 to 70 and they're having some sort of urinary symptoms, I check it. Perfect. If not, or they don't have any family history of it Perfect. We don't even look at it.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Do not treat asymptomatic bacteriuria in non-pregnant elderly women; only treat if symptoms develop.
pearls.verbatim: We try not to treat asymptomatic bacteriuria in aging women. Okay? So if somebody has, like, if somebody's coming in and has no urinary symptoms and has E. Coli in their urine, unless they're pregnant and they're not having symptoms, I would not treat that.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Recurrent UTIs in young girls are almost always due to constipation and holding urine; address toileting habits and bowel regularity.
pearls.verbatim: the biggest one, especially in kids that you guys are gonna see, little girls who have recurrent urinary tract infection, it's almost always because they're not pooping, and they're not sitting to pee. They're just holding their urine all day long.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: For a symptomatic UTI with dirty urine (nitrate positive), start empiric Macrobid without waiting for culture; finish the course once culture returns.
pearls.verbatim: if you get a really dirty urine that's nitrate positive and all that other stuff, then I'll start them on Macrobid. And I'll put them on five days of Macrobid. And then by the time they get the culture back, the cultural desensitization and Macrobid, finish your course, and you're done.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Macrobid does not penetrate tissue and should not be used to treat pyelonephritis; for flank pain or fevers, use a tissue-penetrating antibiotic like Cipro, Bactrim, or Augmentin.
pearls.verbatim: Macrobid does not penetrate tissue. It is a urinary antibiotic. It does not treat pyelonephritis. If you have somebody who's getting flank pain or a female that's having a lot of problems and having fevers and stuff like that, put them on something Cipro, Bactrim, any... Augmentin, all of them penetrates tissue.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Patients with recurrent UTIs do not need three positive cultures before urology referral; refer if they are miserable or feel antibiotics are ineffective.
pearls.verbatim: You do not have to have three positive cultures. If you have a patient who is saying, I am completely miserable. I feel like I an ear or chest infection all the time. This is really driving me crazy. I take antibiotics. Nothing happens. Send them over to us.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: For pediatric UTI in an uncircumcised male under 6 months with febrile UTI, refer to urology for ultrasound and workup.
pearls.verbatim: If an uncircumcised male has a UTI and he's, you know, a febrile UTI and he's six months old, yeah, that patient could probably come over see us. We can get an ultrasound and and work them up and everything like that.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: For pediatric female UTIs, there is no strict threshold for referral; use clinical judgment.
pearls.verbatim: for females, you know, whatever you're comfortable with.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: 50% of patients with ectopic pregnancy have no identifiable risk factors, so do not let it drop off your differential.
pearls.verbatim: fifty percent of patients who end up with an ectopic pregnancy have no risk factor. So don't let it drop off your differential if somebody's not, like, walking in with a classic set of risk factors.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: In a normal intrauterine pregnancy, hCG should increase by one-third to one-half over 48 hours; a slower rise (~25%) suggests ectopic.
pearls.verbatim: If there's a living child and the HCG is going up, we would expect it to increase by a third or a half ED forty eight hours. And there's kind of like a leveling off of the curve as it goes. So, like, if you start at a high HCG, maybe you're seeing them at a later gestational age, that's more like a third increase. If it's earlier, it's more like a half increase. But if somebody's got an ectopic pregnancy, you'll see maybe a 25% increase in their HCG ED two days.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Expectant management of ectopic pregnancy is only appropriate for asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic patients with low hCG who can reliably follow up and understand warning signs.
pearls.verbatim: If they're stable, then you have a little bit more time, and this gets to to Sarah's question. So I was, again, surprised, and I had not heard much about the possibility of just expect who have an ectopic pregnancy. So in the literature, it's one where you wanna be very selective about people who are asymptomatic with it or minimally symptomatic. ... The key thing is that low HCG that we talked about. That's gonna tell you the the likelihood that this is favorable in terms of watching carefully. Then you're gonna wanna counsel them. Sarah, that's what you're saying. Like, you just wanna tell them and make sure this patient is someone who can understand you and can follow-up you or can get themselves to the ED if happens.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: After treating ectopic pregnancy, trend hCG all the way to zero to ensure no persistent trophoblastic tissue remains.
pearls.verbatim: Just keeping an eye on folks and making sure you trend the HCG all the way down to zero when you treat an ectopic pregnancy because if you miss the fact that there's one that's ongoing because you stopped watching it, then that's gonna be troublesome.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Always obtain Rh factor in ectopic pregnancy management to prevent alloimmunization.
pearls.verbatim: Get your Rh factors that you can prevent alloimmunization.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: In Oklahoma, non-OB/GYN physicians should avoid treating ectopic pregnancy surgically because state law may classify it as homicide; refer to OB/GYN.
pearls.verbatim: Anything that they categorize as an abortion is a homicide if you're not licensed and boarded an OB/GYN. So better have the OB/GYN doctors do it and figure out the gray area than be fighting a homicide case.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Use nitrazine test to detect basic pH of amniotic fluid (turns blue) compared to acidic vaginal pH.
pearls.verbatim: the pH of normal vaginal fluid, if I remember correctly, is acidic. It's more on, like, the threes, fours, and the pH of amniotic fluid is more like sevens or so.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Use no lubricant on the speculum during examination for PROM to avoid false results on AmniSure test.
pearls.verbatim: No lube. Because if we were gonna get the amnestyure test subsequently to try to confirm the diagnosis, we didn't wanna have this interfere.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Administer magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection when delivering preterm to reduce the risk of cerebral palsy.
pearls.verbatim: They found that the relative risk of cerebral palsy is, like, way lower if you give MAG at the right time.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: For PPROM at 20–23 weeks, give a single dose of azithromycin and then a course of oral amoxicillin.
pearls.verbatim: we gave her a onetime dose of azithromycin, and then we sent her home on a course of amoxicillin.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Avoid Augmentin (amoxicillin-clavulanate) in PPROM because clavulanate increases the risk of necrotizing enterocolitis in the neonate.
pearls.verbatim: They recommend against the clavulanate part, so don't give the Augmentin brand because the clavulanate increases the risk of necrotizing enterocolitis once you are born as a baby.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: At 22–24 weeks, give IV antibiotics for two days then transition to oral to complete a total of seven days; no benefit if extended beyond seven days.
pearls.verbatim: if you're in the zone of 22 to 24, you for sure give antibiotics... you get into IV antibiotics times two days, and then you can transition to PO times five days if you want. But it's seven days of antibiotics. Does not show any benefit if you extend past seven days, so it's just one week of antibiotics.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Steroids are only indicated if delivery is expected within seven days; they may be considered starting at 22–23 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: steroids aren't only gonna be if you think delivery is gonna happen in less than seven days.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Tocolytics should only be used for transport to a higher-level NICU or to allow a single dose of steroids, as they only delay delivery 48 hours and increase infection risk.
pearls.verbatim: the tocolytics show a decrease in delivery, but only over the next forty eight hours. And they show an increased risk of infection.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: At term (≥37 weeks) with PROM, you can offer expectant management for 12–24 hours, then induction to avoid infection.
pearls.verbatim: if the lady comes in at 37 or beyond and she's ruptured, but she's not in labor, it's just prom. ... you can give her some time for expected management, usually twelve to twenty four hours. At that point, the risk of infection starts to outweigh the risk of induction.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Obtain all four type 1 diabetes autoantibodies (GAD, IA-2, ICA, ZnT8) when suspecting the diagnosis; do not rely only on GAD.
pearls.verbatim: I would encourage you when you're thinking about type one diabetes to obtain all of the antibodies and not just the GAD because it could be any one of them.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: When interpreting C-peptide, always obtain a simultaneous glucose level; a C-peptide of 0.3 with a glucose of 80 indicates type 1 diabetes.
pearls.verbatim: If you have someone... Let's say you're in the hospital testing someone for pancreatic function, and their glucose is 80, and they come back with a C peptide of 0.3, you've got type one diabetes.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Always order a glucose level with the C-peptide; you cannot interpret C-peptide alone.
pearls.verbatim: To get a glucose with that C peptide. You cannot just look into C peptide and send your diagnosis. You need to know where the person is, so it must be in... Or glucose dose... Glucose level with the C peptide.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Do not rely on C-peptide to determine diabetes type when blood sugars are very high, as glucotoxicity artificially lowers C-peptide.
pearls.verbatim: when your blood sugars are very high for whatever the reason, C peptide can be artificially low, and you don't wanna use it in an uncontrolled state to determine the type of diabetes you have.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: When in doubt about diabetes type, start at least basal insulin to control glucose and determine the diagnosis later.
pearls.verbatim: When in doubt, always start insulin, at least basal insulin for these patients, and figure it out on the back end.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Screen patients with autoimmune diseases (celiac, hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism) for type 1 diabetes antibodies, as they are at higher risk.
pearls.verbatim: anybody with autoimmune problems, celiac, hypothyroid, hyperthyroid can be tested for antibodies because they are at higher risk developing type one diabetes.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Screen for presymptomatic type 1 diabetes by checking islet autoantibodies in patients with a family history of type 1 diabetes, thyroid disease, or celiac disease.
pearls.verbatim: Anybody with a family member of type one diabetes, any type of thyroid disorder, whether its hypo or hyperthyroidism count and celiac disorder.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: When assessing for insulin deficiency, check a C-peptide level with a concurrent glucose in the 100–200 mg/dL range; avoid checking when glucose is markedly elevated.

pearls.text: When evaluating COPD, always get a chest X-ray to look for alternative diagnoses such as CHF, bronchiectasis, or interstitial lung disease, even though it is not required by GOLD.

pearls.text: A history of a recent large fatty meal or dehydration can precipitate a gout flare within 24–48 hours.

pearls.text: Thiazide and loop diuretics are common drug triggers for gout flares; consider holding them during acute episodes.

pearls.verbatim: If they have gout and they're already been on, like, an HCTZ, just for blood pressure change, Switch him over to an ACE or an ARB, preferably losartan. Losartan has been proven actually to lower your rate.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout
