pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Use the Canadian Syncope Risk Score on MD Calc to identify low-risk patients (only 1% adverse events at 30 days in low-risk group).
pearls.verbatim: Canadian risk score. It's on your MD calc if you pull it up. But it's extremely helpful. They did a study on 2,200 adults, and then 1,400 classified as low risk using this calculator, and only one percent of them had a significant clinical required procedure at thirty days.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: For patients with normal weight obesity (BMI 24 but >30% body fat), the cardiometabolic risk is similar to traditional obesity; consider body composition assessment even if BMI is not elevated.
pearls.verbatim: if a patient comes in with a BMI of twenty four, now we're not doing body composition on them, but hopefully one day we will. But if they present with, like, greater than 30% of body fat, that phenotype is just as a similar risk of a traditional obesity cardiometabolic disease.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: When patients on GLP-1s consume very low calories (e.g., 500 kcal/day), they are at high risk of losing lean body mass because the body will use amino acids from muscle for gluconeogenesis to supply glucose-dependent tissues like the brain.
pearls.verbatim: I had a 74 year old female come in, just recently got placed on a set bound, and she was only consuming about 500 calories a day. She's 74. Right? So we wanna be concerned for that.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: For patients with lower BMI (e.g., 27) starting GLP-1s, they have less fat tissue to draw from, so they are more prone to losing lean body mass; assess baseline body composition before prescribing.
pearls.verbatim: in regards to people that are lower BMI, that they don't have as much fat tissue, they're more prone to losing lean body mass.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Collagen protein is low in leucine, a key amino acid for turning on muscle protein synthesis; advise patients using protein shakes to avoid collagen as their main source and choose higher-quality proteins.
pearls.verbatim: if somebody's doing, like, collagen protein, then they can do that per hair skin cells if they want to, but that may not... That that may be their their main protein source because collagen and other sources of proteins could be low in leucine, and that's not optimal.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Protein shakes like Ensure Plus and Ensure Complete are poor choices because they are high in sugar and low in protein (13 g); recommend options like Fairlife protein (150-160 kcal, 30 g protein, minimal sugar/carbs/fat).
pearls.verbatim: a lot of the protein shakes that patients typically go to are junk, like Insure Plus, Insure Complete, full of sugar, 13 grams of protein, the list. Yeah. So all those are junk. So, like... So so certain protein shakes like fair light protein, they're at 150 calories, 160, 30 grams of protein, minimal sugar, minimal carbs, minimal fat, Premier popular.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Dose protein at 1.2-1.6 g/kg of ideal body weight (up to 2 g/kg), not actual body weight, to avoid overfeeding fat tissue; use ideal body weight to feed lean mass.
pearls.verbatim: if somebody is... Okay. Here. Here. Person a has seventy five kilos. The BMI of twenty three. Person b is a hundred and twenty five kilos. The BMI of thirty nine. Obviously, I'm not gonna dose one point two to one point six up to two grams of their actual body weight. You're gonna be giving them way too much protein to take. We wanna feed their lean body mass.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: When using the plate method, first choose a lean protein source (e.g., 3-4 oz chicken breast = ~21-28 g protein), then add a low-carb vegetable for fiber, and optionally a healthy fat; this promotes satiety and reduces hyperpalatable food intake.
pearls.verbatim: when you sit down for breakfast, for lunch, for dinner, choose. What is your lean protein? Roughly, try to get at least 20 grams, ideally 25 to 30 grams of protein coming from.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Use the 5/20% rule when reading food labels: 5% or less of the Daily Value for a nutrient is low, 20% or more is high. This applies particularly to fiber, sugar, and sodium.
pearls.verbatim: I think that's the five the 5/20% rule. If you can remember that, that's quick and easy. Just look at the 5% low, 20% high, and the ingredients that go in decent order.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: The 25 modifier tells insurance that the E&M is separate and significant from the other service; it always goes on the E&M code.
pearls.verbatim: 25 modifier is actually telling insurance that the e and m is separate and significant from whatever else it is that you're billing. So that's why it always goes on that e and m.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: For the Welcome to Medicare visit, visual acuity screening is required; the ad hoc form should not give the patient an option to skip unless they refuse.
pearls.verbatim: The main difference between this one and the other two is that this one does require a visual acuity screening. That is probably the biggest missed thing on this one.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: If a patient cannot complete the health risk assessment in the office, send it home with them and schedule another visit; do not submit charges until all components are done.
pearls.verbatim: I would just say, well, I'm gonna schedule you out for another visit. You bring that form back with you to the next visit, and we can bill you for a Medicare wellness at that time.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: Maintain blood glucose between 40–180 mg/dL in acute stroke.
pearls.verbatim: What's our goal range? 40 to one eighty.
pearls.speaker: Whitaker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Whitaker on CVA Management

pearls.text: Standard head-of-bed elevation for stroke patients is 30 degrees.
pearls.verbatim: Standard of care is the head of bed at 30 degrees.
pearls.speaker: Whitaker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Whitaker on CVA Management

pearls.text: Prescribe a high-intensity statin prior to discharge.
pearls.verbatim: High intensity statin prior to discharge.
pearls.speaker: Whitaker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Whitaker on CVA Management

pearls.text: Avoid hydralazine for acute BP control because it can cause an unpredictable rapid drop.
pearls.verbatim: I don't love hydralazine because it can really drop you quick.
pearls.speaker: Whitaker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Whitaker on CVA Management

pearls.text: For cryptogenic strokes, consider a 30-day event monitor (MCOT) to detect occult atrial fibrillation.
pearls.verbatim: consider a thirty day event monitor or MCOT
pearls.speaker: Whitaker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Whitaker on CVA Management

pearls.text: Tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and azathioprine are major immunosuppressants that increase skin cancer risk, especially squamous cell carcinoma.
pearls.verbatim: tacrolimus or prograf, cellcept, mycophenolate, those are your bigger offenders, really increase their risk.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation carriers have increased melanoma risk and should have an annual skin check.
pearls.verbatim: If they are BRCA one or two positive, their risk of melanoma goes up. So they should probably be getting an annual skin check.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: A lesion described as a 'spider bite' or 'wasp sting' that persists for months or years is almost always a skin cancer, not an insect bite.
pearls.verbatim: I cannot tell you how many people have had a spider bite that has been there for two years. It was a thing. Never a spider bite. I had a lady tell me that she had a wasp sting her on her cheek four years ago. Not a wasp. It's a skin cancer.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: A solitary scaly patch on the leg that does not respond to clobetasol should be biopsied to rule out squamous cell carcinoma in situ.
pearls.verbatim: I have seen a not insignificant number of squamous cell carcinoma carcinoma in situ that people will be like, that's just my patch of psoriasis, but it doesn't go away with clobetasol. And it's like, if you have someone who has one patch of psoriasis on their leg, I don't think of psoriasis. I will always biopsy it.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Do not trust a negative margin on a biopsy; margins are only reliable when the lesion is excised completely and processed for margins.
pearls.verbatim: So that's why I would not trust your unless you are doing it as an excision. Because if you do it as an excision, they will process the tissue differently to give you margins.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: For melanoma, always perform a broad shave biopsy rather than a punch biopsy to avoid missing invasive components that may be present in different parts of the lesion.
pearls.verbatim: broad shaves are preferred for sure for melanoma. So this is where you can get a false diagnosis if you punch a melanoma or a mole that looks weird Because part of it may be a melanoma in situ, like, just kinda skating along the epidermal dermal junction where this part over here was invasive, and that's where you're gonna get your res load up.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: For pregnant patients with suspected melanoma, use lidocaine without epinephrine to avoid theoretical placental vasoconstriction.
pearls.verbatim: Use lido without epi, and that's really all you have to do.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: For squamous cell carcinoma, take a generous biopsy because they can 'blow right back up' after biopsy or bleed persistently if not enough tissue is removed.
pearls.verbatim: the squamous just... I've I've had them... They'll just, like, blow right back up after you biopsy them if you don't get a lot of it out, or they'll just sit there and bleed.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: If unsure about a lesion, take a shallow biopsy to avoid a bad scar; it's okay to refer if the procedure seems too complex.
pearls.verbatim: if you're not sure, I would take a shallow biopsy because then they're gonna have, like, a bad score. Right. Right. So... And that's where if you're like, that sounds like too much. I'm not dealing with that. It's really okay.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: For ED&C, never use it on the head or neck; only use it on low-risk areas like arms or back for small lesions (1 cm or under).
pearls.verbatim: I never do it head and neck ever. Anywhere that's a high risk area, I'll never do it. So if it's like an arm, a back, it's like a real small one, I'll do those.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Always warn male patients about priapism when prescribing trazodone for insomnia.
pearls.verbatim: What's a very unfortunate side effect of trazodone? Priapism. So I always warn my male patients about that.
pearls.speaker: Williston
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williston on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Sleep terrors occur in non-REM sleep; children do not remember them. Treatment is reassurance for parents and ensuring a safe sleep environment — no harm to the child.
pearls.verbatim: The treatment is really reassuring the parents harming the kids. It can be very disruptive to the whole family.
pearls.speaker: Williston
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williston on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: CPAP is the most effective treatment for OSA, recommended in conjunction with weight loss and alcohol avoidance. For CPAP-intolerant patients, refer to ENT and consider the Inspire hypoglossal nerve stimulator.
pearls.verbatim: CPAP is the most effective treatment for obstructive sleep apnea, and it's recommended in conjunction with weight loss.
pearls.speaker: Williston
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williston on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Avoid sleep studies in patients with chronic insomnia unless there are symptoms of an actual sleep disorder (Choosing Wisely).
pearls.verbatim: avoid sleep studies in patients with chronic insomnia unless they have actually symptoms of an actual sleep disorder.
pearls.speaker: Williston
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williston on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: For patients with chronic insomnia who fail nonpharmacologic measures, limit hypnotic use to no more than twice weekly to reduce dependence risk.
pearls.verbatim: I will give them hypnotics and tell them don't take it any more often than twice a week.
pearls.speaker: Williston
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williston on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: If you lie in bed for 30 minutes and are not asleep, get out of bed to avoid conditioning the bed as a place for wakefulness.
pearls.verbatim: if you lay in bed for thirty minutes and you're not asleep, get out of your bed.
pearls.speaker: Williston
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williston on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Driving drowsy is as dangerous as driving drunk; if nodding off, do not drive.
pearls.verbatim: driving drowsy is just as dangerous as driving drunk.
pearls.speaker: Williston
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williston on Sleep Disorders

pearls.text: Protozoa like amoebas, Giardia, and malaria do not have a tissue migratory phase and therefore are not likely to cause eosinophilia.
pearls.verbatim: protozoa in general, these don't have, like, a tissue migratory phase, and so these are also not likely to cause eosinophilia.
pearls.speaker: Winters
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Winters on Malawi & Parasites 5/14/26

pearls.text: Schistosomiasis cercariae penetrate intact skin painlessly in as little as 3–5 minutes; a cut on the leg does not increase transmission.
pearls.verbatim: It's painless. It can happen in, like, three to five minutes. If you have, like, a cut on your leg or something, it doesn't actually, like, increase the transmission. They penetrate intact skin.
pearls.speaker: Winters
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Winters on Malawi & Parasites 5/14/26

pearls.text: Praziquantel is only effective against adult schistosome worms, so if given a week after exposure it will not stop the life cycle; wait 4–6 weeks after exposure to treat.
pearls.verbatim: it's only against, like, adults. So you're not going to... If you give it, let's say, a week after exposure, it's not gonna stop the life cycle process. You have to give it four to six weeks after exposure.
pearls.speaker: Winters
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Winters on Malawi & Parasites 5/14/26

pearls.text: For invasive Entamoeba histolytica (tissue-active), use metronidazole; for luminal cysts, use paromomycin.
pearls.verbatim: Metronidazole is first line choice. When it's luminol, so the cysts are just in the intestine, it will be like paromomycin.
pearls.speaker: Winters
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Winters on Malawi & Parasites 5/14/26

pearls.text: The transition from lethargic to stuporous is dangerous because the patient loses protective reflexes and the ability to communicate symptoms like chest pain.

So then history then becomes much more sensitive, and we can't better assess how they're actually feeling. We can't discern what's going on, localize where the problem is. Are you having chest pain? Yes. Correct. They can't communicate their problem. And then, also, they can't follow commands. So, hey. Sit up. Cough your secretions out. Hey. Open your mouth. Those things are starting to diminish. So that's why they become dangerous because those protective reflexes are are gone. Their ability to communicate is diminishing.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Patients with preexisting structural brain issues (dementia, prior stroke, TBI, Parkinson's) are more susceptible to delirium; the weakest link in the chain breaks first.
pearls.verbatim: I'll tell you that those with preexisting structural brain issues will be more susceptible to delirium and mental status decline when ill. And a attending of mine always told me that the weakest link in the chain is the first to break. So if they have cognitive impairment from just diffuse cortical dementia, that's the thing that falls apart first.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: To prevent and manage delirium, keep patients out of bed and in a chair during the day, turn lights on, ensure they have their glasses and hearing aids, and maintain day-night orientation.
pearls.verbatim: When you walk in a room during the daylight, the lights on or off often? Off. Is that good for a delirious? No. No. K. When you walk in, is that person laid up in bed, or are they out in the chair usually? Mobility. Sitting in the dark all day. Are they often... We're we're taking care of mostly the elderly. The elderly have different with vision, the difficulties with vision. Are they wearing their glasses or their hearing aids? It's like being a prisoner of your own body. Does that make sense? So it's no wonder why they're delirious. So if... When I leave, I need you guys to actually be advocates for delirium medication. You gotta be getting your patients up. It's gotta flip on during the day. Gotta keep them day and night set.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Correcting the underlying metabolic disturbance does not immediately reverse delirium; consistent daily management is required, especially in the delirium-prone brain.
pearls.verbatim: If you correct the disturbance, you can often correct the problem, but it's very hard, especially with the delirium prone brain, just fix it. It doesn't just switch off like a light switch. You gotta dig your heel in and make it more consistent every single day.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

So an artery of Percheron stroke happens. This is normal basilar anatomy, but you can have various anatomy. So basilar splits to the posterior cerebral

pearls.verbatim: If you have any of these variants in which the bilateral thalami, medial thalami specifically, are perfused off of one offshoot that branches. If you block that artery, what happens to both of the medial thalami? I actually had one of these last week. It is devastating. The medial thalami is specifically mostly responsible for consciousness. So this dude is in a coma for probably the next few years.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: A blown pupil in an awake patient is not due to uncal herniation; consider ipratropium, scopolamine patches, or trauma as causes.
pearls.verbatim: Remember that this is a sign of increased intracranial pressure. Thus, if that patient is awake talking to you, they're not herniating.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Forced gaze deviation: if eyes look away from the flaccid side, it's a stroke; if towards the flaccid side, it's a seizure.
pearls.verbatim: If they are looking away from the plegic side, so flaccid right looking away, the stroke. If it's looking towards the flaccid side, they're having a sezure.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Implement delium precautions by writing a nursing PAL task every 6-12 hours: lights on during day, patient out of bed, fed, glasses/hearing aids on; at night, lights and TV off, hold nonemergency care.
pearls.verbatim: I've gone as far as to write a nursing PAL task that appears every six to twelve hours. It says during the day, lights must be on. The patient must be out of bed. They must be fed. Glasses, hearing aids on. At night, lights go off. TV goes off. Hold care overnight unless it's an emergency, obviusly.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: A normal echo does not rule out cardiac involvement in metastatic NET; infiltrative cardiomyopathy may only be visible on PET scan.
pearls.verbatim: He probably had a malignant NETs on the heart that we just cannot see on an echo it's all just myocardium and pericardium on an echo. Until you do a PET scan, you're like, that's pericardium.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For neuroendocrine tumors, monitor response to octreotide therapy with chromogranin levels as an objective measure.
pearls.verbatim: they started to do octreotide monthly, and then we're tracking chromogranin levels as the objective measure to see, is this person responding to our therapy?
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: When a patient has metastatic cancer and no curative options, have an honest goals-of-care discussion and offer hospice; avoid wishy-washy warnings.
pearls.verbatim: You never want to be wishy washy with your warnings.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Most neuroendocrine tumors are diagnosed incidentally when an appendix is sent to pathology; always send surgical specimens for histology.
pearls.verbatim: most neuroendocrine tumors are diagnosed when someone gets an appendectomy incidentally, and the appendix goes out to pathology.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: In outpatient evaluation of flushing and diarrhea, rule out common causes like menopause, thyroid disease, asthma, IBS, serotonin syndrome, and endocarditis before considering carcinoid.
pearls.verbatim: Rule out things like menopause. I mean, this guy's a male, so that's ruled out. Things like thyroid disease. Everything that you guys talked about earlier. Do they have asthma? Right? Yeah. Do they have gastroenteritis?
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Obtain a CT of the abdomen and pelvis for suspected neuroendocrine tumors because most are colonic in origin.
pearls.verbatim: Get a CT of the abdomen and pelvis because most neuroendocrine tumors are colonic in origin.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: 17% of patients with neuroendocrine tumors have a second primary malignancy (not metastasis); consider this when new lesions appear.
pearls.verbatim: Seventeen percent of people with neuroendocrine tumors have a second primary malignancy, not a secondary lesion from a primary malignancy, but a second primary malignancy.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Second primary malignancies in NET patients are often very aggressive and may determine the patient's prognosis and cause of death.
pearls.verbatim: Second primary malignancies are very aggressive. Right? And so a lot of times when these patients have a secondary primary malignancy, that's what's probably going to kill them.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: If a patient with NET refuses hospice, obtain a PET scan to identify malignant disease for further management.
pearls.verbatim: If you're discharging them and they don't wanna do hospice, get them to do a PET scan.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For carcinoid heart disease, manage with octreotide and diuretics; valve replacement is rarely indicated because tricuspid regurgitation is not the cause of death.
pearls.verbatim: If they have heart disease, put them on octreotide, put them on diuretics, and then this very unlikely to happen. Right? Valveolar nerve replacement.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: For flushing in carcinoid syndrome, advise patients to avoid triggers such as alcohol and use somatostatin analogs.
pearls.verbatim: If they have flushing, tell them to avoid the things that we talked about. Use this alcohol, etcetera. And then, again, somatostatin analogs.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Use bronchodilators for wheezing in patients with carcinoid syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: Think about bronchodilators for your wheezing patients.
pearls.speaker: Yasmin Keefe
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Yasmin Keefe on Coma for the non-Neurologist

pearls.text: Use corrected age (gestational age at birth plus chronological age) to evaluate growth and milestones; a baby born at 34 weeks at 2 months chronological age is developmentally just 1 month old.
pearls.verbatim: So forty weeks gestational age once they are one month older than that. So let's say, Judah, for example, he was born a month early. So once he got to one month chronological age, he was in at 40. So two months chronological age is one month.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Youmans on Preemies in Primary Care

pearls.verbatim: Washing each pump part after each use is... It's a lot of work, but it's a way to help protect them. It's... We can't use what's called a fridge hack. You can't just keep it in the fridge, so it reduces the number of washes.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Youmans on Preemies in Primary Care

pearls.text: If a preemie is not gaining weight well or has a special medical need, refer to a dietitian; if mom struggles with breastfeeding at term age, refer to a lactation consultant.
pearls.verbatim: Dietitians, if baby is not gaining weight well or if they have a special medical need, calling them. Lactation consultants. If mom really wants to have a breastfeeding relationship with this baby and baby is around term ace but we're still having some trouble, definitely call lactation.

pearls.verbatim: The biggest education that we continue to do is that women assume that if they talk about abortion or think about it or go obtain it somewhere else that they're gonna be prosecuted in jail. It's the ban is for the provision of it.

pearls.episode_title: Karen Alley on the Hope Pregnancy Center

pearls.text: For patients on second-generation antipsychotics, monitor BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, A1c, and lipids at baseline and regularly thereafter.
pearls.verbatim: recommendation is that you're following their BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, a one c, lipids. At initial, get baseline, and then Kinda monitoring that.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: For QT prolongation, do not start an antipsychotic if baseline QTc is 450 or higher; during treatment, if QTc exceeds 500 or increases by 60, reduce dose or switch agents.
pearls.verbatim: should not be started in a baseline of four fifty or higher. K. During treatment, you see higher than 500 or an increase of 60 warrants dose reduction or switch to another antipsychotic.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Obtain a baseline ECG for pimozide and IV haloperidol; for other antipsychotics, consider ECG if the patient is already on QT-prolonging medication.
pearls.verbatim: For the others, you'll need a baseline EKG. But if they're already on QT prolonging medication, it might be a good idea.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Clozapine has significant anticholinergic effects that can cause severe, surgically emergent constipation.
pearls.verbatim: has a lot of anticholinergic action, which results in constipation and infection, which can be very severe, like surgically emergent severe.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: For lithium, check levels after 5 days (steady state) following any dose change; once stable, check every 3–6 months.
pearls.verbatim: So any dose change that you're that you're changing over steady state, which is usually five days at least from when you check the change the dose, check a level. And when they're stable on the dose, every three to six months, I'm probably checking.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Lamotrigine titration must be 25 mg for 2 weeks, then 50 mg for 2 weeks, then 100 mg for 2 weeks; if >5 consecutive doses are missed, restart the entire schedule.
pearls.verbatim: The standard one is twenty five milligrams for two weeks, then you can double it fifty for two weeks, then a hundred for two weeks, and then you can go up to two hundred. ... if they meant five consecutive days, you have to start the titration over again.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Lithium is the only drug with evidence reducing suicidality in mood disorders, but its toxicity makes close monitoring essential.
pearls.verbatim: Lithium reduces the risk of suicide. None of the others have really shown that for moon quarters, which is interesting and always makes me nervous because lithium is toxic at high levels.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: When using lithium to augment for monopolar depression, you do not need to push levels to 0.6–1.0; lower doses can be tried first.
pearls.verbatim: Sometimes when I'm augmenting with lithium in a monopolar depression, I'm not necessarily pushing for the point six to 1.0 level. I might just try a sprinkle of lithium.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: In bipolar depression, antidepressants are never used as monotherapy; if used, they must be combined with a second-generation antipsychotic (e.g., fluoxetine plus olanzapine = Symbyax).
pearls.verbatim: Traditionally, antidepressants are not used. If they are used, it's used... It's never monotherapy, but combo therapy with the second generation. For example, Symbiax is FDA approved. It's fluoxetine and olanzapine together.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Use trazodone or mirtazapine (Remeron) first for agitation in dementia before trying antipsychotics.
pearls.verbatim: I try to do a sedating antidepressant first. So like a trazodone or Remeron first.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Avoid paroxetine (Paxil) in dementia because its anticholinergic properties can worsen the condition.
pearls.verbatim: Paxil's has anticholinergic properties, which you don't want in dementia. Anticholinergic stuff will worsen dementia.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Melatonin 3–10 mg may prevent delirium in postoperative patients and is commonly included in admission order sets.
pearls.verbatim: Melatonin has some evidence of prevention, so that's why it's probably on a lot of admission order sets now. ... Three to ten milligrams to the general vaccine.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Antipsychotics help with agitation in delirium but do not make delirium resolve faster; treat the underlying medical cause.
pearls.verbatim: Generally, the antipsychotics don't help delirium or make delirium resolve faster, but it does help with the agitation related to delirium.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: For patients on antipsychotics discharged with unresolved delirium, ensure caregivers know to expect short-term use and plan to taper.
pearls.verbatim: Again, make sure short term use if they're gonna be discharged on it because their delirium's not completely cleared that the caregiver knows.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: For agitation in developmental delay, treat co-occurring anxiety or depression first; antipsychotics are a last resort.
pearls.verbatim: For other kind of potentials of aggression, you might move to an antipsychotic, but it should be, like, an option of last resort because of all the problems there.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Metabolic syndrome from antipsychotics can occur even with controlled calories; consider metformin or switching to a first-generation agent if severe.
pearls.verbatim: But sometimes extent of the metabolic syndrome... I will do metabolic labs like I'm supposed to, and I'll be like, yeah. You have metabolic syndrome, but I can't see you functioning without this. ... trying to switch to the to the different risk of first generation.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Olanzapine is highly effective but causes rapid weight gain; consider lurasidone or ziprasidone as weight-neutral alternatives.
pearls.verbatim: Latuda tends to be better for weight, so I like that one a lot. ... Geodon tends to be good on weight.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Social rhythm therapy—maintaining consistent sleep/wake schedules—is preferred for bipolar disorder to reduce episode risk.
pearls.verbatim: Social rhythm therapy is preferred for bipolar disorder. It's essentially therapy that really focuses on the circadian rhythm and getting them on a very predictable circadian rhythm.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Antipsychotics & Mood Stabilizers

pearls.text: Benzodiazepines are involved in about 30% of prescription drug overdose deaths, often in combination with opioids, which drove increased scrutiny and a decline in prescribing after 2013–2014.
pearls.verbatim: benzodiazepines are involved about thirty percent of prescription drug overdose deaths. In 2013. ... a lot of those fatalities are actually related to co prescribing benzos.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: About 80% of benzodiazepine users obtain the drug from a friend or relative, indicating that most prescriptions are diverted rather than used as intended.
pearls.verbatim: the majority are half friend or relative who has a from a friend or relative. We look at that half. Wow. That about eighty percent are getting it for one.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Oxazepam, lorazepam, and temazepam undergo phase 3 conjugation (glucuronidation) and do not use the cytochrome P450 pathway, making them preferred in patients with liver impairment.
pearls.verbatim: Please note here that phase three conjugation, this is often tested on in ports. You have or alpha amoxifenazepam. They're not using the cytochrome p four fifty pathway. So for those that have liver impairment, this is why you wanna use these because it's bypassing that.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Benzodiazepines should be used for insomnia for only 1–2 weeks and for anxiety for only 4–6 weeks; longer use leads to tolerance and dependence.
pearls.verbatim: Generally, four to six weeks. One to two weeks for sleep, it's... Or you're gonna build up tolerance.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: When starting an SSRI for anxiety, adding a benzodiazepine short-term (4–6 weeks) can be considered, but patients may perceive the SSRI as ineffective because it lacks the immediate subjective effect of the benzodiazepine.
pearls.verbatim: I caution against this because, clinically, this doesn't work very well because once they've had a benzodiazepine, the SSRIs don't feel like that. It can create a situation where SSRI is not working.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Obtain routine drug testing before starting benzodiazepines and intermittently during treatment.
pearls.verbatim: Obtain routine drug testing before starting it intermittently, and consider a controlled substance agreement.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Flumazenil will precipitate benzodiazepine withdrawal, which can be a medical emergency with seizures and death.
pearls.verbatim: Flumazenil will send them into benzodiazepine withdrawal.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: If a patient is on both opioids and benzodiazepines, document why both are needed and mitigate risks.
pearls.verbatim: If you have both, make sure you're documenting why they're on both, and you've done everything to mitigate the risk of being on both.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Benzodiazepine addiction is a risk of taking benzodiazepine; exposure alone is a risk factor for substance use disorder.
pearls.verbatim: benzodiazepine addiction is a risk of taking benzodiazepine. So exposure is the only risk factor you need to develop a substance use disorder.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Physical dependence can occur within two to four weeks of regular benzodiazepine use.
pearls.verbatim: This can happen within two to four weeks of regular use.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Monitor patients for benzodiazepine use disorder by checking for unsanctioned dose escalation, early refills, and inability to cope without medication.
pearls.verbatim: Repeated unsanctioned dose escalations. Like, they kinda went up on their own without discussing it with you. Right? The need of more medication to function normally. Sometimes this is... They might be supplementing with a friend's benzodiazepine. They might be buying it off the street. Unable to cope without medication.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Never prescribe a benzodiazepine without having a long-term plan for it.
pearls.verbatim: Don't ever enter a visudiazepine prescription without having a long term plan for it.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Assess for suicidality during taper and implement safety plans, as tapering itself is a risk factor for increased suicidality.
pearls.verbatim: Increased suicidality, again, be using mid dose as a risk factor. Tapering is also a risk factor, so it's a very uncomfortable time. So you wanna make sure you're assessing and doing safety plans.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Inpatient care is indicated for patients with imminent risk of significant harm from continued benzodiazepine use, such as inability to control use or risk of falls.
pearls.verbatim: Inpatient care should be considered for a patient with imminent risk for significant harm related to continued use of benzodiazepines.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Patients with a history of delirium tremens (DTs) from alcohol are not candidates for outpatient benzodiazepine taper and require medical monitoring.
pearls.verbatim: If they have a history of DTs, then they're no longer outpatient candidate.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Assume management of all benzodiazepine prescriptions for a patient; do not co-prescribe with another provider.
pearls.verbatim: You should assume management of all benzodiazepine prescriptions. Don't be, like, coprescribing with another provider.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Convert and consolidate all benzodiazepine prescriptions to a single longer-acting agent (e.g., diazepam) before starting the taper.
pearls.verbatim: The prescriber should convert and consolidate the medications to an equivalent dose of the single benzodiazepine prior to beginning the taper.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Offer adjunctive psychosocial interventions such as CBT, sleep hygiene, and physical activity to support the taper.
pearls.verbatim: Exjunctive psychosocial interventions should be offered. CBT, lifestyle factors such as sleep hygiene, physical activity.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Alprazolam is more reinforcing and has higher misuse/addiction risk than other benzodiazepines; consider switching to a longer-acting agent.
pearls.verbatim: It's more reinforcing and has a higher risk use of misuse and addiction compared to other.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: For patients on benzodiazepines <12 months at low therapeutic doses, reduce by 25% every 2 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: Been on it less than twelve months. K? They're on the lower therapeutic dose, meaning they're only one to two times the lowest therapeutic dose prescribed. Usually, this is, like, the lowest milligram tab available. K? Then you can reduce by twenty five percent every two weeks.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: For higher therapeutic doses (≥3 times the lowest dose), reduce by 10–25% every 4 weeks; do not exceed 25% every 4 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: If they're on the higher therapeutic dose, so three three times or more the lower therapeutic dose, then reduce the dose by ten to twenty five percent every four weeks. Adjust based on the response, and exceed twenty five percent every four weeks.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Start the first taper reduction gently to maintain patient trust; even if larger cuts are theoretically possible, a dramatic reduction can cause loss of faith.
pearls.verbatim: However, anything more than the lowest dose, by five to twenty percent every consider the lower end of the range for the first reduction. Because even if they could tolerate a higher, you're gonna lose all faith in the taper from your patient if it feels dramatic or they got a lot of symptoms.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Gabapentin has shown clinical success for benzodiazepine withdrawal despite negative studies; it is helpful in alcohol withdrawal and may be used off-label.
pearls.verbatim: I will say I've had success with gabapentin, which I find interesting. Pregabalin has some positive studies, but gabapentin doesn't. So I use gabapentin quite a bit. Gabapentin is shown to be very helpful in alcohol, protracted alcohol withdrawal.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Oral contraceptives may increase glucuronidation metabolism of lorazepam and decrease metabolism of other benzodiazepines, altering drug levels.
pearls.verbatim: Oral contraceptives may increase glucuronidation metabolism lorazepam. It may decrease metabolism of other benzos. So ICPs can change drug levels.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: At low doses, think in percent reduction, not absolute milligrams; a 25% cut from 2 mg to 1.5 mg is significant and may cause withdrawal symptoms.
pearls.verbatim: Even though you're going from two milligrams, PID to one in the morning and two at night, twenty five percent dose reduction. K. That's a lot. Doesn't seem like a lot when you get to these tiny doses, but you really need to think about percent, not overall milligrams.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: Anticipate a six-month taper for long-term benzodiazepine users; water cuts can help with very small dose adjustments at the end.
pearls.verbatim: But if they've been on it for a long time, anticipate a six month taper if you can. When people... You might need to push it, there's other risk factors. And a lot of people will tolerate water cuts.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Benzodiazepines

pearls.text: For melancholic depression, consider moving to ECT or ketamine more quickly if initial treatment fails.
pearls.verbatim: In the literature, we've seen ECT or ketamine might be... You might go to those a little faster.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: For psychotic depression, ECT is first-line; if not available, use a combination antidepressant plus antipsychotic.
pearls.verbatim: ECT tends to be first line for severe psychotic features of depression. If ECT is not an option, a combo antidepressant is better than either of them.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: For patients with hypersomnia, low energy, and weight gain, consider a norepinephrine agent.
pearls.verbatim: For our shutdown patients that, you know, they they have hypersomnia. They're sleeping all the time, low energy fatigue, apathy, psychomotor retardation, weight gain, lack of initiative, I might wanna make sure that norepinephrine agent is on board.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: Avoid anticholinergic agents (e.g., paroxetine, mirtazapine, TCAs) in elderly patients or those with dementia.
pearls.verbatim: If I have our elderly patients or anyone with any kind of early or late dementia, avoid any cholinergic agents for sure.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: Bupropion can be used first-line in patients with anhedonia, ADHD, or weight concerns, but avoid it in patients with prominent anxiety unless the anxiety is driven by motivational deficits.
pearls.verbatim: If they have really anxious features, I'm gonna probably go more serotonergic than Wellbutrin because Wellbutrin is pretty... Can be activating and can make kinda agitation worse. Now I have seen if their anxiety is rooted in the fact that I cannot make myself do anything and all these things are piling up, Wellbutrin can be great for that because it's activating.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: Serotonin syndrome symptoms include agitation, muscle twitching, sweating/fever, dilated pupils, and rapid heart rate; educate patients on these when starting serotonergic agents.
pearls.verbatim: I talked about, like, kind of feeling agitated. They feel like muscle twitches. That tends to be a thing. Sweating or fever, even though they're not really sick. Dilated pupils, rapid heart rate.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: For very anxious patients starting an SSRI, begin at half the usual dose (e.g., Zoloft 25 mg) to minimize initial activation and insomnia.
pearls.verbatim: So for my very agitated patients, I'm gonna start lower than normal. So for Zoloft, I would have just started at twenty five.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: Do not combine two SSRIs or an SSRI with an SNRI unless cross-titrating; augment with a different class to avoid serotonin syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: You would not have an SSRI or SNRI. They're kind of... You could think of the same class, and we don't do two of the same class. Right? So you would augment with something of a different class.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: After a single major depressive episode, the recurrence rate at two years is over 40%; after three episodes, treat for life.
pearls.verbatim: Following a single major depressive episode, the recurrence rate in two years is forty... Over forty percent. Following two major depressive episodes, their five year recurrence rate is seventy five percent. And after three, it's good to treat for life again.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: In severe depression, patients are often cognitively shut down and cannot engage in therapy; start medication first and add therapy once they begin responding.
pearls.verbatim: When they have severe depression, studies show they're not gonna respond well to therapy. They need to go straight to meds. K? So I'm gonna make a stronger recommendation for medication if we're at the severe level. Once they start kinda responding, then they can enter therapy, but it tends not to be super helpful. Right? There's something happening cognitively that they're so shut down that the engagement therapy is not there.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: A safety plan includes: warning signs, safe environments, coping skills, supportive contacts, professional resources, and means restriction — all done collaboratively; no-suicide contracts do not work.
pearls.verbatim: Safety plan is basically the idea that, you know, suicide is kind of on the shelf as an option. Right? To talk to someone who's like, this is not an option. This is... You can't do it. Doesn't tend to work. Didn't work with people. So instead, it's like, okay. So that's that's there. That is an option. That's an option your depression particularly goes to. But instead, let's talk about the things you're gonna do before you consider that option.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: If a patient in the clinic states active suicidal ideation with a plan and intent, immediately call security and 911 for involuntary transport.
pearls.verbatim: If they're in the clinic, they're saying, like, I have, like, I am an active suicidal ideation. I have a plan. I'm going home doing this. Like, you're calling Yeah. I'm calling 911. K. You have security? I call security. Yeah. So we call our security. We call 911.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: Mirtazapine (Remeron) is especially helpful for cannabis withdrawal symptoms.
pearls.verbatim: Now that being said, Remeron has been great for cannabis withdrawal.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: When transitioning from an SSRI to an SNRI, no cross-taper is needed; but going from an SNRI (especially venlafaxine) to an SSRI requires a slow cross-taper over 1-2 weeks to avoid severe discontinuation syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: If you're going from an SSRI to an SNRI, that tends to be pretty smooth. Yeah. The other way, SNRI. With the norepinephrine, noradrenergic side of that, that tends to be really uncomfortable. venlafaxine's the hardest thing to get off of because of the discontinuation syndrome with SNRIs, especially venlafaxine. And so I would have a cross titration period of of at least a week, maybe a couple weeks, where I'm going down on one while I'm starting the other.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: To ease discontinuation from venlafaxine (short half-life), taper down then switch to a week of Prozac (fluoxetine) which self-tapers due to its long half-life.
pearls.verbatim: because Prozac's half life is so long that it kinda self tapers after they've been on... You know, give them a week of it.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.text: For fibromyalgia or chronic pain syndromes, use duloxetine (Cymbalta) first; tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) are second-line due to higher side effects.
pearls.verbatim: Cymbalta tends to be better for chronic pain or pain syndrome. So I usually go with Cymbalta for our kind of pain syndrome type patients.
pearls.speaker: Kelly Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Kelly Dunn, MD on Pharmacotherapy for Depressive Disorders 12/11/25

pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: Pericardial effusion is anechoic (black) compared to blood; epicardial fat pads are more hypoechoic (gray) and fuzzier, so look in multiple views to confirm.

pearls.text: Phenylephrine is rarely used because sick patients usually need some beta support; it is reserved for MAP pushes in spinal cord injury or stroke where the heart is fine.

pearls.text: Dobutamine causes systemic vasodilation and may drop blood pressure; it is often used in cardiogenic shock with hypertension, not hypotension.

pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Dobutamine can worsen tachycardia in atrial fibrillation with RVR; use caution or choose an alternative agent.

pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: A maxed epinephrine drip at 200 mcg/min delivers 0.2 mg/min, compared to 1 mg push in a code; this illustrates the massive dose given during cardiac arrest.

pearls.text: Epinephrine for anaphylaxis is 0.3-0.5 mg IM; giving 0.5 mg IV to a living patient can cause ventricular arrhythmias and is dangerous.

pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For SVC syndrome, if the cancer is lymphoma, small cell lung cancer, or germ cell tumor, start chemotherapy first because these respond faster to systemic therapy than radiation.

pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For grade 2-3 radiation dermatitis with moist desquamation, use dressings like Mepilex or Metahoney to keep the area dry and prevent co-infection.
pearls.verbatim: If it's a grade two or grade three or you see a lot of the moist desquamation, that's when you're thinking about some dressings. There are, again, a plethora to choose from, Mepilex or Metahoney. Like, there's just a ton. But that can help keep that area dry.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Delay PET scan for 2-3 months after radiation to avoid false-positive uptake from treatment-induced inflammation.

pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: PSA monitoring for prostate cancer should begin about 2 months after radiation; an early bump from cell death is expected before the downtrend.

pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Hopelessness talk equals high risk; listen for it and always try to build hope for the future by reorienting the patient to the future.

pearls.text: Hydroxyzine does not give a patient purpose; medication alone is insufficient for addressing loss of meaning.

pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: When experiencing compassion fatigue, even little things will feel like a big thing, so be careful that things don't get out of proportion.
pearls.verbatim: even little things will feel like a big thing
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Use cognitive, affective, and behavioral skills to create relaxation and lower reactivity—this is the essence of self-soothing.
pearls.verbatim: Self soothing involves the ability to use cognitive, affective, and behavioral skills to create relaxation and lowered reactivity.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Do not ask a suicidal patient what they want to do; they are unable to problem-solve, and asking may reinforce their helplessness.
pearls.verbatim: Don't ask them what they wanna do. But what do you wanna do about this? Don't ask them that.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Hardcore suicidal individuals who are truly determined to die will likely give no clues and are invested in not being rescued.
pearls.verbatim: If they are totally intent on killing themselves, they probably aren't gonna give you any clues.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Always ask about family history of suicide; it is a strong warning sign and should prompt careful follow-up with children and relatives.
pearls.verbatim: Has anybody in your family or your extended family ever committed suicide. That's a such a strong sign that you better be careful with kids and with other relatives.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: A child under five whose parent died by suicide has a ninefold increased risk of later suicide; ask about family history of suicide in all patients.
pearls.verbatim: Surviving child under five years old of a parent who commits suicide is nine times more likely to commit suicide than not.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Do not respond to repetitive suicidal behavior with frustration or harsh treatment; it may make the patient feel worse and cause them to avoid seeking help, leading to death.
pearls.verbatim: That just may make the person feel a lot worse. And next time, they won't come in. They'll just die.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: When a patient says they want to die, understand that they are really expressing a desire to be rescued from an intolerable situation.
pearls.verbatim: Remember that when you hear them say they want to die, what they're really saying is they want to be rescued from what they believe is an intolerable situation.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Suicidal people often do not have friendships; they become dependent on one person to meet all their needs, which can lead to a 'hostage' dynamic where the significant other feels trapped.
pearls.verbatim: a lot of times, suicidal people don't have friends. They take hostages, where they they get totally dependent on one person, or one situation to meet all of their needs, to give them hope, to give them a reason to keep going.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Verbal warnings about suicide should never be dismissed; many people who talk about killing themselves do complete suicide.
pearls.verbatim: It's a very wrong myth that those who talk about killing themselves don't actually do so.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Always begin suicide risk assessment by asking how the person would harm themselves, then use the SLAP assessment for lethality, availability, and proximity.

pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
