pearls.verbatim: For first trimester pregnancy loss, I saw conflicting numbers. And some studies said as early as one to two weeks later, they could start trying for their next baby.
pearls.speaker: Anne Hogan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Anne Hogan on Vertigo 3/12/26

pearls.text: For second/third trimester loss, follow standard pregnancy interval guidelines (e.g., 12+ months).
pearls.verbatim: For doing induction of labor, d and e or something for later, then you would still follow the regular guidelines for waiting if it's for pregnancy intervals. So a year.
pearls.speaker: Anne Hogan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Anne Hogan on Vertigo 3/12/26

pearls.text: ACOG recommends against using quantitative HCG for dating if dates are unreliable because HCG declines after 10 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: If they don't have reliable dates, ACOG recommends against using quantitative HCG because of the fact that you'll have a decline at ten plus weeks.
pearls.speaker: Anne Hogan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Anne Hogan on Vertigo 3/12/26

pearls.text: For ectopic pregnancy, ACOG has an article on tubal ectopic pregnancy that provides HCG averages for gestational age to guide ultrasound interpretation.
pearls.verbatim: ACOG also has an article that talks about tubal ectopic pregnancies. ... I think it's called tubal ectopic pregnancy.
pearls.speaker: Anne Hogan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Anne Hogan on Vertigo 3/12/26

pearls.text: Recurrent first trimester loss (≥3 miscarriages) is an indication for MFM referral for extensive testing including antiphospholipid syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: in our clinic, if you have a patient with, like, more than three miscarriages, one of the OB attendings said that's a easy MFM referral because they have to do extensive testing, make sure there's no tubal defects, antiphospholipid, and a lot of other abnormalities.
pearls.speaker: Anne Hogan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Anne Hogan on Vertigo 3/12/26

pearls.text: Define chronic pain by duration: symptoms resolving naturally do so within 3 months; chronic pain persists beyond 3 months.
pearls.verbatim: Three months is the line in the sand that separates acute and subacute pain from chronic pain.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Match pain medication to mechanism: NSAIDs/opioids help peripheral nociceptive pain but not central pain; TCAs/SNRIs can help both; gabapentinoids/cannabinoids help central pain but not peripheral pain.
pearls.verbatim: NSAIDs and opioids are typically effective for peripheral nociceptive pain but not central pain. Tricyclics and SNRIs are typically effective for both. Gabapentinoids and cannabinoids are typically effective for central pain but not peripheral pain.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: The 1990 fibromyalgia criteria required chronic widespread pain plus >11 tender points; current criteria no longer rely on the tender point exam.
pearls.verbatim: The American College of Rheumatology 1990 criteria established the diagnosis of fibromyalgia and defined fibromyalgia to require a history of the presence of chronic widespread pain and greater than 11 tender points.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: For fibromyalgia with other prominent symptoms, WPI 4–6 plus SS ≥9 also meets criteria.
pearls.verbatim: Have other symptoms than pain can meet the criteria with a widespread pain index of 4 to 6 and a symptom severity scale greater than or equal to 9.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Ask the 19 pain-site questions exactly as worded, using 'pain' over the 'last week'—not 'discomfort'—to ensure standardized scoring.
pearls.verbatim: it's important to ask the question exactly as it's written so that somebody's given the same question. Particularly, I'm referring to pain over the last week, and they do use the word pain, not discomfort.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: The SS scale also asks about six-month bother from headache and lower abdominal pain/cramps, not just last-week symptoms.
pearls.verbatim: over the last six months, have you been bothered by headache? Have you... Over the last six months, have you been bothered by pain or cramps in the lower abdomen depression.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Fibromyalgia diagnosis requires symptoms generally present for at least 3 months.
pearls.verbatim: symptoms should generally be present for at least three months to make a diagnosis of fibromyalgia.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Widespread pain must be demonstrated in at least four of the five body region groups to count for fibromyalgia.
pearls.verbatim: A person should have widespread pain demonstrated by at least four of the five groups being present.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Morning stiffness lasting longer than one hour is a hallmark of inflammatory arthritis, but fibromyalgia patients also have prolonged morning stiffness, so this finding must be interpreted in context.
pearls.verbatim: Morning stiffness lasting for longer than an hour applies to the presence of an inflammatory disease. But beware that fibromyalgia patients also have prolonged morning stiffness.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: In osteoarthritis, the DIP joints are prominently involved and the enlargement is bony and hard; in rheumatoid arthritis, DIP joints are spared and swelling is boggy.
pearls.verbatim: This is a scan of a patient with osteoarthritis, and you see prominent involvement of the DIP joints. So that would... That is something we do not find in rheumatoid arthritis. Also, the enlargement in osteoarthritis is a bony and hard swelling as opposed to a boggy swelling that we find in an inflammatory arthritis.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: The degree of ESR elevation correlates with inflammation: upper limit of normal to 50 is mild, 50-100 moderate, >100 severe.
pearls.verbatim: The degree of elevation of the sedimentation rate correlates with the degree of inflammation. Upper limits of normal to 50 is mild. 50 to a 100 is moderate. Greater than a 100 is severe.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: When using the 2010 ACR/EULAR RA criteria, start at the bottom (symptom duration) and work up to determine how many joints you need to find on exam to reach a score of 6.
pearls.verbatim: I like to start at the bottom and work my way up because it tells me then how many tests I need to find on exam to make the diagnosis.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: In the 2019 EULAR/ACR SLE criteria, mucocutaneous findings (alopecia, oral ulcers, cutaneous lupus) must be observed by the clinician, not just reported historically.
pearls.verbatim: The mucocutaneous domain, as we look under the... On the definition page, we see that these are some things that do need to be observed by the clinician. So alopecia, oral ulcers, cutaneous lupus, these things should be observed by the clinician, not historical.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Any patient suspected of having lupus should be referred to a rheumatologist because it is a lifelong condition that can worsen in myriad ways.
pearls.verbatim: But if you do find someone to have lupus, it's a lifelong condition, and the condition can worsen over time in a myriad of ways. And so anyone that you suspect has lupus, I think you need to refer to a rheumatologist.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Fibromyalgia management includes exercise, a gabapentinoid, a serotonergic agent, and cognitive behavioral therapy.
pearls.verbatim: A little bit of exercise. Gabapentinoid, and a serotonergic and some cognitive behavioral therapy.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: Explain the nature of fibromyalgia to patients; symptoms often settle down after a couple of years.
pearls.verbatim: And an explanation of what's going on. Mhmm. And often after couple of years, things will settle down.
pearls.speaker: B Howard
pearls.episode_title: Dr. B Howard on RA & Lupus 10/23/25

pearls.text: The most common location for a Morton neuroma is between the third and fourth toes because the fourth and fifth digits share a common bone attachment, restricting motion and causing repeated nerve impingement.
pearls.verbatim: The fourth and fifth digits share the same bone that they're attached to, whereas all the other bones have their... An individual attachment point.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: No imaging is needed to diagnose Morton's neuroma; X-rays only show splaying if present, and MRI is rarely necessary.
pearls.verbatim: Do you need to do any imaging? No. No. Great. Let's pretend you did an X-ray. What would it show what would it show? Something. Yeah. It was just splinting, potentially.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: A heel spur on X-ray is a result of chronic inflammation causing calcium deposition, not the cause of the pain.
pearls.verbatim: It's chronic inflammation, which causes increased acidity, which causes calcium phosphorus deposition, and then you get this spurring results out. And so it's not the cause of the pain.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Corticosteroid injection for plantar fasciitis is very painful and risks fat pad atrophy; injecting into the fat pad causes long-term pain with every step.
pearls.verbatim: If you inject this one thing that sits right next to the plantar fascia. Oh, the fat pad atrophies. So the the fat pad is right here, and the injection site is right here. And if you inject into the fat pad, it causes atrophy of it, and then you get pain with every step for...
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Inability to rise on one foot (single heel rise test) is diagnostic for posterior tibial tendon dysfunction.
pearls.verbatim: So if you haven't seen on one foot and then rise up to the ball of their foot, they can't. But your tibial tendon really helps that motion, so they can't rise up. So if they're like, man, I have this pain, stand on one foot, stand up. They can't. Pretty sure that's gonna be the diagnosis.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: PTTD is the number one cause of medial foot pain and is almost always painful.
pearls.verbatim: So this is actually the number one cause of medial foot pain.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: The anterior drawer test is not helpful within 24 hours of an ankle sprain due to swelling and pain.
pearls.verbatim: I always thought it was to... As I was reading about it, like, all these exams we do, probably twenty four hours afterwards, probably helpful at all. So we're causing a ton of pain, a bunch of swelling, like, it's test sensitivity is super low. So it's probably actually not that helpful.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Early motion is critical for ligament healing; casting for weeks impairs proper collagen alignment.
pearls.verbatim: So early motion is, like, really important with, like, ligament injuries. If you put them in a cast and leave them there for a couple weeks, like, you are seriously hurting the healing process.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Prescribe early non-weight-bearing ankle range-of-motion exercises, such as tracing the alphabet with the foot.
pearls.verbatim: Really early, you wanted to have them hanging their foot off the bed and going through the whole alphabet, just, like, the alphabet and all this stuff.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Ottawa ankle rules: X-ray indicated if age >55, inability to bear weight, posterior malleolar tenderness, or sensory deficits.
pearls.verbatim: If they're greater than 55 and they have history of malleolar trauma, weaker bones and less sensation, you get an X-ray. Just get get one. Inability to bear weights. Tenders are the posterior six centimeters or the lateral malleolus, not the anterior malleolus because that's where the ligament is that always tears. ATLF is right there. So only the posterior aspect. And if sensory deficits, just grab one because Ottawa rules are probably not gonna be as accurate.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Jones fracture (base of 5th metatarsal) requires non-weight bearing for 6 weeks to prevent nonunion.
pearls.verbatim: And then a Jones fracture, which is here. So that's a... At the shaft at the bottom. Metatarsal, That's non weight bearing for six weeks. If not, you're gonna get a nonunion during that surgery and have a lot of pain. So don't miss a Jones fracture.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Refer unstable fractures: bimalleolar, trimalleolar, fracture with contralateral ligament disruption, or distal fibular fracture above the tibiofibular line.
pearls.verbatim: Examples of which are bimalleolar, trimalleolar fractures, fracture with contralateral ligament disruption. That's gonna make it unstable. Distal fibular fractures above the tibiofibular line.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Apply ice for 20-30 minutes every 2 hours over a splint, keeping the splint dry.
pearls.verbatim: And then drape an ice bag over it for twenty to thirty minutes every two hours. You can't let this splint get wet.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Isolated nondisplaced lateral malleolus fracture does not require orthopedic referral.
pearls.verbatim: So you have isolated nondisplaced lateral malleolus fracture. No matter how you treat it, all the complication risks, that's great. So we don't have to refer that out.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: For an oblique lateral malleolus fracture, schedule follow-up in 10 to 14 days.
pearls.verbatim: For the oblique lateral malleolus fracture, you're gonna follow-up ten to fourteen days.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: For patients in a cast, check the heel area for dirt – it indicates the patient is walking when they shouldn't be.
pearls.verbatim: you're make sure the cast isn't dirty, and there's not, like, all this dirt on the bottom, especially on the heel. That means they're walking.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Bimalleolar fractures require a short leg cast and immediate ortho referral.
pearls.verbatim: bimalleolar fractures, send them to ortho after... So you're gonna put them in a a short leg cast, and then send them to ortho.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: A lateral malleolus fracture combined with a distal fibular fracture is unstable and warrants ortho consultation.
pearls.verbatim: If you have a lateral malleolus fracture and then a distal fibular fracture, that's also unstable.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: Delay return to work for strenuous jobs until immobilization is discontinued.
pearls.verbatim: Strenuous jobs. You wanna delay the return to work until the immobilization is discontinued.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Foot & Ankle Basics 9/4/25

pearls.text: After a concussion, the risk of a subsequent concussion triples, and most recurrences happen within the following ten days.
pearls.verbatim: with each concussion, your risk of subsequent concussions goes up three times as three fold. So, like, two up from Miami Dolphins. I don't know if you guys watch football, but he's at, like, seven. So... And subsequent usually occur within the following ten days.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Head & Neck in Urgent Care Setting

pearls.text: In MVA, apply the Canadian C-Spine Rule: if all criteria are negative and the patient can actively rotate their neck 45 degrees left and right, the collar can be safely removed.
pearls.verbatim: If you go through all these questions, and they're negative for everything, you can actually take the brace off the neck and don't move their neck. Ask them, can you turn your head 45 degrees? So 45, 45. If they can do that, then that's classified as safe
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Head & Neck in Urgent Care Setting

pearls.text: A history of gross hematuria at any time in a patient with microscopic hematuria places them at high risk for malignancy.
pearls.verbatim: History of gross hematuria. So if they came in with microscopic... And at any time in their past, they've had history of, like, just blood in the urine, that's actually at high risk.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Hematuria Evaluation

pearls.text: Irritative voiding symptoms (frequency, urgency, dysuria) in the setting of hematuria are actually the highest risk for bladder cancer, contrary to the classic teaching of painless hematuria.
pearls.verbatim: if they have consistent, like, irritative symptoms, it's actually your highest for that.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Hematuria Evaluation

pearls.text: Low-risk hematuria is defined as 3-10 RBC/HPF in women <60 or men <40 with <10 pack-years smoking and no other risk factors; these patients can be followed without urology referral.
pearls.verbatim: low risk folks, that's if you get a a microscopic a microscopic exam. There's only three to 10 red blood cells per high power field. Women less than the age of 60, men less than 40, they've never smoked or less than ten years of smoking. And then none of the risk factors.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Hematuria Evaluation

pearls.text: Intermediate-risk hematuria includes 11-25 RBC/HPF, or persistent low-risk findings, women >60, men 40-59, 10-30 pack-years, or any one risk factor; these patients need urology consultation.
pearls.verbatim: Intermediate risk is if you have 11 to 25 red blood cells. If if you were previously low risk and then a repeat with three to 25. So, essentially, if you were low risk, you had three red red blood cells per high power field and are on a recheck, any recheck, it persists, they immediately go to the next category. Women greater than the age of 60, men 40 59, and that's, like, the ten to thirty pack year group. And then if they had any one of the risk factors.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Hematuria Evaluation

pearls.text: Women over 60 are moved from high to intermediate risk category because cancer is much rarer in women.
pearls.verbatim: Women, it's... Cancer is so much rarer than men. They actually move women from the high risk category over 60 to the intermediate risk just because cancer is really rare in in women.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Hematuria Evaluation

pearls.text: Smoking for more than 30 years, combined with any other risk factor, places the patient in high-risk category.
pearls.verbatim: If you smoke greater than thirty years or any one of the risk factors plus any of this stuff, buys you the high risk.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Hematuria Evaluation

pearls.text: Stones <5 mm are likely to pass; 5.1-9.9 mm have increasing risk of not passing; >10 mm rarely pass.
pearls.verbatim: Less than five, you're gonna pass it. 5.1 to 9.9, increasing risk for not gonna pass it. And then greater than ten, two. Good luck.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Hematuria Evaluation

pearls.text: For 1099 work, immediately set aside 20% of each paycheck (5% for state, 15% for federal) to cover taxes, then pay quarterly via IRS Form 1040-ES and the Oklahoma Tax Commission.
pearls.verbatim: What we... Maggie and I do is we pull out 20%. So 5% for state, 15 for the Fed just immediately. Pull that out.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: If a BiPAP patient is tachypneic, shorten the inspiratory time to 0.5 seconds to prevent breath-stacking and patient-ventilator dyssynchrony.
pearls.verbatim: if somebody's, like, breathing really fast and stuff like that, you're gonna wanna set it for half a second just because then if not, you're gonna have the inspiratory positive airway pressure. While they're breathing out.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: For pulmonary edema on BiPAP, raise EPAP to 8; for COPD, keep EPAP at 5 and IPAP at 12–16.
pearls.verbatim: So for him, it... In his book, he has a whole algorithm that you do, but pulmonary edema versus COPD. So you do five half of 16, you have a four. So his expiratory positive airway pressure's a little lower for pulmonary... Or COPD. For pulmonary edema, he would go to expiratory positive airway pressure to eight.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: For RSI on BiPAP, keep the patient on BiPAP while giving medications, then remove it as they fade and bag until unresponsive before intubating.
pearls.verbatim: I just let them sit there while I'm giving all the meds, and I just keep them on the bilevel positive airway pressure until I push. Once they push and they start to fade, I just rip it off, and I'll bag them until, like, they're not responding to me in their eyes, and I just go for it.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: For hypercapnic respiratory failure on BiPAP, the only ventilator adjustment that improves CO2 clearance is increasing inspiratory time (I-time).
pearls.verbatim: All we're gonna do is change the I-time. That's all you're gonna have. I don't have something you can do. The I-time. All you're gonna change.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: When reading CT for PE, look for filling defects—dark areas within the white contrast of pulmonary arteries.
pearls.verbatim: When you're scrolling through, you can see areas of the pulmonary vasculature that were blocked off like POTS.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: Heparin dosing for PE is weight-based and depends more on liver function than renal function.
pearls.verbatim: heparin doesn't depend so much on kidney function as much as liver function.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: Weight-based heparin dosing (80 units/kg bolus, max 10,000 units, then 18 units/kg/hr) achieves faster therapeutic levels than fixed-dose regimens.
pearls.verbatim: the weight based is eighty eighty units per kg as the loading dose, no more than ten thousand units, and then eighteen units per kg an hour.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: In a crashing patient, push-dose epinephrine (e.g., 1 cc of 1:10,000) can be used as a temporizing vasopressor while a Levophed drip is being set up.
pearls.verbatim: Levophed's gonna take twenty minutes to get set up. So push to use prior respite. So we push to. Times one. I got her pressure up beautifully.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: After a patient death, conduct a team debrief to validate emotions, identify system improvements, and prevent self-blame among staff.
pearls.verbatim: So how do you leave the debrief? You're the doctor there. And there's all these people who don't know what that looks like. So what are you gonna do?
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Rural ER Medicine

pearls.text: On exam, look for a transverse nasal crease and bluish turbinates to suggest allergic rhinitis.
pearls.verbatim: Across the bridge of the nose, there's a line. And then nasal turbinates, they're actually blue colored.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: A recurrent sinusitis episode within 5 days of completing treatment should be considered the same infection, requiring a different antibiotic.
pearls.verbatim: If it comes back within five days, it's considered the same infection.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: For sinusitis that fails initial therapy, escalate to high-dose amoxicillin-clavulanate (2 g twice daily) or levofloxacin if penicillin-allergic.
pearls.verbatim: Augmentin two grams twice a day.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Always palpate for posterior cervical lymph nodes; it improves clinical skills and supports the diagnosis.
pearls.verbatim: Check for the posterior lymph node. I always check for it.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: Honey is better studied than any over-the-counter medication for cough from sore throat.
pearls.verbatim: Honey for cough from sore throat is actually better studied than any other over the counter medication.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: If symptoms resolve, do not retest the patient.
pearls.verbatim: If the symptoms resolve, don't retest them.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: If symptoms recur but appear viral, do not retest; only retest if concerning symptoms prompt full reevaluation.
pearls.verbatim: If they get symptoms back but it appears viral and not bacterial, the exam goes along viral, not bacterial, don't retest.
pearls.speaker: Bancroft
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Bancroft on Sore Throat, Rhinitis, & Sinusitis

pearls.text: The risk of lower extremity complications drops significantly when A1c is below 8%; that is a surgical threshold for elective procedures.
pearls.verbatim: The mark on lower extremity complications that we noticed there's a big risk reduction is below eight on an a one c. Below eight, even though it's not ideal, it's still 7.5. The risk to their feet, it goes way down.

pearls.verbatim: When I look at a report, I wanna see this under three.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: For patients with severe OSA (e.g., initial AHI >100), an AHI of 4 may be acceptable if they are symptomatic and at high pressures (16–18 cmH₂O).
pearls.verbatim: If I have somebody who came in with over a 100 events per hour and they have four an hour, I'm not excited. I'm like, okay. You know, especially if they're in upper range of pressures. And I know that, you know, they're they're having to exhale against sixteen, eighteen centimeters of water pressure. If it's four, I'm not gonna get excited, especially if they're feeling good symptomatically
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: Expiratory pressure release (EPR) of 1–3 cmH₂O reduces pressure during exhalation to improve comfort.
pearls.verbatim: when I inhale, I get my 10, but then when I exhale, it backs off by three. And your expiratory pressure release can be a difference of one, two, or three centimeters of water pressure, and it's it's a comfort feature.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: Home sleep study patients receive an auto-adjusting CPAP with a default range of 6–20 cmH₂O.
pearls.verbatim: when they do a home based study, they get an auto adjusting CPAP. So the the settings on that is generally six to 20 unless I narrow the range in the follow-up visit.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: Do not recommend mouth taping; consider a dental device for snoring or airflow limitation instead.
pearls.verbatim: I would rather you have a dental device for treatment of snoring or airflow limitation than ever consider taping your mouth shut. I I just can't endorse that one.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: For inpatients without known CPAP settings, start at 8 cmH₂O and select 'chronic' in the order with a comment about known OSA.
pearls.verbatim: in general, an average pressure for an adult is around eight, and so that's where I would start. ... the chronic part of the order is important. And then in the comment section, you can write down known history of obstructive sleep apnea. Please use nocturnal CPAP therapy during hospitalization.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: Home sleep tests are unreliable for central or complex apnea; pregnant patients, those on narcotics, or with heart failure/Cheyne-Stokes should go directly to in-lab titration.
pearls.verbatim: the home based tests are not super good at central apnea or complex apnea. So particularly people who are pregnant or on narcotics, chronic pain management, or they have a history of heart failure, Cheyne-Stokes type breathing patterns, we'll see that central apnea.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: If home sleep testing shows severe hypoxemia or AHI over 100, bring the patient to the lab for titration because they will likely need high pressures.
pearls.verbatim: if they have a really severe hypoxemia or an index... Apnea hypopnea index in... Events per hour that's, like, over a 100, I'm like, just bring them into the lab to do the treatment part because odds are they're gonna need a higher amount of pressure to control the apnea.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: On BiPAP, keep pressure support (IPAP minus EPAP) at 4 cm H2O or less; higher support impairs ventilation.
pearls.verbatim: So we don't want a pressure support of more than four on a BiPAP. Otherwise, it affects their ventilation.
pearls.speaker: Dolin
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dolin on Obstructive Sleep Apnea

pearls.text: Recognize that the goal of many doctors is to not get in trouble (CYA), which leads to unnecessary testing and defensive medicine.
pearls.verbatim: Our goal is to not get in trouble. You think that's gonna end when you're done with residency? No. Because you know how doctors practice? Do not get in trouble.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Avoid copying and pasting differentials from templates; it takes the thinking out of the diagnostic process.
pearls.verbatim: So we open it up and then list all these things as though you thought about it. Is it true? No. I think it is true, and it and it takes the thinking out of it.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Recognize that men typically come to the doctor only when very sick or when pressured by family (e.g., spouse concerned about genetic disease). Use this pattern to anticipate their fears.
pearls.verbatim: Men don't come to the doctor in general. Yes. They don't do it. They come three times. So sick they're gonna die. Oh, they feel like it. Somebody in the family was just diagnosed with a potentially genetic disease, and they wanna be tested, but the spouse is driving them crazy. That's when men come, like, even for a physical.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Reinforce the analogy that you can buy a new truck but you only have one body, so preventive care is essential.
pearls.verbatim: You can buy a new truck. This is the only body you've got.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Build trust by listening, caring, and affirming the patient's concerns, even if they seem crazy. Say 'That's really hard. I understand.' and show empathy.
pearls.verbatim: But one of the ways that you listen to them, you care about them. You affirm their concerns. Even if it's crazy, you go, wow. That's really hard. I understand. You're empathetic, and they begin to trust you.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: When a physician gets angry at a non-compliant patient, it reveals an ego problem: the doctor is offended that the patient doesn't trust or follow their advice.
pearls.verbatim: When a physician gets angry that a patient is not compliant, It always hits me funny. It's like, so you got an ego problem. Your ego is offended that this person who doesn't know you and or doesn't trust you isn't doing what you're telling them to do.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Contraception prescribing in faith-based institutions may have room for physician-patient private decision-making even if the organization philosophically opposes it.
pearls.verbatim: you can, but it's private and it's hidden in that room even though the organization doesn't really believe in contraception as philosophically and as a faith based thing. So there's room.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: When patients demand antibiotics for viral infections, it is often appropriate to provide reassurance and stand your ground rather than prescribing unnecessarily.
pearls.verbatim: the right something may be reassurance and standing your ground. Because we don't do everything people want.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: When addressing sexual health issues in elderly patients, be prepared to discuss STIs and dysfunction without judgment, as these are common in retirement communities.
pearls.verbatim: some of these retirement centers? Party time, man. There's STIs all over the place. ... it's gonna come. And and then you decide, what am I gonna do?
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: When referring patients to counselors or specialists, know the individual clinician's personality and skills—don't just send them generically, as not all practitioners are equally competent or appropriate.
pearls.verbatim: don't just refer for counseling. That would be... Think of your classmates. There are classmates you had in medical school that are surgeons that you're not sending anybody in your family to.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Treat each patient as you would treat your own family member—coordinate their care with the same level of personal investment.
pearls.verbatim: you treat them like you would your mom, your auntie, your grandpa, your own kid, help coordinate their care.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: On board exams like the ITE, answer based on the accepted standard of care even if you personally disagree with it, because the exam tests consensus guidelines, not personal belief.
pearls.verbatim: when I take the ITE, I'm gonna put that on there. Or else I'll miss it. ITE, it's not like, do you agree with this? It's more like, what is the right answer of the people that are asking.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Controversies in Medicine 8/27/26

pearls.text: Understand and respect organizational hierarchy and authority; the centurion's recognition of being under authority and having authority under him was commended by Jesus as great faith.
pearls.verbatim: And then Jesus said, I have not seen faith as deep of an understanding of human nature and authority in all the world. That's the greatest faith I've seen. Go. And and his servant was healed. But Jesus marveled at him because there was something about this.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Hidden parts of the body (or of a person) often have equal or greater value than visible ones; do not equate visibility with importance.
pearls.verbatim: And sometimes the hidden things even have more value. We don't like that. And our society tends to be, well, the things that are seen and noticed, they have more value. Eye, dunk and a ball, eye color, intelligence, all that stuff. He said, no. Sometimes the hidden ones actually are of equal or more value, but hard to get that as we as human beings.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: When leading, do not try to be another person you admire; instead, discover your own God-given identity and use your unique strengths, just as David used his own sling rather than Saul's armor.
pearls.verbatim: And the most frustrated you can be in life is trying to beat somebody that you're not, that doesn't fit. And I think I'm like David. Remember David? He came to do Goliath in. He's like, here, put on Saul's armor, he tries. He goes, no. That doesn't work. That's not me. I can fight, but I can't fight with that armor, with that suit, in that style. So he took what he had, and he accomplished the will of God.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Submit your natural personality traits (e.g., temper, sensitivity, steadiness) to the lordship of Christ for refinement rather than using them as excuses for ungodly behavior.
pearls.verbatim: And in our personalities, we have some really good stuff. In our personalities, we have some really bad stuff. And it's not bad. It just needs to kinda be fixed, it needs to be surrendered to the lordship of Christ. And and and that's hard too because it's like, that's just how I am. I mean, I had one guy tell me, I just have a temper. Am I a rich Catholic? I have a temper. Everybody in my family has a temper. That's how I am. I said, no. That's true. It's not godly. It's not Christ like. And you have to get rid of it.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Fear leads to self-protection (keeping people at arm's length) and self-promotion (proving your worth).
pearls.verbatim: if there's too much fear, there's two things that happen as a result of that. One is we self protect. If we're afraid and we don't really know who we are, we're always protecting ourselves. And that keeps us distant from people. I'm not gonna let anybody get too close. I'm gonna let anybody know me because if they really know me, they're not gonna like what they find. I have to I have to be careful and protect and hold people at arm's length. The other thing that it goes right with it is we self promote. That we we have to prove to other people who we are and why we're good and why we're okay.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Jesus never had to self-promote or convince people how amazing he was; he simply stated who he was.
pearls.verbatim: Jesus knew who he was. He never had to self promote. He never had to convince people how amazing he was. He said, this is who I am. The light of the world. I'm the bread of life. I'm the good shepherd. I'm here to rescue you.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Being under authority is a place of protection and support, not weakness.
pearls.verbatim: It's a place of protection. It's a place of support. When I go talk to St. John, one of the best things that I can do is say, our board of directors has told me this is where we're going. I'm the spokesperson today, but this is what they have directed me to do to say to you.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: When saying no to someone under your care, your motive must be for their best, even if they don't like you in the moment.
pearls.verbatim: My motive is for your best. My motive is for your well-being. I want what's good for you, and there will be nos sometime. And when I say no, you may not like me. I hope you like me because I really, really want you to like me. But it's more important that I do what's right because I answer to God.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Leadership is not just doing somebody's work for them; sometimes the easiest way out is not the right thing to do.
pearls.verbatim: Leadership is not just doing somebody's work for you. Your personality might be instead of telling them, come on. Get your act together. It might be... Let me just handle that for you. That might not be the right thing to do. It might be, but it might not be. But it might be the easiest way out.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Residency is a three-year leadership development intensive course that happens to be in the profession of family medicine.
pearls.verbatim: I describe IHI as a three year leadership development intensive course that happens to be in the profession of family medicine.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: The goal is to transmit what you have learned to faithful others who will themselves be able to teach others.
pearls.verbatim: He said the things you've heard and seen in me, transmit them, impart them, share them, teach them to others who are faithful, who will themselves be able to teach others.
pearls.speaker: Duininck
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Duininck on Leadership

pearls.text: Methadone is a full mu-opioid agonist available only through federally regulated opioid treatment programs (OTPs) for addiction, though it can be prescribed for pain by any provider.
pearls.verbatim: You can only get methadone for addiction in these OTPs, these fed... Very strictly federally regulated centers. You can prescribe methadone for pain anytime you want, but if you're doing it for addiction, it has to be through one of these centers currently.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Relapse (return to use) should be expected and managed like other chronic diseases—patients should be retained in treatment, not dismissed, because outcomes are better even without complete abstinence.
pearls.verbatim: We call it relapse, which is also a stigmatizing term. Right? They return to use. But if you look at the relapse rates of diabetes and hypertension, it's actually higher than addiction. ... We want to retain them in treatment because we know outcomes are better when they're in treatment. Okay? Even if they're not a 100% sober, if they're in treatment, their quality of life is better.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Harm reduction strategies like seat belts and helmets are routine; applying them to addiction care (e.g., preventing injection behaviors) is no different and should not be stigmatized.
pearls.verbatim: We do harm reduction all the time. But sometimes when we call it harm reduction and addiction, people kinda start getting a little upset. And, again, that's all driven by stigma. Seat belts, reduction. Right? Vacations, harm reduction.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Buprenorphine reduces mortality ratio from 6 to less than 2, making it a life-saving intervention despite causing physiological dependence.
pearls.verbatim: If this reduces mortality ratio from six to less than two, I think it's worth considering.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Methadone has superior pain relief compared to buprenorphine, so patients with uncontrolled pain on buprenorphine may need to transition to methadone maintenance at an OTP.
pearls.verbatim: it tends to be better for pain. Right? And it can lead to euphoria at high doses. It has a weaker affinity, so it can be displaced by other opioids.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: For patients on buprenorphine who have co-occurring pain, the analgesic effect lasts only 4-6 hours, so more frequent dosing or a Butrans patch may be needed.
pearls.verbatim: despite this kind of hanging around, the analgesic benefits are pretty short, like four to six hours. So if you have some of the co occurring pain, you tend to have distal more frequently or try this with Butrans patch and other delivery models.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Higher buprenorphine doses (16-24 mg) produce more opioid-free urines than lower doses; 8 mg is the minimum to block enough receptors to protect against other opioids.
pearls.verbatim: At sixty milligrams, we have a much higher response than even eight. So people sometimes are like, well, you just... You don't need to be on fifteen milligrams or twenty four milligrams. Well, research really supports higher doses are more effective.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Naltrexone can be used as needed around high-risk drinking events (e.g., Fourth of July) to diminish the buzz and prevent relapse.
pearls.verbatim: take naltrexone during that time. And, again, it can still provide some benefit where it might tamper the buzz a little bit so they can not trigger that cycle.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Cognitive behavioral therapy alone was inferior to medication-based treatment in the COMBINE study; patients choosing therapy only should know the evidence.
pearls.verbatim: CBF therapy is their only intervention for an alcohol use disorder according to the study that is inferior treatment.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: In pregnancy, alcohol metabolism is slower due to lower alcohol dehydrogenase, and it is a major preventable cause of birth defects; ask all pregnant patients about drinking.
pearls.verbatim: You're making lower levels of alcohol dehydrogenase, so you're gonna metabolize alcohol slower. Again, it's one of the number one preventable birth defects and developmental disabilities in The US.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Oklahoma physicians with alcohol problems can seek help through the Oklahoma Physician Health Program (OHPP) before any board involvement, without losing their license.
pearls.verbatim: If you have... Identify you have a problem, can you seek out the OHPP before you... Anything bad happens or the board gets involved? You can get help without losing your license.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Extended-release injectable naltrexone (Vivitrol) is rarely rejected by insurance; it reduces GI side effects and eliminates the daily medication decision.
pearls.verbatim: Vivitrol, we don't get rejections.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: SoonerCare allows up to 60 mg of buprenorphine suboxone without prior authorization; amounts above that require a quantity limit override.
pearls.verbatim: SoonerCare allows you to do sixty milligrams of buprenorphine suboxone without a prior authorization. More than that, they do want a quantity limit override, which we get through, but it's just a pain in the butt.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: SoonerCare reimburses advanced drug screening (confirmation testing) daily if needed, not just screening.
pearls.verbatim: SoonerCare allows me to do an advanced drug screen, which we just started doing in the past six months, not just a screen of confirmation testing through a company every day if I want to. They'll pay for it daily.
pearls.speaker: Dunn
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn on Addiction Med

pearls.text: Genetic testing for depression assesses metabolism (tolerability), not efficacy; it is not standard of care and often a waste of money.
pearls.verbatim: Currently, as it as it stands, most genetic testing is testing the ability to metabolize medication. It's not really testing the efficacy. It's it's, like, more a tolerability testing.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Early GI side effects from sertraline are due to serotonin receptors in the GI tract; reassure patients that this is not the therapeutic effect.
pearls.verbatim: you have the most serotonin receptors in your GI system. Right? You first start taking it, it's almost like your cells, like, spit out, like, dose of serotonin.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Aim for remission (PHQ-9 <5) rather than just response; optimize dosing of a single agent before switching.
pearls.verbatim: But you really wanna you really wanna treat to remission if you can.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Mirtazapine is more activating at higher doses; lower doses are more sedating. Optimize dose before switching.
pearls.verbatim: I would first optimize dosing of a single agent. We just... She's on the starting dose of mirtazapine. She's responded to it, but she's not in remission. You can live on it. Right? Higher doses of mirtazapine do tend to be more activating, just so you guys know.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Trazodone at antidepressant doses (300-400 mg) is poorly tolerated; it is primarily used for sleep at low doses.
pearls.verbatim: the doses of trazodone that you need to actually treat depression are gonna be, like, three to four hundred milligrams, which is gonna snow most people. So trazodone is rarely an antidepressant. It's almost always just for sleep.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Light therapy can induce hypomania; the patient's eyes must be open (retinal mechanism) and they should not stare at the light.
pearls.verbatim: Light therapy has actually induced hypomania in people. Right? So it has that capability. They don't have to stare at the light, but their eyes have to be open because the mechanism of action is through the retina.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Second-generation antipsychotics used for augmentation require a 6-12 week trial before determining failure.
pearls.verbatim: For SGAs, they usually need six to twelve week trial before they fail it.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: After two major depressive episodes, the 5-year recurrence rate is 75%; after three episodes, consider lifelong treatment.
pearls.verbatim: After two major depressive episodes, the five year recurrence rate is seventy five percent. And then after three, it's kind of like you should treat for life.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Severe depression (PHQ-9 >20) should be treated with pharmacotherapy first; psychotherapy is less effective until symptoms improve.
pearls.verbatim: In severe depression, pharmacology is preferred over psychotherapy. Okay. So severe... Severely depressed patients are not gonna respond to psychotherapy either. Their brain is just not in state, but that's So this is when you wanna start. Oncology, get them a little bit better, and then they can initiate therapy.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Treatment-resistant depression is defined as failure of two adequate trials of antidepressants from different classes at adequate doses for at least 6 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: major major depressive episode that has now responded to trials of antidepressant monotherapy of different classes for an adequate length of time. So so, again, if they're failed two solid trials, this is when you wanna probably refer to psychiatry.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Bupropion is preferred for non-anxious depression with minimal weight gain and no sexual side effects.
pearls.verbatim: bupropion is a great medication for your nonanxious depressed patients, has minimal weight gain, and no sexual side effects.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Clonus is a key differentiator for serotonin syndrome; symptoms include agitation, confusion, vital sign instability, dilated pupils, and muscle rigidity.
pearls.verbatim: The muscle rigidity, I think, is pretty hallmark. So you wanna... If you're doing neurological exam, you can really feel that muscle to the point of clonus. Okay? So clonus, I think, is a big differentiator in serotonin syndrome.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Document efforts to taper controlled substances to avoid future malpractice claims.
pearls.verbatim: You should be documenting that you're trying. Mhmm. Right? And if you're... That's... Eventually, that's gonna be, like, malpractice.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: Benzodiazepines are not effective for acute panic attacks because the attack is too brief (usually <10 minutes).
pearls.verbatim: So no benzo is gonna work within several minutes.
pearls.speaker: Dunn speaks
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Dunn speaks on Depression

pearls.text: If a patient has typical ACS symptoms (left-sided chest pressure radiating to left jaw/shoulder/arm with diaphoresis and nausea), they need to go to the cath lab even if the EKG is not diagnostic.
pearls.verbatim: That person needs to go to the cath lab. Even if the EKG didn't show what you were expecting, that person still needs to go to the cath lab.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: About one in five patients with ACS do not have typical symptoms; atypical presentations are common in women, diabetics, the elderly, and non-white patients.
pearls.verbatim: somewhere around one in five don't have typical typical symptoms.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Benign early repolarization is common in young men (16-32) and shows ST elevation in every lead without reciprocal changes; it is not a STEMI.
pearls.verbatim: If you see it in every lead and there's no reciprocal changes, that's not as STEMI. That's common.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Unstable angina is a purely clinical diagnosis of new or different chest pain in a patient with known CAD, often without EKG or troponin changes.
pearls.verbatim: Purely clinical, purely history. Yep. And it helps... The majority of people who are diagnosed with unstable angina have known CAD.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: Known CAD means prior cath, coronary CTA showing calcifications/atherosclerosis, or abnormal stress test; peripheral artery disease or carotid disease also suggests coronary disease.
pearls.verbatim: Known CAD means they had a cath. Known CAD means they've had a cath. They've had a coronary CTA, a CTA of the heart that showed calcifications or atherosclerosis, or they've had an abnormal stress test.
pearls.speaker: Engstrom
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Engstrom on ACS

pearls.text: A new bifascicular block in the right clinical context can signal an occlusive MI and warrants calling cardiology.

pearls.text: A change of 3 or more points on the NIHSS indicates a neurological change large enough to warrant head imaging or calling the rapid response team.

pearls.text: For NIHSS command testing, tell the patient to make a fist and close eyes; do not pantomime or place your fingers in their hand to avoid reflexive grasping.
pearls.verbatim: Make sure that you you tell them make a fist and close your eyes or open your eyes. And then if they're just blinking their eyes, that's different. Your fingers in their hand because they're gonna just reflectively grasp onto your hand, and that doesn't count.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Hadwen on Neuro Exam

pearls.text: For extraocular movements in NIHSS, hold your finger about 2.5 feet away and test only horizontal gaze; scoring is based on ability to cross midline.
pearls.verbatim: I told you guys already about, like, holding your finger out about two, two and a half feet when you're doing extraocular movements. If you aren't here, just make sure you're not here because the person's just gonna converge and not able to actually do smooth pursuits and look all the way over. pearls.speaker: Hadwen
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Hadwen on Neuro Exam

pearls.text: When testing visual fields for NIHSS, use binocular vision with fists held 2–2.5 feet away; flash fingers in upper and lower quadrants. If the patient looks toward the stimulus, that confirms intact peripheral vision.
pearls.verbatim: You just go like this. Look at my nose. And even if they don't, they're looking around. It doesn't matter. You just show your fingers like that, and you flash them. One two. One two. And they're looking over at it, that means they have visual fields.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Hadwen on Neuro Exam

pearls.text: For motor testing, hold arms for 10 seconds and legs for 5 seconds; score 0 if no drift, 4 if no movement at all.

pearls.speaker: Hadwen
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Hadwen on Neuro Exam

pearls.text: When testing motor drift, have the patient hold both arms up simultaneously; if one arm drifts lower than the other, score 1. If it drops to the bed within a few seconds despite antigravity, score 2.

pearls.text: To get best motor effort, verbally encourage the patient during arm/leg hold; neurologists routinely coach patients during testing.
