pearls.text: When referring to psychiatry, ensure the patient does not feel they are being dismissed or 'pitched off'.
pearls.verbatim: they would always be referred to psych. We just wanna make sure that they don't see that as a now we're pitching you off.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Conversion Disorder

pearls.text: Prefer the term 'functional neurological symptom disorder' over 'conversion disorder' because it describes what it is and reduces stigma.
pearls.verbatim: We don't wanna call it conversion because ICD uses this. Finally joined the party. And also because then it doesn't make it sound like psych moves into your body. Actually, they are connected. This one also describes what it actually is.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Conversion Disorder

pearls.text: For factitious disorder, clear evidence of deceit must be demonstrated; inconsistency alone does not suffice.
pearls.verbatim: It has to be, like, demonstrated.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Conversion Disorder

pearls.text: Functional neurological symptom disorder and illness anxiety disorder frequently overlap because both are triggered by stressful life events.
pearls.verbatim: it seems like those two really overlap maybe somewhat frequently because of the stimulus is often, like, a very stressful life trigger.
pearls.speaker: Satterlee
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Satterlee on Conversion Disorder

pearls.text: Hematuria must be confirmed by microscopic analysis of a clean urine specimen; dipstick alone is insufficient.
pearls.verbatim: Hematuria is defined by a microscopic analysis. Okay? So that needs to, like, you know, be right front of your brain. If you do a dipstick urine and it's got blood in it, it doesn't matter. You need to confirm that with a microscopic analysis.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: In older women with urinary symptoms but no infection, decreased vaginal estrogen is the most common cause.
pearls.verbatim: The most common cause for urinary symptoms in a older female, which is a lot of the women that you're gonna be seeing, is decreased vaginal estrogen.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Vaginal atrophy predisposes older women to true UTIs by replacing normal vaginal flora with pathogenic bacteria.
pearls.verbatim: The vaginal flora that they have gets replaced with pathogenic bacteria, and they start getting urinary tract infections.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Patients with chronic indwelling catheters need urology surveillance every 1-2 years due to risk of squamous cell carcinoma.
pearls.verbatim: Those patients that have chronic indwelling suprapubic tubes are fully catheters. Those patients get bladder cancer. They should be seen by a urologist every year anyway.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: For intermediate-risk microscopic hematuria, renal ultrasound has replaced CT urography as first-line imaging.
pearls.verbatim: Renal ultrasonography has replaced CT urography in intermediate risk patients.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Gross hematuria is the highest-risk presentation and requires urology workup regardless of other factors.
pearls.verbatim: If a patient is peeing blood, they need to come and see us no matter what.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: CT urography for high-risk hematuria is a three-phase study: non-contrast (for stones), IV contrast (for renal masses), and delayed images (for ureteral/bladder masses).
pearls.verbatim: A CT urogram is a three phase CT scan. The first phase is non contrast. That allows kidney stones and bladder stones and those sorts of things. The second is an IV contrasted phase. ... And then we get delayed images. ... that highlights the contrast moving through the ureters down into the bladder and gives us an idea about whether or not there are ureteral masses or bladder masses or anything like that.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Ask about beet consumption in patients reporting red urine, as beets can turn urine bright red.
pearls.verbatim: One of the questions is they're like, I peed I peed blood. And you say, well, have you eaten any beets lately? And a lot of these people are like, yeah. I did. So beets will turn your urine bright red.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: If a patient says their urinary symptoms don't bother them, you don't need to treat them even with a large prostate.
pearls.verbatim: if their answer is no, I don't care. Okay? I mean, I will do a workup to make sure they're emptying their bladder and they don't have hematuria or UTI or anything like that. But but I don't treat everybody just because they have some element of BPH.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Once a patient starts talking about urinary symptoms, a PSA becomes a diagnostic test, not a screening test.
pearls.verbatim: once a patient starts talking about your urinary symptoms, a PSA test is not a screening test for prostate cancer. It's a diagnostic test.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: You can differentiate nocturia due to prostate vs. other causes by having the patient record nighttime voided volumes; if volumes are small (e.g., 40 cc), suspect non-prostate cause.
pearls.verbatim: So if somebody's waking up every hour to pee, can go six hours during the day, you have to ask yourself, why in the world is that? Why can they have a bladder capacity of four to 500 ccs during the day? And then you have them write down the volumes that they pee at night, and they pee up 40 ccs at night, they feel like they really need to pee. Like, something is going on that has nothing to do with their prostate.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: In obese patients with nocturia, suspect obstructive sleep apnea as the cause rather than prostate disease.
pearls.verbatim: if a patient comes in and you says, like, I wake up eight times a night, I pee, be like, well, is that happening during the day too? And if they say no, then you gotta be like, okay. That... Probably not your prostate gland. Probably something else is going on. And if they're fat, it's probably.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Weight loss, including with GLP-1 agonists, can resolve urinary symptoms by reducing pressure on the bladder.
pearls.verbatim: if you lose weight, and we see this now, thank God for the, you know, the medications, the the shots and everything like that, the GLP-1s, because these patients lose a lot of weight, and I don't see them in my clinics anymore because they don't have urinary symptoms that they had before.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: For patients on Flomax who are having cataract surgery, alert the ophthalmologist because of intraoperative floppy iris syndrome.
pearls.verbatim: a nice thing to do is say, hey. Just... Will you make sure your cat... Your your ophthalmologist knows that you're taking Clomax
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Daily Cialis (5 mg equivalent) improves both LUTS and ED; have patients buy it with GoodRx without using insurance to keep cost low.
pearls.verbatim: Do not have them use their insurance when they get it. They got the GoodRx card. Use the GoodRx. If you run it through your insurance company, the PBMs will jack up the price, and they'll end up paying a lot of money for their Cialis.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: A 50-year-old man with a PSA under 1 has an extraordinarily low chance of being diagnosed with prostate cancer over the next five years, allowing risk stratification.
pearls.verbatim: If you get a guy who's 50 years old and he has a PSA under one, then the chances of him being diagnosed with prostate cancer is extraordinarily low over the next five years.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: When ordering a PSA for a patient with BPH, code BPH with obstruction to make the test diagnostic rather than a screening test.
pearls.verbatim: if I code BPH with obstruction and order a PSA, that PSA is being ordered because of the diagnosis of BPH with obstruction. It is not being ordered as a screening test.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Catheterized urine specimens are the gold standard for accurate urine culture in women.
pearls.verbatim: catheterized urine specimens are the very best way. We do it all the time in our office.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: PCR urine tests often report multiple organisms and lack sensitivity data; standard urine culture with sensitivities is preferred.
pearls.verbatim: PCR tests can be helpful. I do not like them very much because they give you so much information the exception generally of sensitivities, which is the thing that we really both want to know. And it will tell you that there are 17 different bacteria that are growing in this woman, China. Some of them have nothing to do with the urinary system whatsoever.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Double voiding or standing voiding can help women with incomplete bladder emptying due to pelvic prolapse.
pearls.verbatim: doing double voiding or standing voiding or something like that can change those sorts of things.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Vaginal estrogen cream is a first-line treatment for recurrent UTIs in postmenopausal women.
pearls.verbatim: vaginal estrogen cream, very important in the treatment for coronary tract infections. It's one of the first things that we do in a patient who's postmenopausal.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Azo (phenazopyridine) should not be taken for more than five days because prolonged use can cause orange skin discoloration.
pearls.verbatim: Azo, generally, you don't wanna take that one for more than five days because if who's in a prolonged period, it can actually dye your skin orange, which is a little weird.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Nitrofurantoin (Macrobid) has a very low resistance profile and is an excellent first-line antibiotic for uncomplicated UTIs.
pearls.verbatim: Macrobid is my favorite antibiotic of all times. It has a very low resistance profile. It's very difficult for bacteria to become resistant to macrobid.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Severe irritative voiding symptoms may be due to bladder stones (calculi), which require cystoscopy for diagnosis.
pearls.verbatim: They may have a crush on them in situ of the bladder. One of the most common causes that we see of severe irritative.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Many pediatric UTIs are due to voiding dysfunction; management includes a bowel regimen with MiraLAX and potty training.
pearls.verbatim: The vast majority of kid UTIs are because they have weight dysfunction. So they should be... You know, they should have, you know, potty training slash bowel. You know, they should be on some sort of MiraLAX, basically.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: UTIs in boys after age 1 are uncommon; if they occur, refer to urology.
pearls.verbatim: It's uncommon for boys after one to have UTIs at all. So if that happens, send them to us.
pearls.speaker: Sean Doyle
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sean Doyle on Common Urologic Problems

pearls.text: Interstitial (cornual) ectopic pregnancies are more likely to rupture because there is less space for the gestational sac to grow.
pearls.verbatim: I also wanted to highlight just the the C section scar as a possibility for where an extratubal pregnancy could end up implanting because you can get... That's the risk factor that we'll learn about later, but you can get the the child actually implanting in the scar, which is prone to not just cause rupture of a tube, but rupture of the uterus.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: After one ectopic pregnancy, the recurrence risk is 10%; after two or more, it exceeds 25% if no intervention is made.
pearls.verbatim: If you've had one ectopic pregnancy, you're one in ten chance that you're gonna have another one if nothing changes. And if you've had two or more, then you have a greater than twenty five percent chance that you'll have another one if nothing changes.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Chlamydia causes tubal scarring and secretes interleukin-1, which directs the embryo to implant at the infection site.
pearls.verbatim: Chlamydia is a big offender. It causes a lot of scarring, and it also causes the secretion of interleukin one, which is an inflammatory response to the infection in the tubes, but is also a signal that the embryo can detect. It's one of the body's signals to say, hey. You're in the uterus. You should implant now. And so chlamydia, in particular, will direct an embryo to implant wherever the infection is in the tube.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Smoking impairs smooth muscle and ciliary function in the fallopian tubes, increasing the risk of ectopic pregnancy.
pearls.verbatim: Smoking is gonna generally impact your capacity to have smooth muscle and ciliary function.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: If a pregnancy occurs with an IUD in place, 50% are ectopic pregnancies.
pearls.verbatim: if a pregnancy does happen in the presence of an IUD, half of them are ectopic pregnancies.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: On bimanual exam, a closed cervical os helps differentiate ectopic pregnancy from threatened or incomplete miscarriage.
pearls.verbatim: If you do a cervical exam, it will be closed because they are not having a miscarriage from their uterus. This is not a threatened miscarriage or an incomplete miscarriage like you would see for other causes of first trimester bleeding.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Transvaginal ultrasound is the gold standard for diagnosing ectopic pregnancy; MRI may be used in stable patients with suspected extratubal implantation.
pearls.verbatim: Transvaginal ultrasounds are the gold standard for figuring out where somebody's baby has implanted. But in some of those cases where it's extra tubal and it's really hard to see, some of the literature was saying that you could get an MRI if you... Patient's stable.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: In ectopic pregnancy, the uterus can still respond to hormones, and 16% of cases show fluid in the uterus on imaging even without an intrauterine pregnancy.
pearls.verbatim: if you have an ectopic pregnancy, your uterus can still be responding to hormones. And, like I saw, sixteen percent of the time in some cases, you'll have fluid there on imaging even though there's not actually a baby in your uterus.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Rh typing is essential in ectopic pregnancy because maternal-fetal blood mixing can cause alloimmunization.
pearls.verbatim: if they are negative and the baby's Rh positive, you need to give some anti D. Yeah. This is this is an event that can cause alloimmunization. So that's something to keep in mind for sure. It's enough mixing of maternal fetal blood in this case.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: If hCG is at or above the discriminatory zone (~2,000 mIU/mL) and no intrauterine pregnancy is seen on ultrasound, there is a high chance of ectopic pregnancy.
pearls.verbatim: If your HDD is at that level, what should you expect? Intrauterine pregnancy. To be able to see an intrauterine sac with a baby or whatever in the uterus at that time on imaging. So if it's this high and you don't see anything in their uterus on imaging, it means that they have a high chance of having an ectopic pregnancy because we should see something in the uterus at this level of HCG.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: If hCG falls by less than 21% over 48 hours, suspect ectopic rather than completed miscarriage.
pearls.verbatim: If they've had a spontaneous abortion or they've had a miscarriage, you would expect their hCG to start falling, but we would expect it to fall by more than they've gotten the cutoff of 21%. So if you check their hCG again in forty eight hours, they've seen a decline of only 10% of their HCG, that could mean that their bleeding is not from miscarriage. Their bleeding is from an ectopic that is still there.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Low initial hCG in ectopic pregnancy is a favorable prognostic sign; about 85% of such cases spontaneously resolve without rupture.
pearls.verbatim: I did not realize before learning this that the majority of cases that are starting off with a low HCG level will spontaneously resolve. The child can't survive in the environment where they implanted. The embryo dies, detaches, and is passed along with the menstruation, and no harm comes of it. And so if you start with a low HCG level and you have either evidence of or concern for an ectopic pregnancy, that's actually kind of a good prognostic factor that they might not progress to having a a tube rupture.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Salpingostomy and methotrexate are considered direct abortion in Catholic ethics because they directly harm the embryo, whereas salpingectomy does not.
pearls.verbatim: The salpingostomy and the methotrexate are different because the way that they prevent the complication is through either the physical scraping out of the embryo or the chemical toxicity to the embryo. And both of those instances are more of a direct hit on the child rather than the salpingectomy, which is removing the tube that will rupture.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: In Catholic moral teaching, salpingectomy is permissible because it removes the tube prone to rupture without directly harming the embryo, analogous to treating an aortic aneurysm before rupture.
pearls.verbatim: The harm to a mother is because you're gonna have a hemorrhage from your tube rupturing. So, medically, our goal is to prevent that harm. And so by removing the fallopian tube that's prone to rupture, you can treat that. And so that's a good action. That's akin to, like, if you treat somebody's aortic aneurysm before it ruptures. Right? You can say, oh, there's a vessel that's about to burst. We can do a surgery ahead of time to prevent that from bursting and bleeding out. So we're gonna go ahead and do that.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Familiarize yourself with the ethical directives of the Catholic health system to guide decision-making in stressful moments.
pearls.verbatim: I would recommend that we're familiar with the ethical directives and the reasoning behind them because we are working in a Catholic health system at the moment.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: After surgical treatment for ectopic pregnancy, most guidelines advise waiting one menstrual cycle before trying to conceive again, similar to the recommendation for spontaneous miscarriage.
pearls.verbatim: Some guidelines said one month. You just wait one cycle and then you're ready to try again, which would be the same recommendation we often have for spontaneous miscarriages.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Methotrexate has the lowest recurrence rate because it causes the embryo to detach without altering the fallopian tube, but it may not be the best choice for all patients.
pearls.verbatim: So methotrexate is the one that has the lowest recurrence rate because it just causes the embryo to detach, and it doesn't cause any change to the tube.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Salpingostomy carries a risk of tubal scarring and subsequent recurrence of ectopic pregnancy.
pearls.verbatim: The salpingostomy does have a risk of causing scarring in the tube subsequently and having a recurrence because of the salpingectomy.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: Salpingectomy has a very low recurrence rate but significantly impacts future fertility if the other fallopian tube is not healthy.
pearls.verbatim: And then the salpingectomy has very low risk of recurrence because you've taken that tube out, but it does have a greater impact on future fertility if the other side is not healthy to begin with.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Ectopic Pregnancy 2/9/26

pearls.text: A negative AmniSure test provides over 95% certainty that membranes are intact.
pearls.verbatim: If the amnosure is negative, and then what does that mean? You don't have the rupture. Yeah. You're you're very sure. You're, like, over 95% sure that you do not have rupture of membranes
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Avoid digital cervical exam in PPROM to prevent introducing bacteria into the amniotic cavity.
pearls.verbatim: But for just PPROM, you don't check because there's a high risk of introducing more bacteria, and a lot of protection has been broken for the baby.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: The goal in PPROM management is to prolong pregnancy to 34 weeks, which minimizes combined maternal and fetal risks.
pearls.verbatim: the goal is to get to thirty four weeks gestation because that minimizes the risk for both mom and baby.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: For PPROM before 23-24 weeks, outpatient management with strict return precautions is appropriate if the patient is stable.
pearls.verbatim: you can send a lady home with really strict return precautions before twenty three, twenty four weeks.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Suspect chorioamnionitis when the mother has a fever and the baby shows fetal tachycardia.
pearls.verbatim: If infection is present, how would you tell if infection's present? A little fever. Mom's got a fever, and baby's heart rate is fetal tachycardia.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Fetal intolerance in PPROM often results from abruption or cord compression due to oligohydramnios.
pearls.verbatim: abruption is more common. So abruption and then cord compression.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: After 34 weeks in PPROM, further prolongation offers no benefit and increases infection risk.
pearls.verbatim: After thirty four weeks, they didn't really find much benefit in going much further than that, and you're getting more risk of infection, the rates are gonna go up.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Counsel patients with PPROM to have pelvic rest (nothing in the vagina) but not strict bed rest.
pearls.verbatim: you don't necessarily have to counsel these people to be on a complete bed rest. It's a pelvic rest thing. So nothing in the vagina. And, like, taking it easy is not a bad idea, but they don't have to be on bed rest.
pearls.speaker: Seeley-Hacker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Seeley-Hacker on Pre-Labor Rupture of Membranes (PROM)

pearls.text: Insulin autoantibodies are not useful after a patient has been on exogenous insulin for years; test early if needed.
pearls.verbatim: The insulin antibody is tricky. You can obtain it initially before they've had significant exposure to insulin. But if you get someone in your clinic who's been on insulin for two or three years, that insulin antibody may be positive, low levels just because they're getting exogenous insulin.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Teplizumab can delay onset of type 1 diabetes by 2–3 years in presymptomatic individuals with two or more autoantibodies and dysglycemia (stage 2).
pearls.verbatim: So we now have a single medicine that's gonna prevent... Can delay the onset of type one diabetes on average two to three years. It is called.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: In stage 2 prediabetes (two or more antibodies, glucose <126, no symptoms), there is 100% risk of progression to type 1 diabetes within 5 years.
pearls.verbatim: If someone reaches stage two, there is a hundred percent risk at five years they will progress to type one diabetes.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Teplizumab (TZield) is indicated only for patients with at least two positive islet autoantibodies; a single positive antibody does not qualify.
pearls.verbatim: You have to have two antibodies positive. If youre one antibody positive, it it... Youre not a candidate for T cells.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Teplizumab infusion commonly causes lymphopenia around day 5, and the presence of lymphopenia actually indicates a better therapeutic response.
pearls.verbatim: Most common side effects are lymphopenia at about day five, sometimes a rash. And, actually, the more... Like, if patients have lymphopenia, it actually indicates a better response.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Sensor glucoses are inaccurate at high and low extremes; always verify with a fingerstick when in doubt.
pearls.verbatim: The sensor glucoses are not very accurate at highs and lows.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Overnight false lows are common when a patient lies on the sensor, causing compression of interstitial fluid; always ask if the low is real before treating.
pearls.verbatim: So we see a lot of false lows in the middle of the night when someone is laying on the sensor.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Continuous glucose monitors should be offered to all patients with diabetes per 2025 ADA guidelines.
pearls.verbatim: the ADA now has published data in 2025. The guidelines recommend that any person with diabetes should be offered a continuous glucose monitor because it provides insight into patterns and actionable items
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Target time in range >70%, time below range <4%, and very low (<54 mg/dL) at 0%.
pearls.verbatim: Most patients will want a time in range of 70%, time below range of less than four. And, really, that very low range, which is less than 54 blood group o c one at zero.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: When a patient has been on multiple medications for years without control, think about type 1 diabetes.
pearls.verbatim: And this is the reason I wanted to bring this case to you guys because it was four years. Right? Let's keep trying. Let's keep trying. Let's keep trying. You guys inherit somebody that you're like, hey. We've done these things, it doesn't make sense, please think about type one diabetes.
pearls.speaker: Shah
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shah on Diabetes 12/4/25

pearls.text: Always verify abnormal vital signs by checking them yourself.
pearls.verbatim: You should check it yourself.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: When auscultating subcutaneous emphysema, you may hear crackles like bubble wrap and the patient may have pain with stethoscope pressure.
pearls.verbatim: as you put your stethoscope on there, it's like like bubble wrap, like, as you're putting it on the chest wall and you're listening and mild to moderate pain as you're putting the stethoscope on the chest.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: Crepitus felt in the neck and chest wall suggests pneumomediastinum.
pearls.verbatim: This child has crepitus in the neck and chest wall, and that's bad.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: Pneumomediastinum typically self-resolves; manage with high-concentration oxygen to accelerate air resorption.
pearls.verbatim: It usually self resolves. You give high concentrated oxygen, and the air will resorb.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: On ultrasound, right atrial diastolic collapse (a 'dancing' motion) is an early sign of impending tamponade; patients with this finding need close monitoring and possible intervention even if not yet in full tamponade.
pearls.verbatim: if you see a person with pericardial effusion, the first thing you're gonna see is the atria start to dance. The the the right atrium is gonna get this little, like, dancing motion. Just because it's dancing doesn't mean they're already in credit tamponade, but you really wanna watch those patients close, and they might develop into it.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: When ultrasound guidance is distracting or the operator is inexperienced, abandon it and rely on anatomic landmarks for pericardiocentesis; this can be safer if the operator is not comfortable with ultrasound.
pearls.verbatim: The ultrasound was just distracting me. If you... If you've never done it and you're not good with the ultrasound, forget about it. Just focus.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: In cardiac tamponade, pericardiocentesis using the subxiphoid approach is safest for novices: insert needle at 30–45° between xiphoid and left costal margin aiming toward the left shoulder blade, aspirating continuously.
pearls.verbatim: you can feel the the xiphoid here. So you wanna go, yeah, in this pocket between the xiphoid and this costal margin. You wanna go in between that space with your needle, and you wanna be about 30 to 45 degrees and point it towards the left shoulder shoulder blade.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: A pericardial window (surgical drainage) early in tuberculous pericarditis may prevent development of constrictive pericarditis with a calcified rind, which requires open-heart surgery to remove.
pearls.verbatim: The only way for this to get better is he has to have open heart surgery to surgically remove that rind. Otherwise, we won't... For those patients with the pericardial TB... the preventative treatment would have been to take out the fluid and then create a window surgically that it would drain.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: Steroids are the key to making a TB effusion resolve and preventing reaccumulation.
pearls.verbatim: Steroids are what make the fusion go away and prevents reaccumulation.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: BCG vaccine does not prevent pulmonary TB but reduces extrapulmonary TB, especially in children under 5.
pearls.verbatim: It reduces extrapulmonary TB, especially in children.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: When giving the BCG vaccine, clean the skin thoroughly to prevent infection, as dirty injection sites are common in settings without diapers.
pearls.verbatim: So cleaning the skin is really good idea if we're getting a vaccine.
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: When concerned about a baby, proactively ask the neonatologist if you can come examine the baby with them.
pearls.verbatim: If you've got a baby you're concerned and you're calling them, then be like, hey. Can I come and and check out the baby?
pearls.speaker: Shields
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Shields on Shortness of Breath in Tuberculosis Endemic Nepal

pearls.text: Physicians spend more time looking into computer screens than looking patients in the eyes, contributing to the compassion crisis and depersonalization seen in burnout.
pearls.verbatim: health care providers spend more time looking into computer screens than looking patients in the eyes.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: In patients with diabetes, high physician compassion is associated with an 80% higher odds of optimal blood sugar control and 40% lower odds of acute metabolic complications.
pearls.verbatim: in patients with diabetes, research shows that high physician compassion is associated with an eighty percent higher odds of optimal blood sugar control and forty percent lower odds of acute metabolic complications.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Patients who feel their physician knows them as a person have 33% higher odds of adherence to HIV therapy and 20% higher odds of having an undetectable viral load.
pearls.verbatim: Knowing the patient as a person was associated with thirty three percent higher odds of adherence to therapy and twenty percent higher odds of having no detectable virus in the blood.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: 56% of patients report they ‘have time or compassion,’ not both; yet a classic study showed it is not the intrinsic belief in helping but the belief that one has enough time that predicts whether help is offered.
pearls.verbatim: fifty six percent of patients have time or compassion.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Compassion activates reward pathways in the brain of the giver and can buffer or counteract stress pathways, making it a potential antidote to burnout.
pearls.verbatim: Neuroscience studies show that compassion for others can trigger reward pathways in the brain and positive emotion that can buffer or even counteract the activation of stress pathways and negative emotion.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Dr. Simpson’s personal experiment: he leaned into connection, prepared more, and pulled back less, which lifted the fog of burnout.
pearls.verbatim: I connected more. Prepared more, not less. Leaned in rather than pulling back. That is when the fog of burnout began to lift.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Forty seconds of compassion can change everything for a patient and reenergize the provider.
pearls.verbatim: Forty seconds of compassion can change everything for a patient.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Going through the motions of compassion is not faking it; it is an experiment to observe the feedback.
pearls.verbatim: it's just going through the motions to see what the feedback is.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Primary care physicians are asked to fit 25 hours of work into a 12-hour day, making systemic burnout inevitable.
pearls.verbatim: take everything that a primary care physician's asked to do in one clinic visit and extrapolate that over an entire day, then you're asking... You're being asked to fit twenty five hours of work in a twenty four hour day. Know? More like a twelve hour.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: The CARE measure lists specific skills: making the patient feel at ease, letting them tell their story, listening, being interested in the whole person, explaining clearly, and making a plan together.
pearls.verbatim: Making making the patient feel at ease, letting the patient tell their story, really listening, being interested in you as a whole person, totally understanding concerns, showing care and compassion, being positive, explaining things clearly, helping the patient take control, making a plan of action with you.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Compassion and active listening are learnable skills, not fixed personality traits, and can be taught in residency.
pearls.verbatim: I literally trained people to sit and listen. And that that was, like, week one. Let's learn how to sit and listen, right, and be present with the patient.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Use the 'triple e's' (excuse, empathize, explain) when you need to interrupt a patient who is talking too long.
pearls.verbatim: Excuse, empathize, and explain. Right? I'm sorry. I I need to interrupt you. I just wanna talk about it. It's really important. But let's let's get back to this topic that we were talking about.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: When taking notes during a patient visit, pause to tell the patient you want to make sure you record what they said, then turn back to them to maintain connection.
pearls.verbatim: Hold hold on one second. I wanna make sure I get that down. Right? But you said it's really important. Wanna make sure I record that and get back with them.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Compassion is essential in medicine; without it, burnout will come faster and you may not recover.
pearls.verbatim: If you function in medicine without it, I can promise you you'll burn out a lot faster, and there won't... You may not come back from it.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Know your limits and be okay with them; you don't have to do everything.
pearls.verbatim: We have to know our limits, and we have to be okay with that.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: When addressing systemic issues, focus on the 'how' not just the 'what'.
pearls.verbatim: It's not the what. It's the how.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: If a retreat itself is more stressful than the job, it is not effective.
pearls.verbatim: Retreat is more stressful than the job. That's not good.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: When you feel empty, pray: 'I don't have anything in my bucket, but God, you are an ocean of love. I go to you to fill my bucket.'
pearls.verbatim: I don't have anything in my bucket, but, God, I know that that you are an ocean of love, and there's... All I have to go is go to you so I can fill that bucket.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Connections

pearls.text: Repeated exposure through media and video does not meet DSM-5 Criterion A for PTSD unless it is for work purposes. This case should be diagnosed as adjustment disorder, not PTSD.
pearls.verbatim: The traumatic exposure criteria for that, and repeated exposure through media and video does not count unless it's for a work purpose. And we don't think that he meets that criteria.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: PTSD trauma exposure must be either direct experience, witnessing, or learning of trauma to a close person; media exposure does not count unless work-related.
pearls.verbatim: PTSD trauma exposure must be either direct experience witnessing the event, learning that the trauma occurred to someone who's really close or a close a close family member or close friend who are experiencing repeated or extreme exposure to aversive details of the traumatic event.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Adjustment disorder with anxiety means out of proportion distress and functional impairment after a stressor.
pearls.verbatim: It means he has out of proportion distress and functional impairment after a stressor.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Further evaluate for PTSD even if the current trauma does not meet criteria, as there may be past exposures.
pearls.verbatim: Further evaluation for PTSD. Keep that in mind because there may be some other things he has been exposed to.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Substance use is the x factor that complicates all other mental health treatment.
pearls.verbatim: Substance use is the... It's the x factor for everything.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: If a patient has a major substance use issue, you usually cannot make progress on other things until that is addressed.
pearls.verbatim: If I have someone who has a major substance use issue, I'm not just talking about little bit of stuff. I'm not... That's a problem. I can't... I usually can't make much progress on any of other things till we get that dealt with, just so you know.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: For adolescents, the time frame for cyclothymic disorder is one year (half of adult duration), and symptoms must be present for at least six months.
pearls.verbatim: For adolescents, you can have half of one year for adolescents. It can be six months. You can have it for six months for an adolescent because the criteria is one year for adolescent.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Cyclothymic disorder does not match the intensity of bipolar I but can cause significant distress, especially in adolescents.
pearls.verbatim: cyclothymic disorder can be seen as a disorder that does not match the intensity of bipolar one. It can cause significant distress, though.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Consider a media fast or social media fast as a lifestyle intervention.
pearls.verbatim: Media fast. Social media fast, perhaps.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: In adolescents with mood symptoms and ADHD, prioritize mood stabilization over ADHD treatment.
pearls.verbatim: Mood stabilization, a priority over ADHD
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: If mood cycling continues off stimulants, the ADHD diagnosis may need reassessment, as mood extremes themselves impair attention.
pearls.verbatim: If the moods are still going like this while she's off of it, what's going on with her attention?
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Hypercarbia from respiratory distress can impair cognition and decision-making, so neuropsych assessment is warranted.
pearls.verbatim: Hypercarbia... That could be impairing her her thought processes, right, how she's thinking, her decision making.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Psychological Factors Affecting Other Medical Conditions is the appropriate DSM-5 diagnosis when psychological/behavioral factors exacerbate a medical condition, not somatic symptom disorder or factitious disorder.
pearls.verbatim: Symptoms fit. This one is actually in the DSM. Psychological factors affecting other medical conditions.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: Home visits can provide critical insight into a patient's environment and treatment adherence, especially in complex psychosocial cases.
pearls.verbatim: Consider a home visit. Hey. You guys you got a family doctor. You guys can do those things.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Exploring Clinical Cases Using the DSM-5 11/13/25

pearls.text: If patients do not leave with expectation and hope, they are unlikely to return for follow-up.
pearls.verbatim: if they don't leave with expectation and hope, expectation of change and hope, they're not gonna come back.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Keep asking some version of 'Is there something else?' until the patient says no to ensure all concerns are elicited.
pearls.verbatim: And then you keep asking some version of, is there something else till they stop, until they say, no. That's it.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Do not dive into the patient's agenda until their list of concerns is complete, even if they give many items.
pearls.verbatim: Do not dive in until this list is complete, even if they give you a thousand of them.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Use the three Es (Excuse, Empathize, Explain) to politely interrupt a patient and redirect the conversation.
pearls.verbatim: Excuse, empathize, and explain.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Use open-ended questions like 'What do you mean by that?' or 'Explain that to me' to elicit more information and avoid fear of opening Pandora's box.
pearls.verbatim: Well, what do you mean by that? Like, asking open questions. Yeah. And not being afraid of us. Explain that to me.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Attending means being fully present: listen, lean in, make eye contact, and avoid being on the computer.
pearls.verbatim: Attending, what does it mean to attend? Just hearing about it. Being present. Listening, leaning in a little bit, you know, just being actually present, not not on your computer.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Reflection of meaning involves reflecting back what the patient's words actually mean to them, not just the content.
pearls.verbatim: What a reflection of meaning is they'll say something, a whole bunch of stuff, and you reflect what it actually means to them or to you. Right? Not just reflect the content itself.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Keep self-disclosure shallow; avoid sharing your deepest, darkest personal experiences.
pearls.verbatim: Self disclosure, you're probably gonna keep them pretty shallow. You're not gonna tell your deepest, darkest stuff.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Use confrontation or challenge when a patient's harmful behavior needs to be addressed directly, e.g., 'This is literally killing you.'
pearls.verbatim: Challenge them or confront them about things they're not doing. Well, you know, maybe you you really need to stop this really bad behavior because it's literally killing you. And I need to tell you that.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: BATHE is a one-to-five-minute, noninvasive screening tool for psychological distress that can be used with patients, friends, or family.
pearls.verbatim: BATHE is a simple procedure devised by a physician, I will say. It takes anywhere from one to five minutes, and you use it with patients, friends, or family who appear to be in psychological distress.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: The purpose of BATHE is to create a structure to understand the cause of distress and communicate empathy.
pearls.verbatim: The purpose is to create a structure for you to develop an understanding of what is causing the person to be distressed and then to communicate your understanding and empathy to the person.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Using BATHE does not add time to your visit; it may replace small talk and prevent patients from bringing up emotional issues at the end.
pearls.verbatim: research says that using BATHE does not add time to your visit. That's probably because it's very quick and may take the place of other small talk that takes up the same time, and it may keep the patient from slow... Slowing the visit down by bringing up emotional issues toward the end or in an indirect way.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Use an empathic closing statement like 'That sounds really stressful. Let's come back around and talk about that next time too.'
pearls.verbatim: That sounds really stressful. Please let me know how to deal with that and how you're dealing with that. And let's let's come back around and talk about that next time too.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: The 'E' part is empathy and exit: demonstrate understanding and then close the inquiry to move to the medical issue.
pearls.verbatim: The e part is crucial for you to finish with because it demonstrates understanding and your connection with them, and it allows you to close out the inquirer.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Use these skills selectively when the patient's complaints fit into the management plan.
pearls.verbatim: there's times where complaints or concerns the patients have where this would fit into the management of that
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Ask patients 'What troubles you the most about that?' and 'How are you handling it?' to deepen the therapeutic relationship.
pearls.verbatim: What troubles you the most about that, and how are you handling it?
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on Foundational Skills for Physician Counseling

pearls.text: Assess for elder abuse risk by asking if the caregiver has become so exasperated that they have gotten violent.
pearls.verbatim: Have you ever known of caregiver to get so exasperated that they get violent? Right? They get violent, and they have to do with elder care or elder abuse.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Ask explicitly about alone time and respite; 24/7 care without breaks is a major risk for burnout.
pearls.verbatim: Does she have any alone time? Is she with him twenty four seven? Right. And that's particularly true for some for some personalities. Right? Like, they really need alone time, and others need less fun. When you're done at this much, even your extroverts who like to be around people are gonna be like, somebody tag me out of this. Right? I'm done. Need a break.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Encourage involvement in caregiver support groups like Al-Anon to provide peer support.
pearls.verbatim: Is there, like, a caregiver support group like Al Anon? That's a great point. So you... There are... In some communities, you can find that.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Simplify medication regimens when possible; consider the burden on caregivers who manage both their own and the patient's medications.
pearls.verbatim: Be thinking about that when you're thinking about some medication that has to be taken three times a day or whatever.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Chronic hypervigilance in caregivers leads to persistently high cortisol levels, increasing risk for anxiety, depression, and poor quality of life.
pearls.verbatim: So there's an underlying stress. Mhmm. So what's going on physic... Physically or physiologically? Aortisol. Aortisol levels were, like, constantly high. Right? So then we have the ramifications of that, right, which could be many. Right? Anxiety, depression, so forth.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Ask caregivers directly about their support system: 'Who's got you?' or 'Who's taking care of you?' to identify isolation and risk for burnout.
pearls.verbatim: Who's got you, basically? Right? We're taking care of you. Great question.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Role captivity is a strong predictor of caregiver stress; ask if they feel stuck in their role.
pearls.verbatim: They feel stuck in there.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: The caregiver may express role captivity as 'I am a prisoner in my own home' – a red flag for severe stress.
pearls.verbatim: I am a prisoner in my own home
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Use the simple question 'How do you feel like you're doing?' to open a conversation about caregiver competence and struggles.
pearls.verbatim: How do you feel like you're doing?
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Schedule regular follow-up appointments to track caregiver health, as chronic stress elevates cortisol and worsens physical conditions.
pearls.verbatim: regular follow ups to track health, their health, their physical health, because they're on... Remember, cortisol levels, etcetera, constantly high
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: A key resource for any caregiver is the Alzheimer's Association website (alz.org), which offers broad support beyond just Alzheimer's.
pearls.verbatim: go to alzheimer's.org
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Clinicians should follow up with caregivers by asking about their next steps, such as checking out Life Senior Services or other resources, to ensure they are connected.
pearls.verbatim: I would encourage you to to do that. Say, tell me what you're doing next with support group. Have you checked out Life Senior Services or or healthcare.gov or whichever one?
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: To efficiently connect caregivers to resources, clinicians can delegate the task of looking up local community resources to a medical assistant or office staff.
pearls.verbatim: You might employ a MA to to look some of these things up. Right? Or another office there or something.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Medicare and insurance typically cover home health services (medication management, toileting, showering) for only a few hours a couple times a week, not 24-hour care.
pearls.verbatim: You can get home health, which is medication management, help with, like, toileting, getting a shower, and that's going for a couple hours a couple times a week. So that's not, like, twenty four hour care you're paying out of pocket.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: Patients with end-stage dementia (stage 7) who are nearly comatose and cannot speak may qualify for hospice, which provides a separate set of resources.
pearls.verbatim: if they're an end stage dementia, like, stage seven that are not then they could be likely to qualify for hospice. And then that... That's a whole another set of resources.
pearls.speaker: Simpson
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Simpson on The Caregiver Role in Neurocognitive Disorders

pearls.text: In chronic hyperbilirubinemia, bilirubin binds to albumin, so even after fixing the cause, the bilirubin may remain elevated until the albumin is recycled.
pearls.verbatim: If somebody has that chronic hyperbilirubinemia, you can get basically to the albumin. And so even if you fixed the underlying cause, you may have a persistently elevated bilirubin until the albumin has been recycled.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: If a stone is seen on any imaging modality in a patient with suspected choledocholithiasis, proceed directly to ERCP without MRCP.
pearls.verbatim: If you have it on any of those imaging modalities, if you see a stone on there, you can proceed directly to ERCP. You don't have to get an MRCP to confirm it.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: Acute cholangitis is an indication to go straight to ERCP without further imaging.
pearls.verbatim: Or if they've got acute cholangitis, that's the reason you can go straight to ERCP.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: A bilirubin above 4 with a significantly dilated common bile duct on ultrasound meets high-risk criteria for choledocholithiasis.
pearls.verbatim: Or if your cerebelli is above four and you have a pre significantly dilated common bile duct on ultrasound.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: When ERCP is not possible due to patient instability, place an external biliary drain to decompress and clear infection.
pearls.verbatim: if you can't do that or for some reason you can't go to the ERCP because they're too sick, you can put an external biliary drain in.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: In a clinically stable patient with low-to-intermediate risk of CBD stone, intraoperative cholangiography can be performed during cholecystectomy to assess for obstruction.
pearls.verbatim: Intraoperative cholangiography. So, you know, they're clinically stable for cholecystectomy. You're not, like, super concerned that they've... At this risk that there's a CBD stone, but it's not super high, then then they can improperly inject dye into the biliary tree and see if there's obstruction or not.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: Pancreatic head tumors cause jaundice because the head is close to the biliary tree, so painless jaundice should raise suspicion for pancreatic head malignancy.
pearls.verbatim: The majority of it is gonna be in the pancreatic head, especially if it's causing jaundice. Right? Because the head is what's actually close to biliary tree.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: Vascular encasement or invasion of the tumor is a contraindication to resection because you cannot dissect it away from sensitive structures.
pearls.verbatim: You can get vascular encasement yet invasion where it's... You're not gonna be able to dissect it away from other very sensitive structures.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: Small, non-functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors can be monitored with surveillance rather than immediate resection, as they are less aggressive.
pearls.verbatim: So if they're real small and they're not active, you can monitor them. You can survey them.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: In intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, an elevated AFP level helps differentiate it from other liver masses; if AFP is elevated, it is more likely to be a hepatocellular carcinoma rather than cholangiocarcinoma.
pearls.verbatim: So that AFP level can help you know if it's more or less likely a cholangiocarcinoma. Right? If PSF, it's gonna be more likely.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: The IBS smart test is proprietary and costs $250; LabCorp cannot perform it.
pearls.verbatim: LabCorp can't do IBS smart test. You have to pay $250 to the people that developed it and get the anti
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: Anti-IgE monoclonal antibodies improved asthma and resulted in almost complete resolution of IBS in patients with both conditions.
pearls.verbatim: administration of anti IgE monoclonal antibodies not only improved asthma, because we said it was the same disease process, just different tissue, but also resulted in almost complete resolution.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: If a patient has both asthma and IBS, anti-IgE therapy can fix their IBS, but it is not approved for IBS alone.
pearls.verbatim: It means if somebody has both asthma or one of the approved indications for it, that you can fix their IBS as well.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: Historic therapies for IBS include stress reduction, soluble fiber, probiotics, MiraLAX, bromide, and bile acid sequestrants.
pearls.verbatim: Stress reduction, soluble fiber, probiotics, MiraLAX, bromide, and bile acid sequestrants. You still have to remember that. You still have to use that.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: An IgG elimination diet involves blood testing, eliminating positive foods, reintroducing them, and monitoring symptoms.
pearls.verbatim: Doing an IgG elimination diet. So you do the blood test. You find out what the IgG panel shows is positive. You eliminate that. You do a reintroduction, and you monitor their symptoms, and you can re... Redo their blood testing.
pearls.speaker: Slaughter
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Slaughter, DO on Extrahepatic Cholestasis

pearls.text: Avoid applying dung or other non-sterile substances to wounds; they introduce spores and increase infection risk.
pearls.verbatim: the traditional treatment of a donkey bite is to put donkey dung on the... As a kind of, you know, paste. It's not quite neosporin. You know? It's a little bit... In fact, it has plenty of spores in it.
pearls.speaker: Unknown

pearls.text: Building trust with patients through demonstrated care and competence can enable them to accept difficult but necessary treatments.
pearls.verbatim: she trusted that I cared about her, that I knew what I was doing, and that was what motivated her, enabled her to make such an amazingly difficult decision.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #1: Going Deeper in Trust 1/16/26

pearls.text: Take a trust inventory by asking yourself if you really, really believe in God's goodness and ability.
pearls.verbatim: it's worthwhile taking a little trust inventory and saying, you know, do I really, really, really believe?

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #1: Going Deeper in Trust 1/16/26

pearls.text: The worthiness of our trust depends on the worthiness of the object of our trust, not the strength of our believing.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #1: Going Deeper in Trust 1/16/26

pearls.text: When the big noise is coming, look to the shepherd and trust the shepherd, and be at peace because the shepherd is at peace.
pearls.verbatim: when the big noise is coming, we look to the shepherd, and we trust the shepherd. And we can be at peace because the shepherd is at peace.

pearls.text: Trust is not needing more information about Christ, but trusting more deeply the information you already have.
