pearls.text: Childlike surrender and trust is the defining spirit of authentic discipleship and often the most overlooked need.
pearls.verbatim: childlike surrender and trust is the defining spirit of authentic discipleship, The supreme need in most of our lives and often the most overlooked is trust.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: Trust ultimately depends on the worthiness of the object of trust, not on the intensity of your own effort.
pearls.verbatim: trust ultimately depends not so much on that really, really believing as if we have to kind of grit our teeth and really, really believe, but on the worthiness of the object of that trust.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: There are different expressions of trust in Scripture; peaceful trust (Isaiah 26:3) is one, but trust can also coexist with deep sorrow, as seen in Jesus in Gethsemane.
pearls.verbatim: I think about Jesus in the Garden Of Gethsemane, and he trusted the father, didn't he? Absolutely. But when he walked into the Garden Of Gethsemane with this poignant statement, my soul is overwhelmed with sorrow, and he sweat drops of blood. That was not exactly the same picture as his grandson in the arms. And yet I think it was trust.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: When a child develops unilateral weakness and papilledema in a resource-limited setting, immediate medical evacuation is indicated.
pearls.verbatim: She was becoming paralyzed one side of her her body. And so I knew once she alerted me of that, I knew, oh my goodness. Something really neurological is going on. I need to do a full blown neurological exam, so I did. And sure enough, she was weak on the left side of her body. And I looked in her eye, did the eye exam, a fundoscopic exam, and I saw, which a clear sign that I'd almost never seen in residency or medical school in real life, which was florid papilledema, bilateral florid papilledema. It was just huge. And I knew right then and there, oh my goodness. There is something going on in my daughter in my daughter's head. Tumor, infection, whatever it was, it was pressure, and it needed... I knew we needed a CT scan, maybe a pediatric neurosurgeon, and none of those... The whole country of Chad didn't have. At that point in time, Chad didn't have a single CT scan. We were three days from the nearest international airport, much less back to The USA where we could get medical help. And so we knew, okay, this is medical evacuation time.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: The prayer 'Lord, I believe; help my unbelief' is a good prayer because Jesus knows we are sometimes not completely peaceful in trust; He answers that prayer.
pearls.verbatim: Lord, I believe. Help me in my unbelief. Lord, I believe. Same word is used for belief and trust. Help me un... Overcome my unbelief. Help me to trust. Because... And Jesus wonderfully, he answered that prayer.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: When no anesthesiologist is available, ketamine can be used for anesthesia in a resource-limited setting, even if the nurses have little training.
pearls.verbatim: Unfortunately, we had some ketamine, and no... None of the nurses really knew much. But, anyway, it was a crazy situation.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: To cultivate deeper trust, write a personal 'Habakkuk pledge': identify a painful possible outcome and ask yourself, 'Even if ___, will I trust the Lord?' If you can say 'yet I will trust Him,' it moves you toward even-if trust.
pearls.verbatim: A helpful reflective question sometimes we've done is the Habakkuk question and is to write yourself a pledge. You know, sometimes we think about what might be a very painful thing that might happen to us. And we ask ourselves, even if you fill in the blank, will I trust the Lord? And if you can, even with a part of your soul, say, yet I will trust him. It's a very powerful statement to say, yes, Lord.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: Blessed are those who trust God without seeing Him, as Jesus said: 'Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.' This enables trust in the darkness.
pearls.verbatim: Thomas, you have seen, and therefore, have believed. But blessed are those who have not seen and have yet bestowed, have believed, have trusted. Because that's a wonderful... That's a blessed state. When you get to the point where you can trust god, even though you don't see him, then you can trust him in the darkness.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #2: Biblical Types of Trust 1/17/26

pearls.text: Be aware of your own and your patients' cultural 'uncertainty avoidance'; some patients need more structured plans and explicit certainty than others.
pearls.verbatim: And as you can imagine, different cultures are all across across the board. And there are some cultures that really, really wanna avoid uncertainty.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #3: Trust and Uncertainty 1/17/26

pearls.text: When you have a patient in front of you, tell yourself there is no 100% guarantee this treatment will be effective; avoid overpromising outcomes.
pearls.verbatim: there is no 100% guarantee that this treatment is going to be effective
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #3: Trust and Uncertainty 1/17/26

pearls.text: Never assume 100% control or efficiency for an individual patient, even when the data are strong.
pearls.verbatim: There is never 100% control or efficiency.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #3: Trust and Uncertainty 1/17/26

pearls.text: In medicine and faith, risk is obedience in uncertainty; you can act faithfully without knowing how the case will turn out.
pearls.verbatim: biblical risk, I think this was John Piper who said this, is actually obedience in uncertainty
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #3: Trust and Uncertainty 1/17/26

pearls.text: Trust means being so certain of some things or someone that we can move forward even if uncertain in other things.
pearls.verbatim: trust means being so certain of some things or someone, maybe better say someone, that we can move forward even if uncertain in other things.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #3: Trust and Uncertainty 1/17/26

pearls.text: Even if we don't know the way, he knows the way, and he is with us.
pearls.verbatim: even if we don't know the way, he knows the way, and he is with us.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #3: Trust and Uncertainty 1/17/26

pearls.text: Christ is worthy of our absolute trust.
pearls.verbatim: Christ is worthy of our absolute trust.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Sutton Lecture #3: Trust and Uncertainty 1/17/26

pearls.text: For dacryostenosis, perform lacrimal massage with light downward pressure over the nasolacrimal duct area three to five times, three times daily.
pearls.verbatim: you kind of put light pressure kind of in this area and do downward pressure. You do that three to five times about three times daily of that type of pressure
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Disease 12/18/25

pearls.text: A dacrocystocele (swelling over the tear duct) requires immediate ophthalmology referral.
pearls.verbatim: The times to be concerned is whenever they have a dacrocysto... Cystocele, and that's basically where there is swelling.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Disease 12/18/25

pearls.text: If no red reflex is detected, call ophthalmology immediately for same-day evaluation.
pearls.verbatim: if you see no red reflex, Call ophthalmology right away and get them in right away.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Disease 12/18/25

pearls.text: Congenital glaucoma clues: excessive tearing, photophobia, eye rubbing, and cloudy cornea.
pearls.verbatim: They also have sensitivity to light. That's key. They'll be rubbing on their eyes a lot, and they could have a cloudy cornea.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Disease 12/18/25

pearls.text: Orbital cellulitis is suggested by severe pain, ptosis, pain with eye movements, and vision changes.
pearls.verbatim: Generally, orbital cellulitis, you'll have pain... A lot more pain. You can have ptosis. Pain with eye movements is key. Vision changes.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Disease 12/18/25

pearls.text: Contact lens users with conjunctivitis need antibiotic drops that cover Pseudomonas.
pearls.verbatim: If the patient is a contact user, they do need pseudomonas coverage with their eye drops.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Disease 12/18/25

pearls.text: When patching, use a pressure patch that keeps the eye closed, not a pirate patch which can be opened and cause more damage.
pearls.verbatim: Not the pirate patch. I heard that that actually can cause more problems and more damage to their eye because the kids are able to open their eye. You want something that'll kind of keep their eye closed and bring them back within twenty four to forty eight hours.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Disease 12/18/25

pearls.text: For dacryostenosis, perform pressure massage three to five times about three times daily by applying light downward pressure over the lacrimal sac.
pearls.verbatim: you kind of put light pressure kind of in this area and do downward pressure. You do that three to five times about three times daily of that type of pressure, and you have the parents do that.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Diseases 1/15/26

pearls.text: For preseptal cellulitis in children under 8 years, cephalexin is the preferred oral antibiotic.
pearls.verbatim: for kids less than eight, cephalexin would be the next choice.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Diseases 1/15/26

pearls.text: In contact lens users with conjunctivitis, antibiotic eye drops must cover Pseudomonas.
pearls.verbatim: if the patient is a contact user, they do need pseudomonas coverage with their eye drops.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Diseases 1/15/26

pearls.text: For chalazion on the upper eyelid, instruct patients to massage by moving the finger downward and then outward to facilitate drainage.
pearls.verbatim: you hold your finger and you kinda go, like, down and then out. That's, like, the direction that the chalazia drain if it's on the top lid.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Diseases 1/15/26

pearls.text: If corneal involvement exceeds 50%, cycloplegic drops such as homatropine can be used in pediatrics.
pearls.verbatim: if the cornea involvement is severe, it's over fifty percent of the cornea, you can, you know, give cycloplegic drops. Homatropine is what they prefer in pediatrics.
pearls.speaker: Swan
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Swan on Pediatric Eye Diseases 1/15/26

pearls.text: The Greek word 'herkypto' means to thoroughly examine, like flipping over a patient in the hospital to find the cause of a problem.
pearls.verbatim: the Greek word there is called herkypto. And so it's a term that's like, you, like, thoroughly examine
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: A performative culture in medicine can make you base your value on your last rotation or a bad review, but that is not true.
pearls.verbatim: a lot of times, depending on how how you're doing is depending on, hey. How was my last rotation? How was my score? How was my... You know? And that reflects on how how am I as a person? What is my And none of that's true
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: Perfectionism in medicine can lead to mulling over outcomes and feeling like a failure; remember that a person's days are determined by God.
pearls.verbatim: a person's days are determined, you have decreed the number this month, and you have set limits you cannot exceed.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: You don't need to burden or collect yourself and then come to Jesus; your very burden is what qualifies you to come.
pearls.verbatim: you don't need to burden or collect yourself and then come to Jesus. Your very burden is what qualifies you to come.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: When we choose to come to Him in our weakness or sin, that actually glorifies Him more because it puts Him in His right spot as the ultimate provider of mercy and grace.
pearls.verbatim: when we choose to come to him in our weakness or in our sin or anything, like, that actually glorifies him more. It puts him in his right spot.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: Come to Jesus repeatedly with your struggles; He never tires of it and it gives Him honor.
pearls.verbatim: Come to me. Doesn't matter how many times. The more times I can come to him and just say, man, God, I need you this day. Like, this is this is where I'm struggling even though it's again a second time. But he doesn't grow tired of that.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: Christ's joy increases the more the sick come to Him for help – that's the whole reason He came; do not get frustrated when you need to come for forgiveness again.
pearls.verbatim: His joy increases the degree that the sick come to him for help and healing. It's the whole reason he came.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: When your soul is cast down, preach to it: 'Why are you cast down, O my soul? Put your hope in God.' Use Scripture to redirect your thoughts.
pearls.verbatim: Why are you cast down on my soul? Why are you in turmoil with it? Be hope in God, for I shall again trace in my salvation of my God.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: Thankfulness is a soil in which pride does not easily grow; cultivate gratitude in all circumstances as God's will for you.
pearls.verbatim: Thankfulness is a soil in which pride does not easily grow. First Thessalonians five sixteen two, give thanks in all circumstances, but this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: Give thanks in all circumstances as a command and a truth that cultivates the heart for hardship.
pearls.verbatim: give thanks in all circumstances. So that's, again, that's that's starting to cultivate that heart and the soul for when those times come.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: At the wedding at Cana, Jesus had the servants fill jars with water—simple obedience that He turned into wine.
pearls.verbatim: Why did Jesus have the servants do what they did? ... Fill the jars with water. ... Can you imagine if it hadn't looked like wine yet?
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: When sharing faith or praying with patients, it feels like throwing water; but God makes it wine—life from our small acts.
pearls.verbatim: It feels like I just threw some water on that person. ... It's wine inside of them. It's life.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Abiding in Christ

pearls.text: You cannot diagnose COPD without spirometry; clinical suspicion alone is insufficient. The diagnostic criterion is a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio less than 0.7.
pearls.verbatim: you can have clinical suspicion of it. So we have that in oftentimes in the hospital, right, people that come in and you're like, extremely wheezy, and they smoke for forty years. So you can say you have a suspicion for COPD, but you cannot diagnose them with COPD. So you must have spirometry to establish diagnosis.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: The key question for the mMRC scale is whether the patient gets more breathless than others of the same age and has to stop when walking at a regular pace. A positive answer indicates more severe symptoms (grade ≥2).
pearls.verbatim: The question that you probably wanna ask people is this one, where you say, you know, if people the same age, so I get more breathless than I am, and I have to stop when I'm just doing kinda like a regular pace. So the positive for that, they have been more severe based on this scaling criteria.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: The CAT (COPD Assessment Test) score of 10 or more indicates more severe symptoms and helps classify patients into Group B or E.
pearls.verbatim: 10 points or more is more severe symptoms.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: To classify severity, ask patients if they have had exacerbations requiring steroids or antibiotics, or any hospitalization for COPD in the past year. Two moderate exacerbations or one hospitalization places them in Group E.
pearls.verbatim: If they've had two moderate exacerbations or one leading to hospitalization, so this is per year on average, their median e is the most severe.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: A moderate exacerbation is defined as one treated with steroids or antibiotics, not necessarily requiring hospitalization. Ask patients: 'Have you ever needed steroids for this condition?'
pearls.verbatim: Moderate too, just to let you know, is you are treated with steroids or antibiotics for an exacerbation. So I mean, doesn't necessarily mean hospitalization. Just moderate. So you wanna ask them, hey. Have you ever needed steroids for this this condition?
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: Inhaled corticosteroids are no longer first-line for COPD; LAMA and LABA combinations are the mainstay. Triple therapy (ICS/LAMA/LABA) is reserved for specific indications.
pearls.verbatim: steroids used to always be kind of... Do this combination, long acting beta agonist and steroid. Right? That's super common. So that is actually being moved away from and in favor of llamas and llamas. That is the the mainstay of treatment.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: Long-term oxygen therapy does not confer a mortality benefit for patients with isolated ambulatory desaturation; it is only indicated for severe resting desaturation.
pearls.verbatim: So they say don't routinely do it. So not everybody should... You can automatically give them oxygen to. So maybe our hospital patients, you would say consider that, but this is talking about long term oxygen. So just because they're in your office doing well and they walk and it drops, you no no longer need to be getting the oxygen routine.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: Pulmonary rehabilitation within 90 days of hospital discharge is associated with a statistically significant reduction in mortality.
pearls.verbatim: If they did it within ninety days of discharge from the hospital, associated with a statistically significant reduced mortality.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: All patients diagnosed with COPD should be screened once for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, as it changes management.
pearls.verbatim: Who recommends everybody that has a diagnosis of CBD should be screened once or often one Wow. That makes sense. Yep. Okay. Because we can notice it, and it does change what we do for that.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: There is no significant difference in outcomes between MDI and nebulizer for treating COPD exacerbations; choice depends on patient tolerance.
pearls.verbatim: No significant difference between MDI or nebulizer. Whoo. Gold says so.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: For acute COPD exacerbation, prednisone 40 mg for 5 days is recommended per GOLD guidelines.
pearls.verbatim: Steroids, forty milligrams for five days. That's what's recommended for gold.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: Antibiotics for COPD exacerbation are indicated when there is increased sputum purulence, especially if combined with increased sputum volume or increased dyspnea.
pearls.verbatim: They have to have increased sputum. Increased sputum has to be one of them. And then you either need increased Dyspnea. Sputum volume or increased dyspnea. Yep. But it has to be increased sputum purulence.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on COPD

pearls.text: Use finger pad or thumb pad to palpate tender points, not jabbing with fingertips, to avoid causing excessive pain.
pearls.verbatim: Using your finger pad or thumb pad is best instead of jabbing it with your finger pad.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: When multiple tender points are present, treat the most tender one first, then reassess and treat others.
pearls.verbatim: find the most tender spot, treat that one first, and then go back to the other one.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Return the patient to neutral very slowly, especially the first 15 degrees, to avoid re-triggering the protective muscle reflex.
pearls.verbatim: the first, like, 15 degrees of going back into your neutral position was important. So making sure that you would go incredibly slow coming out of that, like, initial area of strain
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Teach patients with upper back tightness to self-treat at home by lying prone with arms crossed and a pillow under the chest for a few minutes.
pearls.verbatim: I teach patients that sometimes too. If they're like, man, I always get that. I'm like, at home, you know, just kinda put your arms on on the bed like this and put a pillow under you.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Recent surgery or trauma within 3 months is a key risk factor for VTE; immobilization risk is within 2 days.
pearls.verbatim: That's gonna be within three months, typically. Three is a common number if you think of that through... Runs through a lot of things in the PPP stuff. So two days for immobilization, three months for recent hospitalization or surgery.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Increased calf circumference of 3 cm or more (measured 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity) is the most useful physical exam finding for DVT.
pearls.verbatim: And the literature is towards three centimeters difference. I mean, it's enough that you can look at and say, You know? But some people have just big right caps that just only work out. Mhmm. So... But that change, though, a three is significant enough. So... And this is based on 10 centimeters below the tibial tuberosity.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Tachypnea is the most common PE exam finding (54%); tachycardia is present in only 24% of PE patients.
pearls.verbatim: Look at tachycardia. Twenty four percent of patients have a tachycardia. Like, honestly, that was a lot less than I had thought when I was kinda looking through this in my mind before this.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Fever occurs in only 3% of PE patients; do not rely on fever to raise or lower suspicion for PE.
pearls.verbatim: And so fever is 3%. Don't hang your hat on couple of these things and say, like, hey. They don't... They're not tachycardic.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Clinical pretest probability should guide testing: low probability warrants a high-sensitivity test; high probability warrants a more specific test.
pearls.verbatim: If you have a low retest probability, then your screening test is less useful. So it's going to miss some... So if you just screen everybody and you haven't assessed their pretest probability, then it's not gonna be a great test.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Normal sinus rhythm is the most common EKG finding in PE, not S1Q3T3.
pearls.verbatim: I'll give you points if you said normal sinus rhythm because that is that is the most common finding.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Purple color changes in the leg (phlegmasia cerulea dolens) warrant immediate ER referral.
pearls.verbatim: If you're looking at the leg and it's like, hold on. I'm seeing purple color changes there. Just thinking about it. Let's go to the ER.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Moderate or high risk VTE patients (malignancy, renal disease, on oxygen) should be started on heparin.
pearls.verbatim: For moderate or high risk patients, these are the ones that were like, man, you got significant diseases, malignancy, kidney problems. You're on oxygen. What are we treating them with? Heparin.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Apixaban is preferred over rivaroxaban for outpatient VTE treatment due to better safety profile.
pearls.verbatim: If you can give them rivaroxaban or Xarelto, that's great. If it's availability cost wise, but if you can choose one, Eliquis has better better background.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Isolated distal DVT (calf only) may be managed with observation if bleeding risk is high.
pearls.verbatim: Really mild if it's only a distal DVT, so just confined to the calf, just those veins alone, you may consider observation.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: For unprovoked VTE, indefinite anticoagulation is the standard recommendation, especially for men.
pearls.verbatim: If it's unprovoked, we don't know why the recommendation now is indefinite, especially for males females.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Provoked VTE due to persistent risk (cancer, autoimmune) is treated indefinitely, with periodic reassessment.
pearls.verbatim: Last one, provoked. They have a reason why. They're like, yeah. They got cancer. They're autoimmune. What is your... I guess we already have it. Likely indefinite
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: HERDOO2 criteria include a D-dimer level, BMI <30, and age <65 (HSV <65 in transcript).
pearls.verbatim: You check a D dimer level. Their BMI has to be less than 30, and their HSV less than 65.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: For men with unprovoked VTE, indefinite anticoagulation is recommended; the HERDOO2 score is not used for men.
pearls.verbatim: Males, sorry. The recommendation number for unprovoked is to stay on it indefinitely.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Standard cancer screening is performed for all unprovoked VTE; thrombophilia workup is not routine but reserved for younger patients, family history, or atypical features.
pearls.verbatim: If unprovoked... So you don't know why actually we work up everybody for cancer. Standard screening. ... But it's not standard. It's not everybody that's unprovoked worthwhile going through that.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Provoked VTE with a removable trigger (e.g., surgery, estrogen) is treated for 3 months.
pearls.verbatim: If you had a trigger removed and no persistent risk, sorry, three months.

pearls.text: Clinical gestalt and risk scores like Wells criteria guide outpatient management and testing decisions.
pearls.verbatim: Your goal is to keep... Stay aware of this, understand, you know, some of these histories and especially risk factors and say, hey. This is enough that I'm gonna go ahead and pursue that route of saying I'm gonna go that route for WellScore.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Counterstrain

pearls.text: Erythema in gout is typically confined to the joint area, unlike cellulitis where redness spreads more broadly.
pearls.verbatim: So this picture right down here, right, you're gonna get the redness just around that MTP joint compared to cellulitis, some of those other ones where it's gonna be much more broad.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Serum urate can be normal during an acute flare in up to 40% of cases; do not rule out gout based on a normal level.
pearls.verbatim: Up to forty percent of gout flares will have normal urine. Your body gets in kind of this proinflammatory state. So the thought is like the uric acid level go down and forms the crystals, and so your levels actually can be normal during forty percent of flare.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Check serum urate two weeks or more after a flare for accurate baseline; levels during the flare are unreliable.
pearls.verbatim: And then I add that on there two weeks or more after flare. That's when it's the most common time.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: The acute gout diagnosis rule (MDCalc) uses male sex, prior arthritis flare, onset within one day, chronic rash, and serum uric acid to stratify probability.
pearls.verbatim: It's called acute gout diagnosis rule. So this takes a history. So you can can look through these, male sex, previous arthritis flare, onset within one day, chronic rash. Everything we talked about in the hypertension risk factors, and then the serum urine level.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Colchicine is most effective if started within 24 hours of flare onset.
pearls.verbatim: Colchicine, most effective if it's within twenty four hours. So that's kind of important.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Colchicine dosing: 1.2 mg then 0.6 mg one hour later, then 0.6 mg BID until flare resolves or up to 14 days.
pearls.verbatim: You give them one point two milligrams, and then an hour later, you give point six. I don't know why we decided that, but that's what it is. And then it's point six milligrams twice a day until the flare resolves or up to fourteen days.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: NSAIDs are reserved for patients younger than 60 with no kidney disease, no cardiac disease, and no active GI disease or gastritis.
pearls.verbatim: they kinda say reserve the NSAIDs for those if they're younger than 60. They got no kidney disease. They got no cardiac disease, and they have no active GI disease or gastritis.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Target urate level is less than 6 mg/dL, or less than 5 mg/dL if tophi present.
pearls.verbatim: the target level that you wanna lower to them is less than six, and then a tophi is gonna be less than five.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Continue prophylaxis for 3 months after achieving urate goal, or 6 months if tophi resolution.
pearls.verbatim: Once they get their urate (correct) level achieved, it's three months after that. Or if they got to a five, you wanna do it at least six months.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Probenecid is third-line; it increases uric acid excretion but carries a high risk of kidney stones.
pearls.verbatim: probenecid, third line, is good to know. If they can't take either of those, it basically increases your uric acid urine production. ... But as you can imagine, you get high risk of getting kidney stones, so which is kind of a bummer.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: For confirmed CPPD, work up for hyperparathyroidism and hemochromatosis.
pearls.verbatim: If you diagnose this, so you get the arthrocentesis that comes back saying, you got CPPD. It'll be good to just check these things just to rule out that they don't have something, particularly parathyroidism, hyperparathyroidism, and hemochromatosis can cause it or increase your risk for it.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Gout

pearls.text: Syncope is defined as transient loss of consciousness due to global cerebral hypoperfusion, with loss of postural tone, brief duration (5-10 seconds), and spontaneous complete recovery.
pearls.verbatim: It's a transient loss of consciousness due to global cerebral hypoperfusion. That part is important too because that's what's actually going on. Right? You have that mentally to know, like, it's a lack of blood flow to the brain and what's causing that. That is the result of this. It's different than other that cause loss of consciousness. It does result in loss of postural tone, so when you're getting the history for that. And the other thing that's very key for syncope is that it's brief. We're talking five to ten seconds.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Vasovagal syncope is the most common cause of syncope.
pearls.verbatim: vasovagal is the the big... It is actually the most common cause.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Exertional syncope during exercise is a red flag for cardiac cause; syncope after exertion is more likely reflex or orthostatic.
pearls.verbatim: exertion may be important to distinguish. So post exertion, if they've already worked out, they're done, walking around, and then it's like, then they have a staining episode. That is different than during exertion.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Delayed orthostatic hypotension (occurring after 5 minutes or more) is more common in the elderly.
pearls.verbatim: most actually are delayed. And if you guys have time to curbside, that's a great one. There's a article that they posted on that. I went to that, and that's it. It's more common in the elderly.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Universal workup for syncope includes EKG and orthostatic vital signs; head imaging is reserved for patients with neurologic deficits or head trauma.
pearls.verbatim: EDG, that is one universal thing, and also could be. In fact, that's probably the only universal thing you're gonna order. ... Who gets head imaging? ... Neurologic deficits. ... head trauma, if they have a significant headache kind of is in there.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Echocardiogram is indicated only if EKG is abnormal or history suggests cardiac cause; not routinely for all syncope admissions.
pearls.verbatim: If they do have an abnormal EKG and they do have concern for cardiac caused by your history, and that's where I go into with the unexplained sleep with that. But if you... If you're doing your history and workup and there is no specific finding that's concerning for cardiac, echo much value.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: For vasovagal prodrome, teach patients hand grip, leg crossing, and abdominal tensing; acute water ingestion (one glass) can also raise blood pressure.
pearls.verbatim: they can do hand grip if they feel like coming on to anything that you're gonna reduce that blood flow going to the peripheries. Like, crossing tensing of the abdomen, you can teach those things. It's actually a really interesting study on acute water ingestion. So, like, if people are getting blood, they start to feel the symptoms. One glass of water, it can bump up the blood pressure.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Review medications that contribute to orthostatic hypotension: antihypertensives, diuretics, alpha/beta blockers, SSRIs, and antibiotics.
pearls.verbatim: Really look at your medications. You're gonna look through those. Antihypertensives, diuretics, alpha beta blockers, SSRI, and antibiotics. Those are the most common ones that can contribute to orthostatic hypotension.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Compression stockings for orthostatic hypotension must be thigh-high to be effective, but patients often dislike them.
pearls.verbatim: compression stockings, they have to be thigh high. Nobody's gonna wanna do that.
pearls.speaker: Tischler
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Tischler on Syncope

pearls.text: Weight cycling on GLP-1s leads to progressive loss of lean body mass because weight regained is predominantly fat, lowering metabolism and making future weight loss harder.
pearls.verbatim: when somebody loses weight, let's say they lose... Let's say they're 300. They lose a 100 pounds over, let's say, twelve months with medications and lifestyle, and they lose about 20% of their lean body mass, and the rest is predominantly fat tissue. Right? And then let's say life happens. They get off the medication for whatever reason. Stress comes on. They gain the weight back. Right? That weight we gain is predominantly all fat tissue.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: To optimize muscle protein synthesis, aim for 25-45 g of protein per meal; anything above 45 g is overkill, but at least 20 g per meal is a practical minimum for patients on GLP-1s who cannot tolerate larger volumes.
pearls.verbatim: I think between 25 to 45 is gonna be your... Yes? What are your thoughts on the protein shakes? Because they range from 13 grams to 45 grams.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Strength training is the most potent stimulus for muscle protein synthesis, but even with adequate protein intake, if calories are too low, it will not fully prevent lean body mass loss.
pearls.verbatim: if you're too low will not will not mitigate. You'll you'll still burn through that amino acid, then you'll still burn a lean body mass even despite you're too too low. Now it'll kinda help, but it's probably not gonna preserve all of it.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: When using starches, avoid pairing them with high fat to prevent conditioning toward overeating.
pearls.verbatim: if you're gonna use a starch, whether it's starchy vegetable, a grain of some sort, then we gotta make sure that we're not carrying a lot of fat with it because, again, that's that's gonna be that conditioning that we're setting in there.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: For very low-calorie diets (<1200 kcal/day), supplementation with third-party tested products (e.g., fish oil) may be needed to meet micronutrient needs.
pearls.verbatim: if you are doing a very low calorie diet, I would say below 1,200, you will not be able to properly hit your micronutrient adequacy doing that low.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Obese patients have altered brain structure and function in appetite-regulating regions, leading to constant hunger; GLP-1 medications can help restore regulation.
pearls.verbatim: these patients, their appetite, they're... They feel hungry all the time. Right? They're hungry. So that's why GLP one medication can be helpful for these patients because their body's not regulating their appetite very well.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: In a controlled metabolic study, participants on an ultra-processed diet consumed ~500 more calories per day compared to a minimally processed diet matched for macronutrients.
pearls.verbatim: the processed food, the ultra processed food diet, people tend to consume 504... 500 calories more per day compared to the unprocessed diet.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Soft-textured ultra-processed foods (e.g., chips) are eaten faster and in greater volume than harder, fibrous foods, increasing total calorie intake.
pearls.verbatim: minimally processed, healthier foods that were harder textured, solid protein foods, fiber foods, tend to eat less of that versus even ultrafast Even ultrafast foods, even if change the texture, you're gonna eat less than than semisolid foods, like potato chips and things eat pretty quickly.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Total sugar on a label includes both natural and added sugars; the 'added sugars' line tells you how much is added.
pearls.verbatim: the total sugar here is encompassing both the natural and the added. Right? And then right below that tells you exactly how much is being added.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.verbatim: But for only one ounce, you're looking at 15 grams of protein for only one ounce for about 60 calories.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: When adding unflavored protein powder to a low-protein food like tomato soup, make a slurry first with a small amount of liquid to ensure it mixes well without clumping.
pearls.verbatim: If you're having tomato soup that's not high in protein, you can mix an unflavored powder with that. I would recommend that you make a slurry before you add it to it so it can kind of mix as well with it.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Aim for at least 20 grams of protein per meal, ideally 25-30 grams, paired with high-fiber low-carb vegetables to enhance satiety.
pearls.verbatim: I recommend at least a minimum of 20. Try to get to 25 to 30 if you can. Pair that with some fiber, predominantly low carb vegetables.
pearls.speaker: Travis Eden
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Less than half the population performs aerobic exercise and less than a quarter performs anaerobic (strength) training; strength training is especially critical during weight loss to preserve muscle mass.
pearls.verbatim: I think I read an article. So it's just a generic article that was saying, like, less than half... Percent of the population actually performed aerobic, but less than a quarter of the population actually did anaerobic. So especially with people losing all this weight, strength training is also very important.

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.episode_title: Dr. Travis Eden on Nutrition and Lifestyle for Obesity Treatments

pearls.text: Family history cannot be left blank; at minimum put 'mom deceased at age 80, unknown cause' – but never use 'noncontributory' as it does not count.
pearls.verbatim: family history cannot just be blank, or it can't say. Right? Like, it has to say something. So maybe everybody doesn't have brothers and sisters, but everybody has parents. So at minimum, you could put, you know, mom deceased at age 80, unknown cause. Something like that.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.verbatim: If it's in that packet, it has to be entered into the EHR somewhere.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: The annual wellness visit is all-or-nothing billing: if you miss one required element, you cannot bill it.
pearls.verbatim: The thing with these is they are an all or nothing. If you miss one thing, we can't bill it.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: Advanced care planning (ACP) can be billed separately only if the teaching physician documents >15 minutes; adding modifier 33 waives patient cost-sharing.
pearls.verbatim: if the TP is spending at least sixteen minutes on advanced care planning and documenting it, if we add a modifier 33 to that, then there is no out of pocket expenses to the patient.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: When billing an E&M alongside a wellness visit, append modifier 25 to the E&M code; the Medicare code takes precedence.
pearls.verbatim: The Medicare code takes precedence, and the e and m becomes the 25 modifier.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: The National Compliance checklist provides a detailed breakdown of all required elements, including sexual history, nutrition, and physical activity.
pearls.verbatim: This very bottom resource here is a nice checklist that National Compliance has put together for us. So you can can see every single thing that's required.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: The after-visit summary (AVS) must be generated and given to the patient; it includes patient instructions and is required for billing.
pearls.verbatim: You have to generate an after visit summary or your MASJ.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: Chronic issues can be addressed during the same visit as the wellness visit, but patients should be informed they may be responsible for their deductible.
pearls.verbatim: If you see them today and you take care of their chronic issues and an annual wellness visit, they're gonna still be responsible for their deductible if they haven't met it.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: The patient self-assessment (first question of the 4Ms) is a required element for billing; it captures the patient's perception of their health.
pearls.verbatim: The piece of the 4Ms that we were always missing when people weren't putting the 4Ms in there is that patient self assessment. That's the first question on there. So if you have that, meaning what I need from a billing perspective.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: If a patient is on an opioid prescription, the medication section of the 4Ms should be filled out, including discussion of non-opioid treatment options.
pearls.verbatim: If they're on a opioid prescription, then I would suggest you fill out that medication section too.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: When uncertain about whether a code is time-based, consult a coder to avoid using an inappropriate code.
pearls.verbatim: There was one where I was using it, and it was actually a time based code. I had no idea. Until I mentioned it to a coder.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: Send a message to billing to request a change to your billing codes so you can learn from the correction and code effectively in the future.
pearls.verbatim: Send us a message or something to say, hey. Can you change this on your billing? Yeah. Just so that we know what we're doing, and we can do it effectively later on.
pearls.speaker: Warman
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Warman on Medicare Wellness Visits

pearls.text: In tPA candidates, blood pressure must be lowered below 185/110 before giving tPA and kept below 180/105 after administration.
pearls.verbatim: If they got tPA, you gotta get them down below one eighty five over one ten to even give it.
pearls.speaker: Whitaker
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Whitaker on CVA Management

pearls.text: Transplant patients should be seen by a dermatologist every six to twelve months due to high skin cancer risk.
pearls.verbatim: Transplant patients do need to be every six months to every twelve months by a dermatologist.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Squamous cell carcinoma risk is 65 times higher in transplant patients on immunosuppression.
pearls.verbatim: squamous cell goes up astronomically high, like sixty five time risk that they're gonna get one.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: When palpating an actinic keratosis, you should not feel a firm 'BB' underneath; if you do, it is likely a skin cancer requiring biopsy.
pearls.verbatim: If you kinda wanna feel around it, you're not gonna feel like there's a little, like, BB underneath it. If there is, that's usually when I'm biopsying one.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Basal cell carcinomas classically appear as pink, pearly papules with telangiectasias on sun-exposed areas.
pearls.verbatim: So they are classically, like, pink, pearly papules.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Squamous cell carcinomas are often painful and grow rapidly over weeks, distinguishing them from slower-growing lesions.
pearls.verbatim: These are the ones that typically will get people into the office because they often are painful. Like, these grow fast. They will be, like, weeks.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: The morbidity and mortality of squamous cell carcinoma is nearly as high as melanoma, so it must be taken seriously.
pearls.verbatim: But the morbidity and mortality of squamous cell carcinoma is almost that of melanoma.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: New facial droop on the same side as a prior squamous cell carcinoma on the ear may indicate metastatic disease and warrants MRI.
pearls.verbatim: I had a guy who had most done of a squam on his ear, and he came to me and told... His... He had, like, facial droop. And I was like, what's going on? He's like my... You know, his PCP thought he had, like, Ramsay Hunt syndrome or something. I was treating him with valacyclovir, but his facial droop didn't get better. And I was like, it was on the side of the squam that he had. So we did an MRI, and he had metastatic squam.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: A shave biopsy is adequate for most skin cancers and allows evaluation of the entire lesion; it is less cumbersome than suturing.
pearls.verbatim: So shave biopsy is kinda what it sounds like. You just numb it, and you are shaving kind of blush with the skin. Totally adequate. It's also less cumbersome than doing stitches and all of that. It also lets you evaluate the whole lesion.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: First-degree relatives of melanoma patients (siblings, children, parents) should be screened because they have higher risk than the general population.
pearls.verbatim: if you have a 50 year old lady who comes in had a melanoma diagnosed, like, we need to screen her siblings, her children, her parents because that first degree, like, branch has a higher risk than just your population level.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: The most important prognostic factor for melanoma is Breslow depth, which determines whether a patient needs simple excision versus sentinel lymph node biopsy and immunotherapy.
pearls.verbatim: if you see a path report of a melanoma, the biggest prognostic factor is the Breslow depth. So that is how far down in the skin it goes.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Change in a spot is the most important feature; if a patient says a spot has changed, biopsy it even if it looks normal.
pearls.verbatim: Change is the biggest thing. If someone's like, the spot has changed. It didn't used to look like that. Even if it looks totally normal, I take it off.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: For melanoma, the threshold for involving other specialties (surgical oncology, etc.) is T1b: 0.8 mm or greater with ulceration, or 1 mm in depth.
pearls.verbatim: the t one b, which is, like, 0.8 millimeters and greater with ulceration or one millimeter in-depth, That's when we start kinda circling the wagons with all the specialties.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Melanoma patients need skin checks every 3-6 months for 2-5 years after diagnosis, as they are not 'one and done' cases.
pearls.verbatim: they need skin checks every three to six months for two to five years.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Patients with a history of non-melanoma skin cancer should be seen at least once a year for skin checks.
pearls.verbatim: With the history of non melanoma skin cancer, we wanna see them at least once a year.
pearls.speaker: Williams
pearls.episode_title: Dr. Williams on Skin Cancer Basics 9/3/26

pearls.text: Melanoma can metastasize years after a clear margin excision, so have a low threshold to work up any new or unusual symptoms in patients with melanoma history.

pearls.verbatim: I'm able to spend time with my kids on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I don't have to be at the office. The patients can text me and email me
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: Distinguish DPC from concierge medicine: concierge charges $3,000–$5,000 per year on top of insurance, making it accessible only to wealthy patients.
pearls.verbatim: concierge is really kind of like a rich person's thing. You know? So it's like, hey. You have an insurance, and then you also pay, like, 3,000, $5,000 on top of that a year.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: Expect about one-third of DPC patients to be uninsured, one-third with traditional insurance, and one-third with health shares or high-deductible plans.
pearls.verbatim: in direct primary care, I'd say it's about a third uninsured. A third have traditional insurance, and then a third or so have, like, a health share or a high deductible health plan.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: Schedule new patients for 60 minutes and established patients for 30 minutes to allow thorough care and relationship building.
pearls.verbatim: I spend an hour with new patients. Mhmm. Thirty minutes with established patients.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: Offer an intensive weight loss program for an extra $25 per month, providing GLP-1 agonists like semaglutide, Ozempic, or tirzepatide.
pearls.verbatim: We do weight loss as a... As an aside. We charge $25 extra a month for, like, an intensive weight loss program. We give them, like, semaglutide, Ozempic, tirzepatide, those types of things.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: Keep overhead low by employing only one staff person who handles phones, rooms patients, and performs other tasks.
pearls.verbatim: We keep your overhead low. You have one staff person.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: If you opt out of Medicare, you can see Medicare patients and they pay you directly; you cannot bill Medicare.
pearls.verbatim: He can see Medicare patients because he's opted out of Medicare. He can't bill Medicare, and they can't bill bill Medicare. They can still pay the 80 of them.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: In DPC, after-hours calls are rare; Dr. White had none in 4 years.
pearls.verbatim: I've never had anybody contact me at the middle of the night. Four years.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: Don't start a DPC business if you don't want to run a business.
pearls.verbatim: don't start a business if you don't wanna run a business.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: DPC physicians recommend patients have some medical expense plan (e.g., health share or high-deductible insurance) even though the DPC practice does not bill insurance itself.
pearls.verbatim: When I talk with patients, you know, if they don't have insurance, you know, I do talk with them, like... And it's in my contract as well. Like, not insurance. We do recommend you have something in place for your medical expenses.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: The largest direct surgery center in the United States is in Oklahoma City, with prices lower than Blue Cross insurance.
pearls.verbatim: The largest direct surgery center in The United States is in Oklahoma City. And their prices are definitely lower than Blue Cross Card insurance.
pearls.speaker: s. Greuel and White
pearls.episode_title: Drs. Greuel and White on Business of Medicine

pearls.text: Screen all adults 18 and older for unhealthy drug use per USPSTF recommendation.
pearls.verbatim: USPSTF recommends screening everyone 18 or older for unhealthy drug use.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 1

pearls.text: Emphasize that identity is not the problem; in Celebrate Recovery, identity is in Christ, not the struggle.
pearls.verbatim: your identity is not your problem, what you're struggling with.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 1

pearls.text: At each Celebrate Recovery meeting, a chip ceremony marks milestones in recovery, allowing participants to publicly commit to step one.
pearls.verbatim: at each Celebrate Recovery meeting, there will be a chip ceremony
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 1

pearls.text: In Celebrate Recovery, a blue chip is used for the first step, whereas AA uses a white chip.
pearls.verbatim: Blue chips for the... Which is what I'm trying to pull apart right here. It's different from language in AA. You'll hear people talking about a white chip.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 1

pearls.text: The first step requires admitting powerlessness over a problem and that one's life has become unmanageable.
pearls.verbatim: We admitted that we were powerless over our problems and that our lives have become unmanageable.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 1

pearls.text: Naaman's story illustrates that healing requires following simple instructions with humility, not expecting a grand cure.
pearls.verbatim: he acknowledged his powerlessness, followed the instructions, and recovered completely.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 1

pearls.text: The only path to recovery is admitting powerlessness, humbling oneself, and submitting to the process.
pearls.verbatim: The only answer is to admit our powerlessness, humble ourselves, and submit to the process that will eventually bring recovery.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 1

pearls.text: When treating AUD, address underlying comorbidities like depression, as alcohol may be masking an emotional issue; otherwise, patients may substitute another substance.
pearls.verbatim: Also figuring out why are you drinking so much and then treating the underlying emotional cause. Ah. Otherwise, we'll just fill it with something else. The depression.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 2

pearls.text: Baclofen can be an option for AUD in patients with severe liver or renal disease, as it increases abstinent days without reducing cravings.
pearls.verbatim: So baclofen, it helps reduce the risk of returning, I think, meant to say drinking here. It increases abstinent days. Doesn't reduce cravings necessarily like some other drugs, but it can it can be an option for those with severe liver or renal disease.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 2

pearls.text: Sublocade is a depot injection that leaves a knot and may require surgical removal if a reaction occurs; Brixadi is a newer IM injection that does not require refrigeration and is less painful.
pearls.verbatim: Problem with Sublocade, if someone has a reaction to it, you actually have to surgically remove the to resolve that reaction, whether it's allergic anaphylaxis. So that's more concerning. And doesn't require refrigeration.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 2

pearls.text: Methadone for OUD can only be prescribed from a federally certified opioid treatment program; it cannot be prescribed from a general clinic for addiction.
pearls.verbatim: methadone can only be prescribed for opioid use disorder in the outpatient setting from a federally certified opioid treatment program.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 2

pearls.text: For cannabis cravings, gabapentin may help adults and N-acetylcysteine may help adolescents.
pearls.verbatim: Some have said gabapentin can reduce cravings in adults and acetylcysteine actually in adolescents.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 2

pearls.text: Prefer buprenorphine in your clinic so you can maintain the therapeutic relationship.
pearls.verbatim: I would rather have them on buprenorphine, some type of product where we can work on that together.
pearls.speaker: s Jones & Shannon
pearls.episode_title: Drs Jones & Shannon on Addiction Med Part 2

pearls.text: Placebo effects for female sexual dysfunction drugs are strong, exceeding 40%. This must be considered when evaluating treatment efficacy.
pearls.verbatim: More than 40%. Pretty strong placebo effects
pearls.speaker: Unknown
