pearls.text: Human beings do not consistently recognize what turns them on sexually. This is a common misconception.
pearls.verbatim: Human beings consistently recognize what turns them on sexually. False
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: The inability to accurately detect sexual arousal is called non-concordance. This is a key concept to understand when assessing sexual response.
pearls.verbatim: The inability of humans to accurately and consistently detect sexual arousal is non-concordance, not the description here
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Non-concordance refers to the mismatch between subjective and genital arousal within an individual, not between partners. It occurs within the individual.
pearls.verbatim: Nonconcordance occurs in... Within the individual and not between partners
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Genital response is not a good indicator of sexual arousal. Arousal is primarily a cerebral experience.
pearls.verbatim: Genital response is a good indicator of sexual arousal. False
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Arousal is a cerebral phenomenon, not solely a genital response. Remember that arousal occurs between your ears, not your legs.
pearls.verbatim: arousal occurs between your ears, not your legs
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Men recognize sexual concordance more consistently than women, but only 50% of the time. So no one is very good at it.
pearls.verbatim: Men recognize sexual concordance more consistently than women? It's actually true, but only 50% of the time
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Women do not respond less often to sexually relevant stimuli compared to men. This is a myth.
pearls.verbatim: In comparison with men, women respond less often to sexually relevant stimuli. False
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: The idea that the distance between arousal and desire is significantly different in women compared to men is a myth. There is more variation within groups.
pearls.verbatim: The idea that is significantly different is a bit of, like, a myth
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Practice asking sexual history questions with friends outside of clinical settings to build fluency and reduce awkwardness.
pearls.verbatim: One thing you might do this Friday night is gather a group of your friends and practice ask... Asking sexual questions
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Practice using explicit anatomical language regularly to become comfortable; have your partner repeat terms back to normalize them.
pearls.verbatim: you say repeatedly, penis, penis, penis, and she has to repeat it back. Vagina, vagina, vagina. Because she needs to be comfortable with language and anatomy
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Beta blockers should be avoided as first-line antihypertensive in women due to their negative impact on sexual function, especially orgasm.
pearls.verbatim: Beta blockers are the worst. Just never make them your first line drug.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: A DSM-5 diagnosis of a sexual disorder requires symptoms for a specific duration (at least 6 months) and associated distress.
pearls.verbatim: a DSM five diagnosis requires symptoms for specific duration and distress
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Counsel patients that simultaneous orgasm with a partner is not necessary for a healthy sexual relationship.
pearls.verbatim: it is important, though, to bust the myth that everything should be synchronous, that they should have an orgasm at the same time as their partners
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: There is no universal physiological measure of a female orgasm; diagnosis relies on patient self-report.
pearls.verbatim: there is no absolutely universal way to measure physiologically whether a woman has had an orgasm
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: When a patient reports pain with sex, ask specifically where in the act the pain occurs to differentiate the differential diagnosis.
pearls.verbatim: You have to, like, get specific with him. Where in the act is the pain? Because that's gonna differentiate your your differential.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Low sexual desire that is not distressing or is context-dependent (e.g., responsive to partner initiation) is not a dysfunction.
pearls.verbatim: I don't have, like, a lot of interest in sex, but when my husband shows interest or when the act starts or foreplay starts, I'm okay. So that would not necessarily be a function.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: For SSRI-induced low desire, options include adding high-dose bupropion or sildenafil, but cognitive behavioral therapy and mindfulness are first-line.
pearls.verbatim: There is not out there that you could add sildenafil to to try to help. You could also do a high dose of bupropion along with the SSRI. Of course, it's not the SSRI. That could be that too. Cognitive behavioral therapy is always the right answer on the test. Always the right answer. Mindfulness training.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Pelvic floor physical therapy is a high-yield, patient-satisfying intervention for many women with genitopelvic complaints.
pearls.verbatim: Every woman who has had a baby and or... I should say every woman. Everyone needs pelvic floor PT. Like, it's a slam dunk. It's a big patient satisfier.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: For orgasmic disorder, the most effective intervention is education about the woman's body and how it responds to stimulation.
pearls.verbatim: Orgasmic disorder, what helps the most is education. Education of the woman, of her body, how it's supposed to respond, what kind of touch or or stimulation it will respond to, and and just working through that.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Concordance between genital response and subjective arousal is only 10-25% in women, so genital response is not a reliable indicator of arousal.
pearls.verbatim: Only 50% overlap consistently for men, maximum, and it's much less for women. Perhaps, like, 10 to 25.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Genital response does not equal sexual arousal; it is a common misconception to equate lubrication with arousal.
pearls.verbatim: genital response is pretty good indication does not equal sexual arousal.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Desire can be thought of as arousal in context, shifting the focus from low libido to contextual factors.
pearls.verbatim: Desire then, we can think about as arousal in context.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: In behavioral medicine, the primary focus for women with low desire is brake relief (stress, low affection, non-erotic context) rather than low libido, unless physiological.
pearls.verbatim: break relief is actually the number one thing that we tend to work with women on in terms of behavioral med. It's very seldom actually low libido unless it's physiologically related to, like, an illness or to a medication. It's more about, can we help them get the brakes off?
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: A partner approaching during a non-erotic activity like doing dishes creates a mixed signal system because the context is not low-stress or erotic.
pearls.verbatim: If they're standing doing dishes and their partner comes up behind them and does something to them, touches them in some way, they have a very mixed signal system at that point. Right? Because strangely enough, DISH is not exclusively erotic and not associated with the low stress environment.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Ask patients to make a timeline of their sexual history and list of when sex worked well to identify contextual patterns.
pearls.verbatim: I would say to them, why don't you start making a list? Why don't you make a a timeline of your sexual history and sexual experiences as you remember them? And why don't you start making a list of things when it has worked really well and what was happening? Just a few descriptors.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: It is important not to impose your own understanding of sex onto patients; explore their cultural and ritual context.
pearls.verbatim: Important not to, like, impose our understanding onto our patient. And so really trying to understand where we're coming from and taking Ah. Ritual context.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Female Sexual (Dys)function

pearls.text: Volume overload is the number one cause of poor outcomes in patients with cardiac and ESRD diagnoses; main treatment is to dialyze them.
pearls.verbatim: Volume overload is also the number one cause of which can be an independent cause for poor outcomes with our patients with cardiac as well as ESRD diagnoses. So main treatment for volume overload in ESRD is to dialyze them.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Document all treatments, especially IVF, in the H&P and progress notes under the specific problem being treated or in an FEN section.
pearls.verbatim: Documenting all treatments, especially IVF, a drug that's being added to the patient in our HNPs and in our progress notes under either the specific problem that it's treating or in an FEN section.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: When assuming care of a patient, always check the MAR to see if any IV fluids are running, as they may not be documented in the H&P or progress notes.
pearls.verbatim: Whenever I take four patients to the hospital that first day, like, one of one of the things I look through is the MAR to see what meds they're on, and you will be shocked. It's not documented, but it's running.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Check all lines and their rates when seeing a patient in the morning, as fluids may be running at a rate not ordered.
pearls.verbatim: When we check our patients in the morning, we should always check all the lines that are... To see, like, where... What's running and, like, what rate is it running? Because half the time, it's running at a rate that we didn't even order.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: One-third of patients with confirmed MI have no chest pain; dyspnea alone can be an anginal equivalent.
pearls.verbatim: Of the one third of patients with confirmed MI had no chest pain. So really You know, dyspnea on exertion is kinda androgenic. Dyspnea alone can be simply a cause.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Severe neutropenia is defined as an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) less than 500 cells/μL.
pearls.verbatim: ANC was point two, so that's 200, and severe neutropenia is anything that's less than 500.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: File a variance for direct admission delays to drive systemic change; it is the mechanism for quality improvement.
pearls.verbatim: we got to file a variance to make any type of systemic change.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: FMIS August MM

pearls.text: Healthy Start enrollment is not income-based and accepts all pregnant women in eligible ZIP codes, including teens and older moms.
pearls.verbatim: It's not income based, and I really see everybody. I see teenage moms, and I see a 42, 43 year old that's sixth, seventh, eighth baby, and they're still learning things.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Lactation referrals to St. John's Breastfeeding Resource Center are available via phone, not formal referral.
pearls.verbatim: There is a phone number that you guys have that you guys can call, and they... You can give it to your patients. Her name is Suzanne Reeder, and she is with St. John's Breastfeeding Resource Center. So that's information that you guys can give them since referrals are not an option anymore.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Patients may hide food insecurity from doctors; home visits can uncover needs like lack of adequate food.
pearls.verbatim: I have one mom who did not want to tell the doctor that she had ice cream, she... A block of cheese, and a frozen thing of orange juice for her and her almost two year old daughter.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Milk typically comes in 3-4 days after delivery; colostrum is sufficient for the newborn's cherry-pit-sized stomach.
pearls.verbatim: their milk's not gonna come in for about three or four days. They think once they deliver, that milk's gonna come in, and they're just gonna be producing all of this milk, and that is not the case.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Hospital-provided formula (e.g., Similac) is chosen by lowest bid, not medical necessity; switching brands is safe.
pearls.verbatim: the hospital puts in a bid, and it's the cheapest bid from the hospital. Basically, it's like Similac's giving the hospital room to give out their formula is basically how it goes.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Similac commonly causes constipation in breastfed infants who supplement; Enfamil is often better tolerated.
pearls.verbatim: My number one complaint with Similac, if they're gonna have Similac or any formula and breastfeed, it constipates the babies.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Wet diaper count is the primary gauge of adequate intake; 6 wet diapers per day indicates sufficient feeding.
pearls.verbatim: how many diapers did you have? Six. Great. Now you're you know you're eating enough.
pearls.speaker: Gina Blevins
pearls.episode_title: Gina Blevins on Healthy Start

pearls.text: Perimenopause onset is defined by irregular periods (interval, flow, or duration), not by hot flashes or night sweats.
pearls.verbatim: the onset perimenopause is defined by the onset of irregular periods. It's not by hot flashes or night sweats. It's irregular periods.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: Menopause is diagnosed after 12 months without a menstrual period; if a woman has gone 11 months and then has a period, she is not yet menopausal.
pearls.verbatim: What do you have to do to become menopausal? Have to not have a menstrual period for how long? One year.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: Progesterone-only pills help menorrhagia by thinning the endometrium, which also reduces prostaglandin production and thus dysmenorrhea.
pearls.verbatim: It pins the lining of the endometrium. Okay. So it helps the menorrhagia because progesterone does what the endometrium... Stops it from dividing.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: PCOS diagnosis requires two of three criteria: irregular menstrual periods, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, and elevated testosterone (or clinical hirsutism).
pearls.verbatim: Three things that you look at currently for polycystic ovary syndrome, irregular menstrual periods, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, elevated pretestosterone. Those are the three things. You have to have two of the three to make the diagnosis.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Gyn with Dr. Calvert

pearls.text: Insurance companies like UnitedHealthcare preemptively deny about 70% of cases, but 92% of peer-to-peer reviews overturn those denials.
pearls.verbatim: UnitedHealthcare, in particular, is notorious for denying about seventy percent of cases just across the board... I would say ninety two percent of the time, we get those overturned.
pearls.speaker: Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: The clock for inpatient restarts when you change a patient from observation to inpatient — even if they have already been in obs for 36 hours.
pearls.verbatim: when we admit them, the clock restarts for inpatient.
pearls.speaker: Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: When an insurance bundling rule applies (e.g., readmission for a post-op complication within 30 days), the hospital gets a single bundled payment for the entire episode.
pearls.verbatim: If it is a post op complication, they will bundle that with the operation. So it's it's bundled. That stay, we're not getting paid for because it's part of what happened before.
pearls.speaker: Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: If you admit as inpatient but the patient meets criteria only for observation, you can change the order to observation using a Moon letter/Code 44 — it's easier to step down than to upgrade.
pearls.verbatim: If we admit... and then change their status to something lower
pearls.speaker: Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: If a patient needs SNF placement, admit them as inpatient and document why; if they are sick enough for SNF, they should qualify for inpatient with proper documentation.
pearls.verbatim: if you know that your patient is gonna need placement, give them an inpatient, but document why. If they need sniff, they're sick, and they should qualify for inpatient with the proper documentation.
pearls.speaker: Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: For trauma patients, once the surgical phase is complete (typically around 6 days), the surgeons sign off and transfer to medicine because medical complications allow continued length of stay extensions.
pearls.verbatim: once the surgical part of it is completed, say, you know, six days, and now it's the post op stuff, it's the medical things, it's the, you know, chronic respiratory failure. We can't get them off the vent, those kind of things. That initial stay when the surgeons sign off and flip it over to medicine is because they're not meeting the length of stay requirements from a surgical standpoint. But from a medical standpoint with medical attendings, those kind of complications get us a continued length of stay extension.
pearls.speaker: Heather Bell
pearls.episode_title: Heather Bell, DO on the Role of Physician Advisor

pearls.text: UnitedHealthcare gives only 3 days to set up a peer-to-peer review after a denial letter is issued; other insurers allow 2-4 weeks.
pearls.verbatim: UnitedHealthcare gives us three days to set up a peer to peer once they issue the denial letter. A lot of the other insurance companies, it's two to four weeks.
pearls.speaker: Heather Bell

pearls.text: Address underlying causes such as depression and pain when patients request assisted suicide.

pearls.text: When interpreting POCUS, systematically identify the view, three pieces of anatomy, and whether the findings are normal or abnormal.
pearls.verbatim: I want you to tell me what view it is. I want you to tell me three pieces of anatomy in that view, and I want you to tell me what what you see. Like, is it normal or is it abnormal?

pearls.text: In the FAST exam, finding free fluid in the abdomen after trauma plus a bladder with heterogeneous material suggests bladder rupture.
pearls.verbatim: So his his bladder rupture. So this is a example of how you could use the past exam.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: A D-sign on parasternal short-axis view (left ventricle appearing D-shaped instead of circular) indicates acute right ventricular pressure overload, classically from pulmonary embolism.
pearls.verbatim: When the right side pressure increases enough to overpower the left side, starts pushing against ventricle creating what looks like a... And that's evidence of increased right sided pressure. This... I think this is only an acute sign.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: Recording POCUS clips and comparing them with confirmatory imaging (e.g., CT) reinforces learning and builds diagnostic confidence.
pearls.verbatim: if you do try and you do see something and then it is confirmed on CT PE protocol, and then you go back and looked at it, and if you save your clips or your images, that's gonna reinforce, oh, I I did that.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: In the parasternal long-axis view, if the mitral valve leaflet separation from the septum is greater than 1 cm, it suggests reduced left ventricular ejection fraction.
pearls.verbatim: Mitral valve is very far from the So distance are you looking for? Centimeter. You're doing the eyeball test. It's a one centimeter.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: A left atrium three to four times the size of the aorta is abnormal and suggests chronic diastolic dysfunction or volume overload.
pearls.verbatim: Eyelination of this ventricle is pretty remarkable as is the size of the left atrium. Right? So it's three or four times the size of the aorta and break down to the size of the aorta throughout the contraction.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: If you have three B-lines in two different lung zones on both sides, that's pretty high sensitivity and specificity for pulmonary edema usually from decompensated heart failure.
pearls.verbatim: If you have three v lines in two different lung zones on both sides, that's pretty high sensitivity and specificity for pulmonary edema usually from decompensated heart.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: A normal left ventricle in short axis appears circular and contracts concentrically; you can eyeball it and say 'that's normal' if it collapses at least 50%.
pearls.verbatim: It's a circle, and it's closing concentrically. You can learn to eyeball this and say, oh, that's normal.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: Right ventricular strain is suggested by a right ventricle that looks smaller than the left (less than two-thirds the size) and contracts poorly from apex to base.
pearls.verbatim: it looks smaller than the left side. Don't know if I could give as specific as two thirds, but it looks smaller. And then it's contracting from from apex to thigh.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: In left ventricular systolic dysfunction, the mitral valve barely moves and does not get within 1 cm of the septum (EPSS >1 cm).

pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: A hyperdynamic left ventricle that completely collapses on itself is actually normal, not abnormal.
pearls.verbatim: this left side is hyperdynamic. It's, like, completely collapsing on itself. Normal or abnormal? Normal.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: POCUS with Dr. Ledbetter

pearls.text: Epinephrine code dose is 1 mg IV push; a 1 mg ampule (1:1000) and a 1 mg pre-filled syringe (1:10,000) contain the same amount of epinephrine, just different concentrations.
pearls.verbatim: When someone says an amp of epinephrine, what they're literally talking about is just the glass container it's in, and an amp of epinephrine contains one milligram of epinephrine.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: To dilute code-cart epinephrine, draw the 1 mg/10 mL epi into 9 mL of saline to get 50 mcg per 0.5 mL.
pearls.verbatim: You would draw this into nine mils of saline, and then you have that.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Dopamine is a prodrug that requires functional adrenal glands to convert to norepinephrine/epinephrine; prefer direct beta agonists like epinephrine.
pearls.verbatim: It's a prodrug that counts on having working adrenal glands to convert it into norepinephrine and epinephrine.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Renally dosed dopamine (low-dose for renal vasodilation) is outdated and ineffective.
pearls.verbatim: We know that that's not a thing. It doesn't really work, but that was the thinking.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: The MAP goal of 65 can be lowered in chronic ICU patients if there is no end-organ dysfunction (e.g., no AKI, normal troponin, fully cognitive).
pearls.verbatim: you may find that you've had someone on vasopressors for a certain number of days, and their MAP keeps going low, but they're not developing an AKI. Their trope is staying normal. They're fully cognitive. They don't need that MAP of 68. They can have the MAP of 58.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Choose the starting dose of Levophed based on how many points of MAP you need to make up to reach 65.
pearls.verbatim: I literally choose my dose of levophen based on how many points on their MAP I have to make up to get to 65.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: It is better to overshoot MAP initially to perfuse organs than to slowly titrate up while organs are ischemic.
pearls.verbatim: I would so much rather that person accidentally shoot a little bit hypertensive when we're actually perfusing their organs than slowly titrate up over an hour and a half with the organs not being perfused.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Peripheral IV lines can run any vasopressor for at least 12 hours without needing a central line.
pearls.verbatim: You have twelve hours of of any pressor running through peripheral lines.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: To improve ultrasound IV success, place a second tourniquet above a distal IV and flush 30 cc of saline to distend proximal veins.
pearls.verbatim: You can you can put on tourniquet, a second tourniquet, a third tourniquet. If they have a a distal line in the hand and you just need something better, why don't you shoot thirty ccs of saline in it to pump them up more and so you can get that thing?
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Calcium boluses can be given to children on vasopressors to provide additional inotropic support.
pearls.verbatim: Kids who are on vasopressors, is not at all uncommon to give them a bolus of of calcium.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: For pressor extravasation (e.g., phenylephrine or levophed), inject phentolamine locally into the vasoconstricted tissue.
pearls.verbatim: just locally injecting phentolamine.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Use the PediStat app or Braslow tape for pediatric code doses; it costs $4 and provides all drug doses and tube sizes.
pearls.verbatim: I use an app on my phone called PediStat. It costs me $4. 4 of your thousand CME dollars. You have PD stat for a lifetime. It's not a subscription, and it has every tube size, dose, drug.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: In ESRD patients with refractory bradycardia, suspect hyperkalemia.
pearls.verbatim: What is this patient who has ESRD and refractory bradycardia probably have? Hyperkalemia.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Pressors - Engstrom

pearls.text: Immobilization of the head, neck, and shoulders using a custom mask ensures the patient does not move more than 2–3 millimeters during treatment.
pearls.verbatim: We're able to immobilize the head along with the neck and then the shoulders, ensuring that the patients are not moving while on the treatment table.
pearls.speaker: Unknown

pearls.text: The Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score (SINS) uses six questions to determine if a spinal lesion is mechanically stable; a score of 4 indicates stability.
pearls.verbatim: So for his T spine lesion, he gets a point. Asual nonmechanical pain, he gets a point. Elastic, he gets no points. His alignment's normal. He has no collapse, but he has more than 50% involved. We don't see an axial, but you'll have to trust me on that. So he gets a point. And posterolateral involvement, he has unilateral. So he gets a point. So he's a four on this spinal instability score, so he's technically stable.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For radiation dermatitis, advise patients to wash the area daily with mild soap and lukewarm water; patients who washed had less itching and earlier healing times.
pearls.verbatim: patients who washed and kept the area clean obviously did better. Less itching, earlier healing times. And so it's important to encourage good skin hygiene.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: For grade 1-2 radiation dermatitis, apply Aquaphor or similar moisturizer when you get up, when you go to bed, and at least one other time in between.
pearls.verbatim: Aquaphor, that's basically what that means. Anything like Aquaphor, I don't get paid by them, but it's great. You put a layer. I always say, when you get up, when you go to bed, and at least one other time in between, it just puts a good a good layer on there.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Cellulitis from radiation dermatitis is treated like normal cellulitis with standard empiric coverage; no special antibiotics are needed.
pearls.verbatim: You treat it just like you would a a normal cellulitis. So so same coverage you would normally do. There's not any specific thing you need to take into account per se when you're empirically covering them.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: Counsel patients with published percentage estimates of success based on clinical trials to set realistic expectations.
pearls.verbatim: We base all of our treatments on studies. So I can say with the percentage, you know, we're gonna get this.
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Radiation Oncology Primer for Primary Care - Gabriel S. Vidal, MD, FACP

pearls.text: If you suspect self-harm, open the topic and ask questions directly; do not wait for the patient to bring it up.
pearls.verbatim: If you ever get the sense that maybe somebody is in danger of self harm, you addressing... You opening up the topic, you asking the questions is probably a really positive thing to do. Don't wait for them to bring it up.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Do not ask a suicidal person what they want to do; they wouldn't be in that situation if they could solve the problem positively themselves.
pearls.verbatim: Don't ask them what you wanna do. They wouldn't be in this situation if they could solve the problem in a positive way themselves.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Kindly and compassionately tell the patient what they must do; take charge of the situation because they are looking for direction.
pearls.verbatim: Kindly and compassionately tell them what they must do. This sounds a little bit bossy, but that's exactly what the goal is. Take charge of the situation.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Most suicidal people experience a suicidal episode only once; if you stop them during the initial episode, odds are they won't try again later.
pearls.verbatim: Most suicidal people experience a suicidal episode only once in their lives. That's a real plus. If you can stop them from killing themselves during the initial epis... Episode, the odds are in your favor that they won't try again later.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Acute suicidal danger is usually extremely brief—only seconds or minutes—and suicidal feelings come and go in waves like depression.
pearls.verbatim: Most suicidal people are acutely suicidal, imminent danger for an extremely brief period of time. Usually, only seconds or minutes.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: A high ACE score increases the likelihood of suicidal thinking; use the ACE test to assess cumulative family and childhood adversity.
pearls.verbatim: If you get a... The higher the score, the higher likelihood is that they would be susceptible to suicidal thinking because they've probably been fighting for their... On their life.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Only about 5% of the suicidal population are truly determined to die; the rest are ambivalent and can be redirected.
pearls.verbatim: Hardcore suicidal, only about five percent of the suicidal population are really determined to die.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Placing a truly determined-to-die patient in an institutional setting may worsen the situation because it feeds a sense of being trapped.
pearls.verbatim: Placing them in an institutional setting will not stop them and maybe even make it worse because it feeds that now I'm trapped here.
pearls.speaker: Rev Joel S. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev Joel S. Leitch on Suicide Prevention 5/14/26

pearls.text: Feeling trapped by the need to respond until you resent or hate doing the right thing is a sign of burnout.
pearls.verbatim: We can feel trapped by our need to respond to a situation until we actually resent or even hate doing the right thing.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Empathy can become overtaxed and exhausted even when you are diligently maintaining self-care skills.
pearls.verbatim: this empathy can become overtaxed and exhausted even when the caregiver is diligently maintaining self care skills
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Fear of exposing oneself, illusions of omnipotence, and difficulty trusting other professionals contribute to the silencing response that prevents reaching out for help.
pearls.verbatim: Fear of exposing oneself, illusions of omnipotence, and difficulty trusting other professionals seems to contribute to the silencing response and often presents us from reaching out for the help we need.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: When countertransference arises, intentionally purpose to not let it be about you.
pearls.verbatim: I had to really purpose, intentionally purpose to not let this be about me.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Compassion fatigue can result in diminished capacity to function at work, home, and within personal relationships.
pearls.verbatim: Compassion fatigue is a very real concern and one that might result in diminished capacity to function at work, home, and within personal relationships.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Anger is a control measure used to feel in control when feeling helpless or overwhelmed.
pearls.verbatim: Anger is a control measure
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Dread working with certain patients is a normal symptom of compassion fatigue that should be recognized.
pearls.verbatim: Dread working with certain people and clients.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Decreased feelings of work competence, especially in interns, is a common symptom of compassion fatigue and usually resolves with time.
pearls.verbatim: Decreased feelings of work competence.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Silencing response assumptions like 'talking about it won't help' prevent you from seeking needed support.
pearls.verbatim: Silencing response assumptions: I can't do anything about it. Talking about it won't help.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Practice good sleep hygiene, exercise, and take time out to enjoy things as much as your schedule allows.
pearls.verbatim: Practice good sleep hygiene as much as you're able with your schedules and getting some exercise and having some time out so you can just enjoy things a little bit.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Identify automatic negative thoughts (ANTS) and develop a plan to counter them, as they are often counterproductive.
pearls.verbatim: identifying those kind of thoughts and behaviors that are in our life that are counterproductive and developing a plan.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Understand that developing a nonanxious presence takes practice; it does not change instantly but is cultivated over time through self-discovery and intentional effort.
pearls.verbatim: This doesn't tend to change, like, over the... You know, in in just a minute. This is something that we work on. We discover ourselves. We discover more about ourselves, and we discover more about our automatic negative thoughts or automatic negative behaviors, and we begin a process of doing a Bible study or devotional based on how God would say he wants to help us with those things, and we grow.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Leverage the principle of isomorphism: making a positive change in one area of life will generate improvements across other areas.
pearls.verbatim: This is known as the principle of isomorphism when you affect change in one area of your life, and it has a generative effect across the board to other areas.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on How Continue to Burn Without Getting Burnt Out 1/8/26

pearls.text: Always ask every patient in an initial interview about any history of suicidal thinking or acting out.
pearls.verbatim: I always ask them if there's any history at all of any suicidal thinking, of any acting out
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Patients rarely say directly that they are planning suicide; listen for indirect clues in what they say.
pearls.verbatim: They may not say, well, I came to see you today because I'm planning on killing myself. They're not likely to do that, but they may say some things to kinda give you some clues
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Be aware that some actively suicidal patients may not want to be rescued—do not assume they are ready to accept help.
pearls.verbatim: If they're hardcore or suicidal at the time, they may not wanna be rescued.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Immediately assure the suicidal person that you will definitely get them the help they need, even if you are unsure of the specifics.
pearls.verbatim: It's imperative to quickly assure the suicidal person that you are definitely going to get him the help he needs
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: You must become the problem solver for the patient; kindly and compassionately tell them what they must do.
pearls.verbatim: You become the problem solver for it. Kindly and compassionately tell them what they must do.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Instead of asking, kindly and compassionately tell the patient what they must do—this removes their burden of decision-making.
pearls.verbatim: Kindly and compassionately tell them what they must do.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: If you can stop the patient from killing themselves during the first suicidal episode, they are unlikely to attempt again.
pearls.verbatim: If you can stop them from killing themselves during the initial episode, the odds are in your favor that they will not try again.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: The three H's—helplessness, hopelessness, and haplessness—are the key words that signal the need to assess for suicide risk.
pearls.verbatim: Helplessness, hopelessness, and haplessness.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: If a patient expresses hopelessness, it is a strong red flag for suicide risk—more predictive than depression alone.
pearls.verbatim: If somebody is speaking hopelessness, something you really need to be careful with, really need to attend to.
pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Actively work to build hope and reorient the patient toward the future to counteract hopelessness.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Never be afraid to ask patients directly if they have thoughts of hurting themselves or killing themselves.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Ask yourself how you can regenerate hope until the patient's life situation improves; hopelessness is a core driver of suicide.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Ambivalence means a suicidal person may harm themselves while simultaneously pleading for help; recognize this as a sign of ambivalence, not manipulation.

pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch

pearls.text: Any small positive action or word can tip the balance away from suicide during the ambivalent period.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: To identify the significant other, ask the patient: 'If you were going to write a suicide note, who would you write it to?' because suicide notes are usually written to the person the suicidal person wants to impact most.

pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: The dyadic nature of suicide means the suicidal person has invested all hope in the significant other; when that person is not available, the suicidal person feels totally alone.

pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: When a patient says 'you're the only person who understands me,' it is a confession of poor interpersonal and communication skills, and often leads to arguments and breakdown of communication.

pearls.speaker: Rev. Leitch
pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: The significant other may be hostile or unwilling to cooperate, but can still provide clues about what was happening; even if they won't talk to the suicidal person, they can help you understand the situation.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Motivations for suicidal behavior include wanting to escape an intolerable situation, join a deceased loved one, gain attention, manipulate others, avoid punishment, punish survivors, get revenge, or avoid becoming a burden.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: About 75% of suicidal individuals give notice of their intentions through early warning signals; some purposely present signals, others do so inadvertently, hoping someone will pick up their trail.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: Look for a cluster of warning signals piling up together, especially in the context of a dramatic life event such as loss, grief, depression, or physical pain.

pearls.episode_title: Rev. Leitch on Suicide Intervention

pearls.text: The greatest suicide risk is during the first 90 days after depression begins to lift.

pearls.episode_title: Thyroid Disorders - Dr. Amanda Lucashu, DO

pearls.text: For subclinical hypothyroidism, most patients need only observation ('prayer and a pat on the back'); treatment exceptions include symptoms, TSH >10, family history, pregnancy plans, or positive antibodies.

And so if the patient is symptomatic, you know, we just talked about what the symptoms are with the review of systems and things, then you might consider starting a low dose of levothyroxine. The other thing is if they have a high risk for overt hypothyroidism. So some of those risks are if the TSH is above 10, if they have a family history of hypothyroidism, goiter, pregnancy, or plans to become pregnant because of the risk of congenital hypothyroidism. Or if for whatever reason, this is not an indication to check for antibodies, but if you, for whatever reason, have antibodies in the chart, you can't ignore them, and that would be a time to treat as well.

pearls.text: Any commercial sexual exploitation of a minor is automatically human trafficking, regardless of coercion.

pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Look for delay in seeking medical care; traffickers avoid losing money by delaying care until absolutely necessary.
pearls.verbatim: delay in seeking medical care is really important because they don't want them to lose the money
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Be suspicious of tattoos, especially if the same tattoo appears on multiple people; victims often avoid discussing them.
pearls.verbatim: if I see tattoos or if I start seeing the same tattoo over and over on people, I get suspicious
pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Look for a second cell phone that is always connected to someone; it may indicate the trafficker is listening.

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.speaker: Unknown
pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.text: Ask yourself whether the patient knows there are alternatives and resources available; often they do not.

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care

pearls.episode_title: Trauma Informed Care
